added.subject: [BugFix][KV Pool] Bound PP/MTP GVA allocations by physical copy extent (#19877)
added.body: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Follow-up to #19422 and #19421. Keep the physical KV-layer synchronization and make the GVA object large enough for every physical layer, including MTP at the last PP stage. For a GLM configuration with 78 target layers, PP partition `42,36`, and one MTP cache layer, PP1 has 37 physical KV layers. The existing global-layer estimate allocates 7,002,294 bytes, but the unchanged PP byte origin plus the actual packed payload requires 7,092,024 bytes. The SDK rejects the final layer's copy with `BatchCopyWritePath -3102`. Compute the PP byte origin once and share it between allocation and `LayerBatchBuilder`. For metadata-complete GVA groups, allocate `max(existing_shard_size, pp_byte_offset + sum(group_block_len))`. Align the resulting shared DCP shard to the existing 2 MiB boundary before computing the full allocation and shard origins. Preserve the block-key path, metadata fallback, keys, and existing byte layout. No MTP, layerwise, or SSD feature is disabled. Actual failing range, reproduced twice with the fix absent: ```text object base = 72057626250182656 allocated bytes = 7002294 physical layer = 36 (zero based) copy GVA = 72057626257157944 copy offset = 6975288 copy bytes = 83968 copy end offset = 7059256 > 7002294 SDK result = -3102 last entry end = 7092024 (another 32768-byte entry follows) ``` The SDK-reported address exactly matches the observed out-of-range copy. The SDK rejects the operation before copying; this does not establish that an out-of-bounds write actually occurred. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Fixes pooled KV save failures for PP stages whose physical KV payload extends beyond the target-model layer estimate. All readers/writers sharing an affected key must use the same layout. Rebuild the affected cache during upgrade: an existing undersized object cannot be made safe by changing the requesting allocation size alone. Validation used isolated task-owned pools; existing public SSD storage was not initialized or cleared. ### How was this patch tested? **Target-branch CPU regression:** ```bash python3 -m pytest -q \ tests/ut/kv_offload/test_pool_worker_pp_layer_count.py \ tests/ut/kv_offload/test_pool_worker_pp_object_bounds.py ``` On each of the two target branches independently: 33 passed with the fix; reverting only the production change causes 10 expected boundary failures and leaves 23 passing; restoring the fix gives 33 passed again. No skipped tests or collection errors. The new tests inspect every actual `LayerBatchBuilder` copy range, covering single/multiple MTP layers, unequal cache entries, PP0/PP1, all four shared DCP shards and 2 MiB alignment. Existing DeepSeek multi-group tests, block-key behavior, fallback, and layouts requiring no growth remain covered. CPU execution uses the real worker/builder with NPU interfaces mocked, without an SDK service. **Four-node NPU causal check, SSD enabled throughout:** Frozen runtime: vllm-ascend `394fa92ad2ee3499569dbed625c11866c2319cb9`, vLLM `ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607` (0.30.0), memcache/memfabric 1.3.0, Python 3.12.13, torch 2.10, torch_npu 2.10.post7. P: TP16 x PP2, partition 42/36, layerwise and MTP1, eager. D: DP16 x TP2, original MTP5 and FULL_DECODE_ONLY graph settings. Model, dependencies and native extensions were held fixed. No weights were moved. Each hardware stage used the same frozen 507-token input, concurrency 1, temperature 0 and seed 1024. The minimal reproducer caps output at 16; semantic checks allow 512 tokens. | Stage | Result | | --- | --- | | Original allocation | Last physical-layer save rejected with the address/range above and `-3102` | | Apply capacity fix | Allocation 7,092,024 bytes; no save error; two complete, correct arithmetic answers | | Withdraw capacity fix | Same input reproduces `-3102` at the same relative range | | Restore capacity fix | No save error; four complete correct answers; two replays each report 384 pool-hit tokens and request-associated G2L copies succeed, including PP1 layer 36 | For the restored PP1 layer 36, observed G2L entry lengths include both 83,968 and 32,768 bytes, result 0, associated with the replay request ID. This checks actual loading as well as saving. The arithmetic prompt asks for `17 + 25`; complete responses correctly answer 42 and stop normally. This is a focused functional/semantic check, not a general accuracy benchmark. **Scope and remaining coverage:** - Hardware A/B/A/B applies the production methods to the frozen runtime above. The three affected methods are AST-identical to this PR and its companion. It does not claim full NPU validation of the latest target branch and its complete dependency stack. Both target branches were separately imported and CPU-tested; main uses its pinned vLLM source. - SSD write coverage is observed: six objects flushed, 42,306,822 bytes. Replays above prove actual external loads, but do **not** establish DRAM eviction followed by SSD rewarm into the current request. The separate 1 GiB/worker SSD eviction/rewarm run was prepared but has not run; SSD read acceptance remains unverified. - One restored-stage launch failed because the previous Meta had not fully released its process lock. No model request was issued; it was classified as infrastructure failure and rerun after confirmed shutdown. - Ruff check/format, codespell, forbidden-import, boolean-context-manager, long-function and symbolic-meta checks passed separately on both branches. `bash format.sh ci` was attempted on both but blocked while downloading actionlint (network disconnect/timeout); the complete formatting pipeline is not reported as passed. Full target-stack NPU CI and broad accuracy/performance testing remain outstanding. - Temporary address/request diagnostics used for the hardware experiment are absent from this PR. Companion release PR: #19878. - vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c0b6f74bee518aeaf5d72b200a0216e72fbb5e7c --- Need help on this PR? added.author: Zhaocen
added.subject: [Feature][Model] Support GLM-5.3-Flash with PCP (#18511)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable prefill context parallelism (PCP) for GLM-5.3-Flash on Ascend.
KPool compression and cache writes consume global causal token order
while sparse queries remain local to each PCP rank.

For KPool configurations using packed SFA C8 main KV cache, this PR
depends on #19079 for cache layout selection, allocation, reshaping, and
associated regression coverage.

- Read PCP context and cache-group indices from
`AscendCommonAttentionMetadata` after rebasing. Keep metadata buffers
independent across MTP draft steps and graph replay.
- Gather and restore KPool inputs before compression. Keep NoPE SFA KV
and cache slots in matching rank-gather order, removing redundant
`index_select` operations and cache-write metadata.
- Restore causal token order for KDA recurrent updates and use global
request metadata for Runner V2 Mamba state handling.
- Shard KDA projections, gates, convolution weights, and recurrent state
across PCP ranks when TP=1, and reduce the output over PCP. Retain TP
head sharding when TP>1.
- Remove the leftover rank-based convolution initial-state override from
the shared GDN builder. Fresh requests and continuations retain their
actual initial-state masks without a GLM-specific builder.
- Add multimodal padding/EVS regression coverage for the existing Runner
V2 preparation flow. `vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_states/default.py`
matches the PR base and has no diff.
- Keep the main KPool capture adapter for capture-specific state-table
allocation; remove obsolete PCP kwargs forwarding and the redundant tail
capture override.

- Reuse the shared PCP cache-input gather for NoPE, preserving padded
rank strides and using the returned slot mapping to avoid duplicate
replicated decode writes.
- Separate Mamba PCP padding selection from context propagation, cache
PCP group information in KDA layers, and document remaining head/decode
sharding work with TODOs.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. GLM-5.3-Flash can use PCP on supported Ascend hardware through the
existing `--prefill-context-parallel-size` option. No new environment
variable or CLI option is introduced.

### How was this patch tested?

Current head: `98d23a27e06ef3b5ee64812bd885c78388bdf508`, one commit
based on Ascend main `7ec720c5f8a542e08729d3a785f365cd967da418`.

- **42 focused isolated CPU checks passed on `5d2d605f4`** (this head
only removes the release-note fragment; Python sources are unchanged),
executing methods and test functions from the current sources with
runtime imports and NPU/distributed boundaries mocked. Coverage includes
the NoPE shared-gather path with mixed decode/prefill, padded and empty
local inputs, KDA gather/output mapping, Mamba padding independent of
PCP context, GDN context propagation, and parallelism policy. This is
source-level isolated testing, not a normal full-module pytest or NPU
run.
- Regression tests updated in `tests/ut/attention/test_sfa_cp.py`,
`tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_kda_dispatch.py`,
`tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_kda_pcp.py`,
`tests/ut/ops/test_gdn_attn_builder.py`, and
`tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v2_mamba.py`.
- All-file `pre-commit run ruff-check --all-files --hook-stage manual`
and `pre-commit run ruff-format --all-files --hook-stage manual` passed.
- Python syntax checks passed for all 20 PR Python files; `git diff
--check` passed.
- Normal pytest for the five affected test modules could not load the
shared conftest on the local Windows CPU environment: vLLM is not
installed, and pointing PYTHONPATH at the local upstream checkout then
encounters the missing `uvloop` dependency.
- Full `bash format.sh ci` was attempted again but was interrupted after
the Markdown lint Node environment installation stalled during
dependency download. Full pre-commit/CI, NPU correctness/performance,
E2E, and PCP PIECEWISE capture/replay validation remain required before
merge.
- The earlier head `8851b761` previously passed 76 isolated CPU
regression cases; that broader isolated set was not rerun on this head.

added.author: Yunxiao Ning
added.subject: [BugFix][Engram] Align private Host-UVA payloads for correct device reads (#19695)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix incorrect device reads from small private Engram `HostUvaBuffer`
allocations observed on A3 with CANN 9.2.0. The current community
implementation can publish correct CPU data while the NPU reads
different bytes through the returned device alias.

Reserve at most 65,535 extra bytes per buffer and use a 64 KiB-aligned
payload for the CPU tensor, host registration and device-pointer query.
Retain the original allocation for `aclrtFreeHost` on normal close and
initialization rollback. Registration flags and lookup kernels stay
unchanged; there is no additional hot-path copy. This change is limited
to private `HostUvaBuffer`; it does not change `SharedUvaBuffer` or a
VMM allocator.

Observed on a 16,384-row INT8/FP32 table (4 MiB codes, 512 KiB scales):

| Check | Original private buffer | Aligned payload |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CPU publication | Exact | Exact |
| NPU raw codes | Exact | Exact |
| NPU raw scales | 122,850 byte mismatches | Exact |
| Indexed scales | 25/32 mismatches | Exact |
| Native and grouped gather/dequant | Incorrect | Exact |

The original scales host pointer had low 16 bits `0x1000`; the returned
alias lacked those low bits, and a source prefix fingerprint appeared at
byte offset 4096 in the NPU-read stream. Aligning the registered payload
removed the mismatch. This establishes a reproducible user-visible
failure and a tested workaround on this stack; it does not establish
which vendor layer is responsible or a universal 64 KiB API requirement.
Switching to MAPPED-only flags or grouped scale loads did not fix it.
Manual alias-offset experiments faulted and are INVALID, so they are not
the fix or correctness evidence.

Reproduction outline (pseudocode; compare through a device kernel, not
`aclrtMemcpy` on a registered alias):

```text
allocate private codes[16384, 256] as INT8
allocate private scales[16384, 8] as FP32
fill CPU views with deterministic codes and nonconstant power-of-two scales
record host_pointer % 65536 for each buffer
register each CPU payload and query its device alias
NPU kernel: read raw alias bytes into ordinary device output
compare output.cpu() with CPU payload bytes
NPU kernel: gather/dequant selected rows; compare with CPU reference
repeat with 64 KiB-aligned payloads inside the original allocations
```

Earlier #16689 design of the host-backed Engram has been ported to
current main. Related sharing work: #19528. This PR independently fixes
the current private Host-UVA implementation; it makes no claim that
those VMM or sharing designs are defective.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Private host-offloaded Engram lookups avoid the observed
small-buffer mapping corruption on A3/CANN 9.2. Each private buffer
reserves up to 65,535 additional host bytes. Release note:
`release_notes/fragments/19695.yaml` (bugfix).

### How was this patch tested?

- Added
`tests/ut/models/test_engram.py::test_host_uva_aligns_registration_and_frees_original_allocation`:
deliberately unaligned original allocation, aligned CPU/register/query
address, payload bounds and CPU alias writes, original-allocation free,
repeated close, and rollback on registration/device-pointer-query
failures.
- Local isolated-source CPU validation: all 45 cases PASS (5
allocation/registration outcomes x 3 dtypes x 3 alignment offsets). It
extracts the actual class and added test from source, supplies the CANN
mock and CPU tensors, and checks success, allocation error, successful
allocation with NULL output, registration failure and pointer-query
failure across UINT8/BF16/FP32 and offsets 0/4096/65535. This is **not**
a full pytest run or full vLLM import environment. Negative controls:
unfixed `origin/main` fails the alignment test; the previous PR head
fails all nine NULL-output cases with `TypeError`, while the updated
source raises a clear `RuntimeError` before registration or pointer
arithmetic.
- `bash format.sh ci` and `git diff --check`: PASS. Focused mypy 1.11.1
on the two affected files passes for Linux/Python 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12
(local missing imports ignored; full repository mypy is left to CI).
- Reused hardware evidence from A3/CANN 9.2.0: the actual fixed `npu.py`
loaded as a component overlay gives exact raw NPU bytes, indexed scales,
and native/grouped gather outputs against CPU data. Ten existing
component cases using Host-UVA lookup, real BF16 WKV projection weights,
gate outputs, eager execution and multistream graph replay report
correctness PASS. These are component checks, not a rebuilt full wheel
or full-model E2E, and imply no WKV performance claim. No new
accelerator job was started for this PR.
- Completed full-environment CPU CI on the current head: [run
40068579976](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/40068579976),
verified vLLM main: **12,348 passed / 82 skipped**; v0.31.0: **12,342
passed / 88 skipped**. All **45 added Host-UVA regression cases passed
in each lane**. Full repository pre-commit/mypy and DCO pass.
- Not validated: full-model E2E, other CANN versions/A5, or
shared-buffer small allocations. The remaining `ci-gate` failure is the
missing `ready-precise` label; pre-commit and both CPU UT lanes
succeeded. A [maintainer
request](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/19695#issuecomment-6380798181)
is posted because the author account cannot add labels.

To repeat the isolated CPU check from the repository root (requires CPU
PyTorch and pytest):

```bash
python3 - <<'PYTEST'
import ast
import ctypes
from pathlib import Path
from types import ModuleType, SimpleNamespace

import pytest
import torch

source = Path("vllm_ascend/models/deepseek_v41/engram/npu.py")
tests = Path("tests/ut/models/test_engram.py")
module = ModuleType("isolated_host_uva")
module.__dict__.update(
    ctypes=ctypes, torch=torch, CHUNK_ROWS=1 << 22,
    _host_library=lambda: None,
    DeviceOperator=SimpleNamespace(host_register_flags=lambda: 0x10000002),
)
cls = next(n for n in ast.parse(source.read_text()).body
           if isinstance(n, ast.ClassDef) and n.name == "HostUvaBuffer")
exec(compile(ast.Module(body=[cls], type_ignores=[]), str(source), "exec"), module.__dict__)
name = "test_host_uva_aligns_registration_and_frees_original_allocation"
test = next(n for n in ast.parse(tests.read_text()).body
            if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name == name)
test.decorator_list = []
namespace = dict(ctypes=ctypes, torch=torch, pytest=pytest, npu=module)
exec(compile(ast.Module(body=[test], type_ignores=[]), str(tests), "exec"), namespace)
for failure in (None, "malloc", "null", "register", "device_pointer"):
    for dtype in (torch.uint8, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32):
        for offset in (0, 4096, 65535):
            with pytest.MonkeyPatch.context() as patch:
                namespace[name](patch, failure, dtype, offset)
print("PASS: 45 isolated CPU lifecycle/rollback cases")
PYTEST
```

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: deliberately unaligned base and
payload bounds.
- [x] **Regression test**: unfixed source fails the added test.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: registration and pointer-query
rollback.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: CPU alias writes, address
ownership and lifecycle.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: allocation-only correctness fix; no
performance claim or full-model performance regression run.

added.author: YuhanBai
added.subject: [Refactor][WeightTransfer] Build HCCL engine reusing upstream NCCL engine (#18944)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

The HCCL backend duplicated the trainer/worker weight-transfer
orchestration already provided by upstream vLLM's NCCL engines. This PR
reuses that implementation and retains the HCCL-specific rendezvous, NPU
data plane, device binding and communicator lifecycle.

- Build the worker and trainer engines on `NCCLWeightTransferEngine` and
`NCCLTrainerWeightTransferEngine`. Reuse the upstream layerwise-reload
lifecycle, trainer send orchestration, metadata/iterator checks and
worker initialization payload.
- Define `HCCLWeightTransferInitInfo` in `hccl_common.py` as a subclass
of upstream `NCCLWeightTransferInitInfo`. Reuse upstream rank fields and
rendezvous validation while retaining HCCL's required TCP endpoint and
optional packed settings; reject NCCL-only unique-ID rendezvous.
- Register `HCCLTrainerInitInfo` and `HCCLTrainerWeightTransferEngine`
with `WeightTransferTrainerFactory`. Align the trainer's default with
upstream: `packed=True`.
- Keep HCCL-specific endpoint creation and explicitly assign trainer
rank 0 and worker rank offset 1.
- Synchronize inherited packed settings during initialization and
re-initialization. Preserve optional per-update packed settings and
reject conflicts with values fixed at initialization.
- Bind transfers to the assigned NPU and normalize source tensors before
broadcasting. In unpacked mode, synchronize each broadcast to keep its
staging tensor alive until the collective completes.
- Explicitly close HCCL communicators on shutdown and
initialization/send failures. Reject further sends from failed or closed
trainers.
- Remove the legacy worker-side static `trainer_init`,
`trainer_send_weights` and `HCCLTrainerSendWeightsArgs`, without
forwarding wrappers.
- Migrate both RL examples and the HCCL state-transition E2E test to the
trainer factory, upstream HTTP/Ray weight-sync clients and
`engine.send_weights()`.

The PR changes seven files: the HCCL engine, HCCL common helpers,
backend registration, HCCL unit tests, two RL examples and the HCCL
state-transition E2E test.

The packed utility fixes remain in #19127. This PR does not modify
`packed_tensor.py` or `npu_ipc_engine.py`, and the existing packed skip
in the checked-in E2E test remains unchanged.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Trainer integrations using the removed static interfaces must
migrate to `WeightTransferTrainerFactory`, `HCCLTrainerInitInfo`, a
weight source and an upstream weight-sync client. The updated HTTP and
Ray examples demonstrate the new API.

The new trainer defaults to `packed=True`, matching upstream. Set
`packed=False` explicitly to use unpacked transfers.

The `hccl` backend name and optional per-update packed settings remain
supported. Conflicting initialization and update settings now raise an
explicit `ValueError`. No new environment variable or CLI flag is
introduced.

### How was this patch tested?

**Unit tests — without #19127**

- **178 passed** across `tests/ut/distributed/weight_transfer` and
`tests/ut/distributed/device_communicators`.
- A separate rerun of
`tests/ut/distributed/weight_transfer/test_hccl_engine.py` completed
with **32 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.
- Coverage includes upstream inheritance and orchestration, packed
defaults, initialization/re-initialization, sender/non-sender
handshakes, worker rank offset, packed-setting conflicts, source
normalization, device binding, both receive modes, shutdown and failure

added.subject: [BugFix][CI] Align bisect rebuilds and AOP diagnostics with nightly (#17977)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Follow-up to #17902. Besides aligning candidate rebuilds with the
nightly uv installer, this migrates the remaining AOP/bisect hardening
from the test branch so the bisect pipeline matches nightly end to end:

- Candidate rebuilds now use `uv pip install -e . --no-deps` and `uv pip
install -r requirements-dev.txt` (nightly uv installer, no dependency
resolution), so a rebuilt candidate can no longer diverge from the
nightly baseline environment and skew bisect verdicts.
- `csrc/build` is cleaned before each rebuild: the custom-op build
preserves `CMakeCache.txt`, which can pin `HI_PYTHON` to a short-lived
uv build-environment interpreter and break the next candidate build in a
new isolated environment.
- Failed installs now record CMake Python-path diagnostics (`HI_PYTHON`,
`Python3_EXECUTABLE`, ...) before/after, append the tails of
`CMakeConfigureLog.yaml` / `CMakeError.log`, and surface the last 4 KB
of the build log in the job log — previously only "(see build log)" was
printed and the log died with the runner container. Candidate deployment
failures are logged as well.
- The single-node, 560T and multi-node nightly workflows now always
collect and upload AOP bisect diagnostics (bisect work dir, pytest logs,
initial test logs) as GitHub artifacts with 7-day retention, even when
the bisect step fails.
- Multi-node `run.sh` scopes bisect reports to the current LWS instance
(`BISECT_WORK_DIR` under `LOG_PREFIX`) so uploads do not mix in older
PVC runs.
- Single-node runners fall back to the legacy config dir
(`tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/models/configs`) when a bisected
candidate predates the config relocation.
- `tools/bisect` docs (README / USAGE_zh) updated to reflect the uv
commands.

Supersedes #17902 (includes its uv-installer alignment).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Auto-bisect candidate rebuilds use `uv pip install` instead of plain
`pip install`. No vLLM-Ascend runtime behavior changes; ordinary nightly
test execution is unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

- `python -m py_compile` on the modified `tools/bisect` modules,
`yaml.safe_load` on the three modified workflow files, and `bash -n` on
`run.sh` all pass locally.
- No new unit tests: the change is CI/diagnostic tooling that requires
the nightly image and package indexes to exercise (uv rebuild, artifact
uploads, CMake cache behavior). CI validation pending.

added.author: recky-c
added.subject: [Refactor][MRV2][PCP][Attention] Decide PCP layout from builder outputs (#19800)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Attention builders and cache-write paths currently treat an enabled PCP
configuration as proof that every step uses a PCP-sharded layout. A
replicated draft decode can have no PCP context and keep rank-local
slots, so that assumption can select the wrong metadata or an
unnecessary KV gather.

Resolve each step's PCP layout in the metadata builders and carry it as
`uses_pcp_sharded_layout` through dense attention, MLA, SFA and indexer
metadata. Execution consumes that flag instead of independently
inferring layout from slot lengths. DSA/V4.1 builders use the same
PCP-context decision for ordinary versus sharded metadata. Replicated
draft steps keep local cache writes; sharded steps retain the required
gathers, including ranks with no local queries.

On current main, target builds already carry PCP context and drafts use
PCP=1, so most existing paths retain their behavior. This establishes
the attention-layout contract needed by #19801 (draft-route alignment
and capture staging), followed by #19175 (partitioning the unpadded
global batch).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No new user-facing options or configuration changes.

### How was this patch tested?

Unit/static validation completed on 2026-10-27 for `270903edd`, using
vLLM `c0b6f74bee518aeaf5d72b200a0216e72fbb5e7c`. The real-model
comparison below was performed on `015140ba3` before the subsequent
rebase/refactor.

**Unit and communication tests**
- After the field rename in `b0145a2b5`, all attention unit tests plus
`tests/ut/ops/test_mla.py` and
`tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v2_mamba.py`: **2080 passed, 10
skipped**, 21 warnings, 24.85 s. These used the repository's CPU/mock
fixtures in the remote Ascend container.
- Regression coverage includes builder-resolved target/draft layout
flags, replicated drafts with padding or empty input, local cache
writes, sharded empty-owner participation, and graph capture/replay
metadata.
- Earlier validation on `015140ba3` used real NPU tensors and HCCL in a
separate two-rank test: rank-local replicated decode without a gather,
sharded KV gather with exact tensor/slot comparison, and padded
empty-owner collective participation all passed.

**Real-model inference against the parent commit**

Ran real Qwen3-0.6B weights, with Qwen3-0.6B-eagle3 for speculative
configurations, on two Ascend NPUs with **TP=1, PCP=2, BF16**, greedy
sampling and seed 42. Compared the PR against parent
`2ccd0552f962e6e34e4ae24245cf7ba7fca68c55` under the same source/runtime
environment (torch 2.10.0, torch_npu 2.10.0.post7).

| Configuration | Requests per revision | Compared output tokens | Token
mismatches | Max absolute selected-token logprob difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Eager, no speculation | 12 | 201 | 0 | 0 |
| Eager, Eagle3 with 3 speculative tokens | 12 | 201 | 0 | 0 |
| FULL_DECODE_ONLY, Eagle3 with 3 speculative tokens | 12 | 201 | 0 | 0
|

Each configuration covered a short singleton, a 743-token long
singleton, and mixed batches of 3 and 7 requests, with output limits
from 1 to 32 tokens. Prefix caching was enabled and the chunked-prefill
budget was 128 tokens. Across all configurations, each revision
completed **36 requests / 603 generated tokens**, with identical output
tokens and selected-token logprobs.

Logs confirmed target and draft graph capture plus active draft
prefill/decode ACL graph replay. Source-file hashes and import paths
were verified for both revisions.

Full-model coverage is limited to the tested dense-attention
Qwen3/Eagle3 path; MLA, SFA, DSA/V4.1 and Mamba-hybrid full-model runs,
dataset accuracy and performance benchmarks were not performed.

- Modified runtime files passed mypy 1.18.2 for Python 3.10, 3.11 and

diff --check`. The local full format entrypoint could not run because

added.subject: [BugFix] Strip stream_options on decode path when stream is false (#19622)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?
fix #19619

In
`examples/disaggregated_prefill_v1/load_balance_proxy_server_example.py`,
the
Prefill-Decode disaggregation proxy forwards requests to two backend
roles:

- **Prefill** via `send_request_to_service` -> `build_prefill_request`,
which forces
  `stream=False` and pops `stream_options` (`:834`).
- **Decode** via `stream_service_response`, which forwarded `req_data`
**as-is** without
  stripping `stream_options`.

`build_prefill_request` operates on a copy, so the original `req_data`
still carries
`stream_options` when handed to `stream_service_response`. When a client
sends a
**non-streaming** request with `stream_options`, the decoder receives
`stream=false + stream_options` and returns:

```
Stream options can only be defined when stream=True`. (parameter=stream_options)
```

Reproducing request:

```json
{
  "model": "glm5.3",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}],
  "stream": false,
  "stream_options": {
    "include_usage": true
  }
}
```

**Fix**: in `stream_service_response`, copy `req_data` and pop
`stream_options` only
when `stream` is falsy. Streaming requests keep `stream_options` (valid
for
`stream=true`); non-streaming requests have it stripped before reaching
the decoder.
Both decode call sites (initial pre-opened stream `:1065` and recompute
retry `:1130`)
go through this function, so both are covered.

This is safe because the proxy reconstructs usage information itself
(`update_cached_tokens_in_chunk` at `:1157`, `completion_tokens`
accounting at `:1171`)
and does not rely on the backend's `stream_options={include_usage}`
final usage chunk.

Fixes #<issue_number>

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This only affects the example proxy server
(`examples/disaggregated_prefill_v1/`).
Non-streaming requests that previously failed with a 400 error now
succeed; streaming
behavior is unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

Manual verification with a PD disaggregation deployment:

1. Start one prefiller and one decoder vLLM backend.
2. Start the proxy:
   ```bash
   python load_balance_proxy_server_example.py \
     --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9000 \
     --prefiller-hosts 127.0.0.1 --prefiller-ports 8100 \
     --decoder-hosts 127.0.0.1 --decoder-ports 8200
   ```
3. Send a non-streaming request with `stream_options` (previously
failed):
   ```bash
   curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:9000/v1/chat/completions \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{
       "model": "glm5.3",
       "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}],
       "stream": false,
       "stream_options": {"include_usage": true}
     }'
   ```
- Before: HTTP 400, `Stream options can only be defined when
stream=True`.
   - After: HTTP 200 with a valid completion response.
4. Send a streaming request with `stream_options` (regression check):
   ```bash
   curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:9000/v1/chat/completions \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{
       "model": "glm5.3",
       "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}],
       "stream": true,
       "stream_options": {"include_usage": true}
     }'
   ```
   - Streaming output and final usage chunk are delivered as before.

No unit tests were added because this is an example script (not part of
the
`vllm_ascend` package tested by `pytest`). The change is a 3-line guard
validated
manually end-to-end.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: Reviewed. Edge cases
considered:
`stream` absent (treated as falsy -> pop), `stream=true` (keep
`stream_options`),
  `stream=false` (pop), `stream_options` absent (pop is a no-op).
- [ ] **Regression test**: Manual regression check performed for the
streaming path
(step 4 above) to confirm `stream_options` is preserved when
`stream=true`.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: The fixed path is itself an
error/failure path
  (400 from decode backend on invalid `stream_options`).
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: Manual end-to-end verification on
a real PD
  deployment.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: Not applicable. A shallow `dict.copy()`
per decode request
  is negligible compared to network I/O.

added.author: Yunxiao Ning
added.subject: [Performance] Avoid redundant Engram lookup output initialization (#19657)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Engram preparation zero-initializes a local BF16 result that lookup
immediately overwrites. Allocate it with `torch.empty` instead, removing
one redundant full-result initialization per prepared layer. Both native
device-table and mapped-host kernels write every allocated local head,
including zeroes for invalid IDs; the CPU reference has the same
contract. Empty-token/empty-head tensors contain no elements to
initialize.

This follow-up comes from the Engram data-path investigations in #16689
and #19528. Credit to both efforts for motivating the removal of
intermediate buffer work: this patch applies their
final-buffer/overwrite reasoning to the existing common embedding path.
It is independent of their VMM/shared-owner changes and can merge on its
own.

DP row exchange, TP head all-gather, graph-buffer publication, and tail
padding are unchanged.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Lower local Engram preparation overhead, with no API/configuration or
numerical change. A performance release-note fragment is included.

### How was this patch tested?

- Added 24 parameterized dirty-buffer correctness cases for BF16/INT8,
TP-shaped heads 1/2/4, DP windows 1/2, zero/nonzero tokens,
non-contiguous layer IDs, and valid/invalid IDs. Newly allocated output
is poisoned with NaNs and checked before mocked collectives and at
return.
- Executed those cases locally using isolated production
`embed_gathered`, `lookup`, and CPU-reference source, because local vLLM
is unavailable. This bypasses package imports and mocks collectives; it
is not a native full-suite pytest run. In a normal test environment:
`pytest tests/ut/models/test_engram.py -k
lookup_overwrites_dirty_output_before_exchange`.
- A3 NPU: 24 HBM/local-host-VMM workload shapes passed native INT8
lookup versus CPU reference and graph-replay before/after equality. The
benchmark used the existing image's native lookup wrappers/kernels and
the modified preparation method; it was not a full wheel built from this
branch.
- `bash format.sh ci` and `git diff --check`.

Matched NPU microbenchmark, microseconds per layer preparation:

| Backing | Local heads | Tokens | zeros | empty | Time reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| HBM | 6 | 32 | 13.663 | 11.560 | 15.39% |
| HBM | 12 | 32 | 13.370 | 10.177 | 23.88% |
| HBM | 12 | 4096 | 197.403 | 182.265 | 7.67% |
| Local host VMM | 6 | 32 | 14.933 | 12.766 | 14.51% |
| Local host VMM | 12 | 32 | 14.778 | 12.238 | 17.19% |
| Local host VMM | 12 | 4096 | 403.760 | 392.944 | 2.68% |

Method: 65,536 fully initialized rows, 256 INT8 codes + 8 FP32 scales
per row, eight distinct seeded query batches per NPUGraph.
Baseline/candidate differ only in the output allocator. Three warmup
replays, ABBA timing phases (each >=0.2 s and >=20 samples); pooled
NPU-event median divided by eight calls. Tokens 32/128/1024/4096 and
local heads 6/12/24 were tested for both backings. The method's
ID-contiguity copy remains in both variants.

These are warm, single-NPU preparation timings. `tp_size=dp_size=1`
intentionally isolates allocation/initialization plus lookup; head
counts represent local shard sizes, not actual TP/DP execution. It does
not measure TP collectives, graph-buffer publication/padding, remote
HCCS reads, full-model E2E throughput, or a hardware bandwidth ceiling.
The local VMM setup used the adapter from #19528; the optimization
itself needs no VMM support. No E2E speedup is claimed.

### Checklist

- [x] Boundary / edge-case coverage: zero/nonzero tokens and invalid
IDs.
- [x] Meaningful tests: dirty outputs must be completely overwritten
before communication.
- [x] Performance evidence attached with measurement boundaries.
- [ ] Native multi-rank TP2/4 and full-model E2E validation for this
patch.

added.subject: [Bugfix] Fix N-gram speculative decoding compatibility with Triton 3.6.0 (#19912)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix an N-gram speculative decoding failure observed after upgrading to
Triton 3.6.0.

`ngram_spec_decode_kernel` passes `care_padding=False` to three
`tl.load` calls. The `tl.load` implementation in the affected
environment does not accept this argument, causing kernel compilation to
fail with:

```text
TypeError: load() got an unexpected keyword argument 'care_padding'
```

This PR removes the unsupported argument from the sampled-token, n-gram
matching, and draft-token loads in
`vllm_ascend/ops/triton/spec_decode/ngram.py`.

The existing bounds masks are preserved. Invalid matching candidates
remain excluded by `valid_n`, and draft-token loads retain `other=-1` to
pad unavailable draft positions. The n-gram matching algorithm,
longest-match/earliest-position selection, and valid-draft-count logic
are unchanged.

The corresponding fix for `releases/v0.30.0` is tracked in #19913.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Fixes the compilation failure when using N-gram speculative decoding in
the affected Triton 3.6.0 environment. No public API or configuration
changes.

### How was this patch tested?

Validation results have not yet been recorded.

Planned regression checks:
- Confirm that the kernel compiles and executes with Triton 3.6.0
without the `care_padding` argument error.
- Compare draft token IDs and valid draft counts against a reference
implementation, covering matching and non-matching sequences, block
boundaries, and cases with fewer than `k` available draft tokens.
- Run an end-to-end generation case with N-gram speculative decoding
enabled.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change
involves
boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max
values,
off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). Where applicable,
I
added unit tests covering these edge cases in `tests/ut/` or
`tests/e2e/`.
- [ ] **Regression test**: If this PR fixes a bug, I added a regression
test
  that would fail without the fix.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: I covered abnormal paths
(exceptions,
timeouts, out-of-range, division by zero) in addition to the happy path.
- [ ] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New tests assert real behavior
and are
  not written merely to satisfy CI.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: If this PR touches a performance-sensitive
path,
  I attached benchmark results and added performance regression tests.

added.subject: [Performance] Drop the redundant KDA padding mask in recurrent_kda for GLM5.3flash (#19620)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?
The KDA recurrent step zeroed graph-capacity padding rows with a full
[1, T, H, D] masked_fill on every layer and every decode step. None of
the consumers read those rows:

- the spec/MTP path merges with index_copy_, which copies valid token
rows only, and the destination was zeroed beforehand;
- the pure-decode path passes output_buffer, and write_recurrent_output
already copies valid rows and zeroes all captured padding in one launch;
- the mixed prefill+decode path takes chunk_kda output as-is, which
never masked its padding either.
### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
NO.
### How was this patch tested?

Precision:
We tested this PR on two datasets; on Gsm8k the score is 97.27 and on
AIME26 the score is 93.33%.
Performance:
10.6us can be saved in one-time forward(1.08ms).

added.author: zhichao-lin
added.subject: [BugFix][KV Pool] Fix Mooncake sleep/wake, PD handshake, and prefix-cache reset (#18118)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Port two KV-pool fixes onto current main. `patch_partial_wake_up` is not
included: current `EngineCore.wake_up` already resumes scheduling only
after the executor is fully awake.

**Mooncake sleep/wake and PD handshake**

- Unregister Mooncake transfer-engine buffers before CaMem sleep,
disconnect peers, and reregister them when waking with `kv_cache`.
- Retry `DONE_RECVING` on a fresh socket so a dropped handshake cannot
leave prefill holding KV.
- Abort an allocated remote-prefill request with an empty recv, so
decode does not wait for a transfer that will never start.
- Truncate the prefill prompt before the prefix-cache lookup and rebuild
`request.block_hashes`, so the shortened prompt is not looked up with
the original hashes.
- Count hybrid-attention prefill ports from each decode rank. Send
counts are applied only when remote DCP and PCP are both 1.

**Reset the Mooncake KV pool on prefix-cache reset**

- `AscendStoreConnector.reset_cache` drains the rank-0 send queue, then
calls `store.remove_all(force=True)`, so a put already queued on rank 0
cannot repopulate the pool after a weight update.
- Lookup ZMQ frames gain a tag: `lookup` or `reset`. Scheduler and
worker must be updated together.
- Mooncake layerwise returns `False`. Other backends return `None`.
- The scheduler does not clear in-flight save bookkeeping. The caller
must pause generation and wait until every writing rank has finished its
puts before `reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True)`. This branch no
longer has `_delayed_free_req_ids`; attention saves are fenced by
`wait_for_previous_save` and are not visible to the scheduler.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. Public APIs and request interfaces are unchanged. The fixes stay
inside the Mooncake KV-pool connector.

### How was this patch tested?

- `tests/ut/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/test_mooncake_connector.py`
and
`tests/ut/distributed/kv_transfer/utils/test_mooncake_transfer_engine.py`:
37 passed, with the workspace vLLM on `PYTHONPATH` and a Mooncake
`TransferEngine` stub.
- AscendStore unit tests cover reset ack/nack, tagged lookup frames,
`remove_all(force=True)`, and join-before-`remove_all`.

added.author: Xiaoliang
added.subject: [BugFix] Forward uses_mrope to NewRequestData.from_request in BalanceScheduler/DyntraLB (#19731)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

`NewRequestData.from_request()` strips the payload of multimodal items
that are fully covered by a prefix-cache hit. With the upstream default
`uses_mrope=False` it drops every payload field, including the
`keep_on_cpu` `image_grid_thw` / `video_grid_thw` that M-RoPE models
need to compute positions.

vLLM core's `Scheduler` already forwards
`uses_mrope=self.model_uses_mrope`, and the Ascend `RecomputeScheduler`
/ `scheduler_profiling_chunk` copies do the same. The balance-scheduling
copy (`patch_balance_schedule.py`) and `dyntra_lb_scheduler.py` do not,
so with `enable_balance_scheduling` (or DyntraLB) plus prefix caching,
an M-RoPE multimodal model crashes the engine when a request reuses a
cached video prefix.

Reproduced on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (hybrid Mamba model, block size 1152) with
vLLM 0.30.0 + vllm-ascend 0.30.0rc2, `--enable-prefix-caching
--additional-config '{"enable_balance_scheduling": true}'`. The second
request that hits the cached video prefix emits:

```
SchedulerOutput(scheduled_new_reqs=[NewRequestData(..., num_computed_tokens=4608,
  mm_features=[MultiModalFeatureSpec(data=None, modality='video', mm_position=PlaceholderRange(offset=4, length=3190), ...)])])
```

and the worker dies with:

```
File "vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_vl.py", line 2677, in _iter_mm_grid_hw
    t, h, w = mm_feature.data["video_grid_thw"].data.tolist()
TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable
```

which kills EngineCore (`EngineDeadError`, HTTP 500).

After the fix, the same two-request sequence succeeds and the cached
second request keeps the CPU-side grid fields.

Fixes #19727

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This is an internal scheduler fix (forwarding `uses_mrope` to
`NewRequestData.from_request`). It does not change public APIs, CLI
flags, configuration keys, or output semantics; it only prevents an
engine crash and restores the intended behavior for M-RoPE models with
prefix caching.

### How was this patch tested?

Unit tests (CPU only), in
`tests/ut/patch/platform/test_patch_balance_schedule.py`:

- `test_mrope_ascend_schedulers_forward_uses_mrope_to_from_request` —
source guard over every `NewRequestData.from_request()` call in
`patch_balance_schedule.py` and `dyntra_lb_scheduler.py`.
- `test_balance_schedule_forwards_uses_mrope_to_new_request_data` —
schedules a real `BalanceScheduler` with `model_uses_mrope=True` and
asserts `from_request` receives `uses_mrope=True`.

Both pass with the fix (`2 passed`) and both fail when the fix is
reverted (`2 failed`), so they guard against regression.

End-to-end on Ascend 910B (2 NPU, TP2, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, vLLM 0.30.0 +
vllm-ascend 0.30.0rc2, `--enable-prefix-caching`, balance scheduling
enabled, OpenCV video backend):

1. Send `video + long text` twice; the second request hits the prefix
cache (`num_computed_tokens=4608` covering the whole video span).
2. Before the fix: request 2 fails with HTTP 500 / `EngineDeadError` and
the traceback above.
3. After the fix: both requests succeed (`OK`, 4 output tokens) and the
log contains no traceback.

### Checklist

- [x] The title contains a change-type tag accepted by the CI title
check (`[BugFix]`).
- [x] Applicable test coverage and validation results are recorded in
this PR.
- [x] CI checks pass before merge.
- [ ] Outstanding NPU hardware or performance validation is completed
before merge.

- Adapt version gates, KV-cache planner imports, attention/metadata, PCP
and speculative-decoding interfaces to the exact release/main contracts.
- Migrate Ascend schedulers to upstream's `skip_zeroing_group_ids`
contract, preserving asynchronously transferred KV state.
- Initialize target metadata on all PP stages and draft metadata only
where a drafter exists; forward EPLB `model_name`.
- Read GLM5Next text-model configuration from `hf_text_config` and
forward the tail-cache `record_for_zeroing` decision.
- Avoid double normalization in the Qwen vision path while preserving
dtype conversion.
- Align FastAPI in both dependency declarations to `>=0.133.0,<0.137.0`;
add the release-note fragment.

### Why these four compatibility commits are needed

These are the four retained behavioral adaptations added after the
initial release-lane migration. They add logic or interfaces missing
from the previous dual-version implementation. Changes that only
relabel/remove a version condition or reuse an already-correct version
branch are excluded from this section. Commit links below use the
rebased history currently in this PR; the two combined commits address
separate contracts.

| Commit | Why the previous implementation fails | What changes and why
|
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`54547b74c` — scheduler KV
zeroing](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/commit/54547b74cc531a041bb3fd489cc8ded5f0c8bc0a)
| Upstream v0.32 removes `_skip_zero_block_ids` and
`get_zeroing_block_ids_in_range`. The Ascend async remote-KV path still
accessed them, producing an AttributeError. Recreating the old set alone
would not restore upstream's zeroing behavior. | Recompute, DyntraLB and
profiling-chunk schedulers pass connector-loaded group IDs through
`allocate_slots(skip_zeroing_group_ids=...)` during asynchronous loads.
Remove the obsolete post-allocation bookkeeping. Received groups are
protected from zeroing races while other groups/local allocations retain
normal zeroing. The V4 Flash PD failure has a matching runtime stack;
related Pro/V4.1 cases share the affected path but their original
first-error stacks were incomplete. |
| [`8d4cea773` — PP metadata and draft
EPLB](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/commit/8d4cea7734e0c164485b567b5823f69973d91cb5)
| **PP:** upstream's initializer also initializes a drafter, while
Ascend owns a drafter only on the last PP stage and initializes it after
binding KV tensors. Calling the inherited initializer on an earlier
stage asserts on `None`. **EPLB:** the upstream caller now supplies
`model_name`, which the Ascend override did not accept. | **PP:** build
target attention metadata on every stage, preserve microbatch/block-size
handling and reorder-threshold calculation, and leave drafter
initialization in Ascend's existing later path. **EPLB:** accept
optional `model_name` and forward it to the parent, preserving named
target/draft registration rather than discarding the argument. These
address GLM 200k PP-PD and the A5 GLM registration TypeError; the later
HIXL error is a separate issue. |
| [`0751e6271` — Qwen visual
normalization](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/commit/0751e627109889a97f18b3c3571f242e99f77b48)
| Ascend already normalizes image/video patches before its vision call.
The v0.32 upstream vision encoder also installs a normalizer, so the
composed path normalizes twice and changes the input distribution. This
is a concrete source defect consistent with the 310P TextVQA regression.
| Keep Ascend preprocessing, including encoder-graph selection, and
replace only `self.visual.input_norm` with `IdentityInputNorm`. Preserve
dtype conversion and apply numerical normalization once. Both 310P Qwen
cases later passed; 27B reaches 81.0352 against the unchanged >=78
threshold, without claiming complete restoration to the old 83.16
result. |
| [`17f336860` — GLM Flash configuration and PD tail
cache](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/commit/17f3368600edaee5ac07a81ed0e3430e2fc3484e)
| **Configuration:** the Transformers-native text configuration is
nested under `hf_text_config`; reading text-only linear-state fields
from outer `hf_config`, or relying on old vendored helper
properties/aliases, fails during construction/state-shape calculation.
**Tail cache:** the upstream coordinator passes `record_for_zeroing`,
missing from Ascend's external tail allocation signature. |
**Configuration:** use `Glm5NextTextConfig`/`hf_text_config` for target,
MTP and state shapes; use native field names and layer types, keep MTP
on MLA, preserve trained constants and Ascend rotary scaling, and reject
unsupported sparse-indexer configuration explicitly. **Tail cache:**
accept and honor `record_for_zeroing` when claiming a ring block;
externally initialized async state can skip zeroing while local
allocations default to normal zeroing. GLM Flash 130k PD later passed.
The defects are source-confirmed, but missing original CI rank stacks
limit attribution of that first failure. |

The linked nightly results below are model-level follow-up evidence.
Earlier isolated checks establish individual API/method contracts, not
full hardware coverage. Five optional PP/EPLB/GLM regression files were
subsequently removed at the author's request; the production adaptations
remain. These four commits do not claim to fix PCP startup-time
variability, the reverted Triton/build-policy issues, or existing
shutdown warnings.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

The supported vLLM release becomes v0.32.0. Compatibility corrections
restore affected model startup, PD execution and Qwen visual accuracy
under that release.

Temporary PCP diagnostic/comparison code and both diagnostic YAML cases
have been removed. The original PCP case retains its 2800-second
readiness timeout. Experimental Triton/torch-npu pin changes and
build-isolation workarounds have been reverted; this PR has no net
workflow installation changes relative to its current base. The five
optional regression files requested for removal are absent; their
production fixes remain.

added.author: ckeyever
added.subject: [BugFix][KV Transfer] Isolate dense DP replica endpoints (#19744)
added.body: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Dense-model DP engines run independently. vLLM preserves the original serving replica in `parallel_config.data_parallel_index`, then resets the compute `data_parallel_rank` to zero. The connectors currently use that reset rank to allocate endpoints, so replicas on the same host can bind the same address during startup even when the port was free before launching the service. Use the preserved serving index for: - Mooncake V1 scheduler metadata and worker handshake ports. - Mooncake V2 scheduler control ports and worker handshake metadata. - AscendStore lookup IPC paths, shared by the scheduler and worker. For example, dense DP=2 / TP=1 with `MooncakeConnectorV2` and `kv_port=47000` currently gives both schedulers port `47001`. With this change their control ports are `47001` and `47002`. The corresponding AscendStore lookup paths end in `dp_rank0` and `dp_rank1` even if both replicas use `lookup_rpc_port="0"`. The change only uses the serving identity for endpoint allocation; compute DP configuration is unchanged. Existing MoE rank/index layouts retain their endpoints. This fixes connector initialization shared by Model Runner V1 and V2. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Independent dense DP replicas can allocate distinct Mooncake and AscendStore lookup endpoints instead of colliding during startup. No new configuration is required. The guide clarifies that independently launched services sharing the RPC base directory still need different `lookup_rpc_port` identifiers. A numbered bugfix release note fragment is included in this PR. The current TCP port allocations of MooncakeConnector (V1) and MooncakeConnectorV2 may still overlap ports reserved by other workers or components. This includes V1 worker handshake ports and V2 scheduler control ports. DP-specific endpoint identities do not guarantee disjoint TCP port ranges; the guide and lookup helper document this remaining risk separately from lookup IPC isolation. ### How was this patch tested? - Added regressions covering dense replicas with compute rank zero and serving indices 0/1, ordinary MoE rank/index layouts, V2 scheduler TP=1/2, V1 scheduler/worker port agreement, V2 worker handshake identity, and simultaneous binding of two real AscendStore ZMQ IPC servers. - Local CPU checks: **11 cases passed, plus 5 subtests**. The new dense cases fail against the base implementation and pass with the fix. This used a local import bootstrap based on `tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/_mock_deps.py` for unavailable torch/vLLM/NPU dependencies. Endpoint constructors, address calculations and the ZMQ IPC binds execute the production code; these results do not validate NPU execution or KV transfers. - A broader `test_pool_scheduler.py` run under that same bootstrap reports 70 passed and 6 failures. Those same six failures also occur against the base implementation (unrelated joint-prefix ownership and receive-completion cases under the dependency mocks). A full run with the project's actual dependencies remains for CI. - `bash format.sh ci`, Python compilation and `git diff --check` passed. - Targeted type check: mypy 1.11.1 on `test_pool_scheduler.py` passes for Python targets 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12. Both reported `zmq.Context` / `zmq.REP` errors reproduce on the previous commit for all three targets. Local checks use `--follow-imports skip --check-untyped-defs --ignore-missing-imports` because torch/vLLM dependencies are unavailable; the source adds no type-error suppressions. - NPU service startup / prefill-decode transfer validation was not available locally and remains required before merge. In a project test environment, the focused selection is: ```bash pytest -q \ tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2/test_base_scheduler.py \ tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2/test_base_worker.py \ tests/ut/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/test_mooncake_connector.py \ tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/test_pool_scheduler.py \ -k 'dp_schedulers or initializes_parallel_layout or dp_workers or initializes_parallel_ranks or dp_replica or TestGetZmqRpcPathLookup' ``` --- ### Checklist #### Testing - [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: Dense rank reset, replica indices 0/1, ordinary MoE layout, and TP=1/2. - [x] **Regression test**: New dense-replica cases fail without the fix. - [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: No new error-handling paths; the regressions cover the endpoint collision that caused startup failure. - [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: Exercise production constructors and real IPC sockets; no fixed TCP-port binds in unit tests. - [ ] **Performance impact**: Only initialization-time endpoint identity changes; no hot-path changes or performance claims. - vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c0b6f74bee518aeaf5d72b200a0216e72fbb5e7c --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. --------- Signed-off-by: ckey_Dou Co-authored-by: ckey_Dou

added.subject: [CI] Add Ascend recipe previews and validate against renderer main (#19788)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Recipe changes in vLLM Ascend need to trigger the existing preview and
publication pipeline in `vllm-project/recipes`. This adds the
source-side integration following [vLLM
#63248](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63248) and
[#63259](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63259).

- Send `preview-pr` for recipe PR open, update, reopen, and close events
targeting `main`, and `recipes-updated` for recipe changes pushed to
`main`. Both payloads identify `source: vllm-ascend`.
- Reuse the existing PR labeler for the `recipe` label and expose the
Ascend preview through the workflow environment's **View deployment**
link.
- Document the GitHub App credentials, environment restrictions,
activation order, and end-to-end verification steps in
`recipes/README.md`.
- Remove the temporary validation `renderer-ref`, so the Recipes check
and local validation use the renderer's `main` branch, matching vLLM.

The workflow never checks out or executes PR code. It mints a
short-lived App token scoped to `vllm-project/recipes` and validates PR
numbers before dispatching.

Dispatch stays disabled until the repository Actions variable
`RECIPES_PREVIEW_ENABLED` is set to `true`: the current recipes receiver
still treats all preview events as vLLM PRs. Validation now follows
recipes `main`. At the checked renderer revision
`05b4c575fcd92276332265c52ab259f2f2a93184`, Ascend source registration

prerequisites; this PR does not configure them.

deployment link. There are no inference API, model, or runtime
configuration changes. This is CI/tooling/documentation work, so no
release note fragment is required.

added.subject: [CI] Install the FLA NPU wheel in the main2main runner (#20019)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

The scheduled `Main2Main` job (`schedule_main2main.yaml`) never
installed the `flash-linear-attention-npu` wheel, while PR CI installs
it explicitly in `_selected_tests.yaml`. Since `vllm_ascend` eagerly
imports `fla_npu.ops.ascendc` (`ops/gdn.py`, `ops/kda.py`,
`ops/kimi_kda.py`, `models/glm5next/ops/causal_conv1d.py`), the
main2main runner could not even import those modules, and every GDN/KDA
e2e suite failed.

The knock-on effect was not just a red lane: the adaptation agent
answered the missing package with a source-level stub, which put
`gdn.py` in the adaptation diff. The gate's own-diff triage (`flow.py`,
traceback files ∩ diff) then read the runtime `RuntimeError: fla_npu is
not installed` as a self-inflicted regression, so it could never be
classified as inherited/environmental. Two e2e rounds and one fix round
later the failing set was byte-identical and the gate stopped on
`stop_loss_no_progress` without producing a PR (#275, #276, #277).

This PR closes the root cause only: install the same pinned a3/aarch64
wheel that PR CI uses, verify its sha256, verify `import
fla_npu.ops.ascendc`, and fail the job at that point rather than hours
later inside the gate.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. Test/CI tooling only; no shipped runtime behaviour, no env var, no
requirements entry (`requirements*.txt` is intentionally unchanged — PR
CI installs this wheel outside the dependency set).

### How was this patch tested?

- YAML parses (`yaml.safe_load`); step order is`Install vllm-ascend` →
`Install FLA NPU wheel` → `Save csrc cache` → `Run main2main flow`.
- `bash -n` on the new step body (git bash), job shell is `bash -el
{0}`.
- `FLA_VERSION`, wheel name and sha256 copied verbatim from
`_selected_tests.yaml:275-288`; download falls back to the same
`gh-proxy.test.osinfra.cn` prefix PR CI uses.
- End-to-end confirmation needs the next scheduled run: step-1 logs must
show
 no `No module named 'fla_npu'`, and `gate_e2e_result.json`
  `rounds[0].failing` must no longer contain
  `two_card/model_runner_v2/test_qwen3_6_dflash.py`,
  `two_card/model_runner_v2/test_qwen3_6_dspark.py`,

`two_card/spec_decode/test_spec_decode_heavy.py::test_qwen36_35b_dspark_spec_decoding`.
- Not covered here (tracked separately): the adapter-side trap that
converts an
environment gap into a source patch, and the UT gate's missing exemption
for
  collection errors on the release lane.

added.subject: [BugFix][Attention] Keep M3 FP8 KV alignment in model-specific backends (#19179)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Follow up on #18125 for MiniMax-M3 mixed FP8/BF16 KV with pipeline
parallelism, and keep the model-specific alignment policy in the M3
module.

With TP4/PP2 and a `32,28` layer partition, PP0 starts with dense
attention while PP1 starts with a sparse indexer. The skip-layer
configuration is shared across stages. Upstream heterogeneous-KV
alignment uses the first stage-local backend: #18125 gives the dense
backend a 64-token alignment minimum, but the sparse/indexer backends
still advertise only 128. The reproduced result is PP0=128 / PP1=256,
with indexer-cache allocation OOM in the hardware negative control.

The implementation now keeps all three M3 declarations in
`models/minimax_m3/msa_m3.py`:

- Move the M3 configuration predicate and 64-token alignment minimum out
of `utils.py`. Restore the generic `AscendAttentionBackend` declaration
to `[128]`.
- Add `AscendMiniMaxM3DenseBackend`, inheriting the standard dense
implementation and metadata builder. After normal upstream `Attention`
construction, M3 GQA layers specialize only the exact standard backend
in the affected configuration. A3 and alternate backend selections keep
their original backend. The subclass explicitly preserves the parent's
context-parallel capability.
- Dense, sparse and indexer M3 backends conditionally advertise
`[64,128]` under the same M3 / FP8-or-FP8_E4M3 / skip-layer /
`FP8_ATTENTION` hardware guard. Upstream alignment then resolves the
final FP8 block to 128 regardless of stage-local backend order.

The initial runner cache block remains 128. The value 64 is the
alignment minimum; regression tests exercise the real
`select_common_block_size` function and confirm 128-token FP8 execution.
No platform alignment override, model-runner change, inference-kernel
change, new environment variable or CLI flag is introduced.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Affected M3 mixed-KV PP configurations can initialize with consistent
128-token FP8 cache/kernel blocks, including stages without dense
layers. Existing command lines remain valid. A3, other models/dtypes,
configurations without skip layers and alternate attention backend
selections retain their original routing/declarations. The
model-specific decision runs during initialization. Release note:
`release_notes/fragments/19179.yaml`.

### How was this patch tested?

#### Current revision: `16b55af10811cb24d09654dd3de46e68d84ee4ca`

- Rebased onto Ascend main `b4dded02a` on 2026-10-28 to include #19992,
which removes duplicate Mooncake test module names that blocked both
CPU-UT lanes in [CI
40515899163](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/40515899163).
All five PR patches replay byte-for-byte unchanged according to `git
range-diff`; the push triggers fresh CI. The preceding rebase onto
`8cff540bb6d46a8ba0e53d3bd2e2570444645ebd` resolved import conflicts in
`msa_m3.py` and `attention_v1.py` caused by main's v0.32 main2main
cleanup: preserve main's removal of `vllm_version_is` and its
unconditional batch-invariance declarations, while keeping M3 block
policy model-local. Main's PCP layout changes are retained. All five
commits retain their DCO sign-offs; no block-policy or inference-kernel
change was added.
- **380 related CPU tests passed after the preceding conflict resolution
at `4df3f9948`** (2.82 s), using the complete new Ascend-verified vLLM
source `544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542` through isolated
source paths and existing CPU-test dependencies. The CI compatibility
lanes are now verified main and `v0.32.0`:
`TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 python -m pytest -q
tests/ut/test_minimax_m3_kv_block_size.py
tests/ut/models/minimax_m3/test_msa_m3.py
tests/ut/models/minimax_m3/test_minimax_m3.py
tests/ut/attention/test_attention_v1.py`.
- Coverage includes PP1/PP2/PP4 configuration values;
dense/indexer/sparse-first and single-backend stages; repeated
alignment; real common-kernel selection retaining 128; actual M3
dense-layer constructor routing across A2/A3/A5, five KV dtypes, skip
layers on/off and standard/alternate backend choices; and inherited
dense implementation, builder, cache shape and CP behavior.
- The model-local runtime changes (pre-rebase commit `5e2d7626`,
integration `bc444431`) **passed A5 hardware validation** with verified
vLLM `c0b6f74b` and official #19129's previous interface through
`9bfa7329`. The latter matches this upstream revision without #63017;

Max sequences 128, batch tokens 4096, max length 133000, memory

#### Full GPQA Diamond accuracy validation (2026-10-27)

- **180/198 correct, 90.9091%**, exceeding the requested strict >90%

`bc444431`, verified upstream vLLM `c0b6f74b` and official #19129

added.subject: [Feature][MRV2] Default VL encoder disaggregation to Model Runner V2 (#19183)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Unset `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER` now keeps VL encoder disaggregation on
Model Runner V2. This removes both halves of that blacklist entry:

- `ec_transfer_config` is configured (`VL encoder disaggregation`)
- `mm_encoder_only` is set and `ec_transfer_config` is not (`VL
encoder-only`)

`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` still forces V1, and `=1` still forces V2.
VL encoder graph (`compilation_config.cudagraph_mm_encoder`) stays on
the V1 blacklist.

Mooncake and CPU-offload EC tests already pin
`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`. The unset-env cases this changes are
`tests/e2e/pull_request/two_card/test_disaggregated_encoder.py`
(`Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct`, `ECExampleConnector`) and the weekly
`qwen2-5-vl-7b-epd` case.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. With `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER` unset, a request that sets
`ec_transfer_config` or `mm_encoder_only` now uses Model Runner V2. Set
`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` to keep V1.

### How was this patch tested?

- Unit tests updated: `tests/ut/test_mrv2_utils.py`.
`ec_transfer_config` and `mm_encoder_only` moved from the V1 blacklist
cases to the default-V2 cases. Explicit env override still wins.
- NPU e2e was not run here. CI should run `test_disaggregated_encoder`.

---

involves boundary conditions. The unit test covers both

override.

test that would fail without the fix.

addition to the happy path.

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR corrects two items in the **A2 sections only** of the
DeepSeek-V4-Flash guide — 5.2.5 (A2 DSpark) and 5.2.6 (A2 KV Pooling).
No A3, 950DT, single-node or other section is touched.

**1. Remove `enable_flashcomm1` from the three A2 prefill commands.**

It was introduced in #19505 / #19506 but cannot take effect on this
topology: SP MoE requires `tensor_parallel_size > 1`, and all three A2
prefill scripts run with `--tensor-parallel-size 1`. On a running A2
32-card deployment the engine printed, on every one of 14 prefill
starts:

```
FlashComm1 is enabled, but the current config does not support sequence parallelism
(requires tensor_parallel_size > 1, pipeline_parallel_size == 1, and an SP-capable model family: ...). Disabling.
```

Keeping an inert flag in the sample commands suggests a throughput
benefit that cannot occur here.

**2. Record the measured decode draft profile: draft 4 /
`--max-num-seqs` 51.**

`decode-4k-stable` and `decode-16k` previously recorded draft 1 / 128.
Draft depth and `--max-num-seqs` are coupled by the MoE all-to-all
dispatch bound `max-num-seqs * (1 + draft) <= 256`, so the per-draft
ceiling is 1->128, 2->85, 3->64, 4->51, 5->42, 6->36. Deeper drafts emit
more tokens per step but shrink the concurrency budget, so the useful
metric is the product of the two and the optimum has to be measured.

### Occupancy is the precondition for a valid comparison

A decode engine can only be judged on throughput when its request slots
are actually full. Define per-engine occupancy as `(client concurrency /
DP size) / max-num-seqs`. Measured on the same 16K workload:

| Draft / mns | Client CC | Actual concurrency per engine | Slot cap |
Occupancy | Relative throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 / 128 | 640 | 35.3 | 128 | 28% | 0.267 (invalid - slots 72% empty) |
| 5 / 42 | 640 | 35.4 | 42 | 84% | 0.349 |
| 6 / 36 | 576 | 31.2 | 36 | 87% | 0.339 |
| 3 / 64 | 960 | 52.1 | 64 | 81% | 0.368 |
| **4 / 51** | **816** | **45.3** | **51** | **89%** | **0.403** |

At 28% occupancy the engine is starved by the client, not limited by the
draft depth, so that row cannot be used to compare configurations. With
every candidate fed to roughly 80-90% of its slot cap, draft 4 / 51 is
the measured optimum for this topology: throughput rises with
concurrency up to about 45 requests per engine and falls back beyond
that. The same depth also lifted the 4K stable row, so both rows now
record 4 / 51.

`--gpu-memory-utilization` is left unchanged: the measured runs used
0.96 on prefill and 0.97 on decode, and an 0.98 decode value failed to
start on the reference machine, so the documented values stay
conservative.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

Documentation only. Readers of the A2 DSpark and A2 KV Pooling sample
commands see one fewer `--additional-config` key and a different decode
draft profile in two table rows.

### How was this patch tested?

Documentation only, no code paths change. The numbers come from an A2
32-card deployment (16P+16D, `dev-26.2.0.day20261026` image) driven by
the stock AISBench client: the 16K rows used the native total window,
the 4K stable row used the AISBench native stable window. The
`enable_flashcomm1` behaviour was confirmed both by reading the
`use_sequence_parallel_moe` gate in `vllm/config/parallel.py` and by the
engine log line quoted above.

Honor `mamba_ssm_cache_dtype` for GLM KDA recurrent state by passing it
directly to the upstream `MambaStateDtypeCalculator.kda_state_dtype` in
both layer allocation and model-level cache sizing. This makes explicit

upstream dtype policy.

state is rejected. BF16 storage can affect numerical results and
automatically selected cache geometry.

selection, model/layer cache-spec consistency, page sizing, and
rejection of unsupported state dtypes.

includes FP32 and BF16 state.

identical except for one row: W4A8 MXFP is **rejected** here because

documented default, range, error message, log string, and example was
verified against code; an independent documentation-review pass then

Main fixes:

**User guide (`expert_parallelism_load_balancer.md`)**

clarified as layout-based (`supports_eplb = False`) on all hardware, not

require tuning" advice (window_size 50 / step_interval 50 / redundant
defaults). It is now split into a minimal production command and a

explicit warning.

anchor).
- `load_collection_phase`: documented that it only takes effect with the
STAIR policy (the phase filter is gated on `uses_custom_load_stats` in
`worker/v2/eplb.py`), that values other than `all` require
`--enable-eplb`, that non-matching batches still advance the shared
window, and that a fully non-matching phase skips the next rearrangement
instead of running on an empty window.
- Monitoring: corrected the MRv1 log anchor from the nonexistent
`[Expert Hotness]` to the real `[eplb/worker] Expert hotness imbalance`
line and added MRv2 log anchors; precise env-var accepted values
(`DYNAMIC_EPLB` case-insensitive `true`/`1`, `EXPERT_MAP_RECORD` exactly

warning; described the Random policy accurately (fixed expert pair,
needs >= 4 EP ranks); recommend absolute paths for
`expert_map_record_path`; added the MRv1 update-cycle formula and

stated the `load_collection_phase` constraints.

`eplb/utils.py` from the module tree, replaced the stale DFX code
samples with the actual `EplbConfig` validation behavior, aligned the
`rebalance_experts` contract (`(changed_flag, per_layer_priority,
new_expert_table)`) and the new-MoE-model integration steps with the
current adaptor, and documented the runtime lifecycle (subprocess,
iteration formula, heat classification). `model_runner_v2_eplb.md` —
STAIR is the default policy, phase filtering only applies to
custom-load-stats policies, initial redundant experts are spread
round-robin (differs from upstream), corrected the committed-cycle log
semantics (imbalance ratios, lower is better), and added debug log
anchors.

Ascend policy (was "upstream default policy"); the feature-matrix EPLB

added.subject: [BugFix] Backport nonpersistent image normalization buffers (#20008)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Qwen3-VL legacy pre-sharded checkpoints fail to start on vLLM v0.32.0
with `Missing keys ('visual.input_norm.weight',
'visual.input_norm.bias')`:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/40524055660/job/122258855663.

Backport the runtime semantics of upstream
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62767 without copying its full
implementation: wrap `FusedMMInputNorm.__init__` once and re-register
its processor-derived weight/bias buffers with `persistent=False`. Their
initialized values and device movement are preserved; the buffers no
longer participate in sharded checkpoint requirements or dummy weight
initialization. Learned-weight validation remains strict.

Register the patch before model construction in the common worker path
so it covers 310P as well as the other Ascend devices. It is safe to
apply on the verified upstream main that already includes the fix.
Document removal once every supported vLLM baseline contains upstream
commit `90c4a1a73eecea0428ee4303ad96c9fdeaac3f80` or an equivalent
backport. The process-local wrapper is installed once; no per-request
mutable state is introduced.

The existing Qwen3VL-8B-310p nightly commands, weights and
accuracy/performance thresholds are unchanged. Device-side image
normalization remains enabled. This is the runtime-fix alternative to
the CPU-normalization configuration workaround in #20003.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Legacy Qwen3-VL sharded checkpoints can retain default device-side
normalization without requiring processor-derived normalization
constants in the checkpoint.

### How was this patch tested?

- Isolated `VllmConfig` construction by mocking
`NPUPlatform.check_and_update_config` only during configuration
creation. This avoids unrelated Ascend logging/device initialization and
cross-test global-config pollution; normalizer and loader assertions
still use the real implementations. The prior CPU jobs both stopped in
fixture setup with a mocked log path; CPU CI must rerun on commit
`85bea4a8acc98169ad8a2552ccb8aeecd2684ee2`.

- Added eight parametrized CPU regressions in
`tests/ut/patch/worker/test_patch_mm_input_norm.py`, exercising both
persistent (v0.32) and nonpersistent (fixed upstream) constructor
contracts: real safetensors legacy-shard loading, rejection of a missing
learned parameter, dummy loading preserving constants, float32/float16
normalization over the full byte range, and repeated patch installation.
- Passed local Ruff check and format check, Python byte compilation,
`git diff --check`, `tools/check_long_functions.py`, and
`tools/check_symbolic_meta.py`.
- Executed the actual nightly dispatcher with `Qwen3VL-8B-310p`: only
`dispatch_310p=true`.
- Runtime UT cannot run on this Windows host: the available Python
environment lacks pytest, torch and vLLM. PR CPU CI runs against both
the verified vLLM main and v0.32.0.
- Attempted required `bash format.sh ci`; stopped after prolonged lack
of progress installing the actionlint environment. Full Linux
pre-commit/mypy validation remains pending CI.
- Real 310P accuracy/performance validation requested through `/nightly
Qwen3VL-8B-310p --vllm-ref v0.32.0` to exercise the unfixed upstream
release plus this patch; results are pending. Checkpoints exported with
the old persistent buffers are not covered by this legacy-shard
regression.
- AI assistance was used to implement and prepare this change.

### Checklist

- [x] Boundary / edge-case coverage: both upstream persistence contracts
and full byte-range channel-distinct inputs.
- [x] Regression test added for the original legacy-shard failure.
- [x] Error / failure path coverage: genuinely missing learned weights
still fail.
- [x] Meaningful tests use the upstream normalizer, dummy loader and
safetensors loader.
- [ ] Real 310P accuracy/performance and full Linux CI results pending.

added.subject: [CI][Misc] Make the main2main runner selectable and drop its cron trigger (#20087)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

The main2main job was pinned to linux-aarch64-a3-16-sh-001 and only
started from the in-repo cron entry. Neither could be changed at run
time, so a single unhealthy machine left the whole pipeline blocked, and
the schedule could not be coordinated with the other resource-heavy NPU
jobs.

- Add a workflow_dispatch `runner` input, defaulting to the original
linux-aarch64-a3-16-sh-001, so a dispatch can target another equivalent
A3 16-card pool (linux-aarch64-a3-800i-16) without editing the file.
- Keep an inline fallback in runs-on so an empty input value still
resolves to a real label instead of leaving the job queued.
- Register linux-aarch64-a3-800i-16 in the actionlint self-hosted runner
list, so the label is checked if it is ever hardcoded again.
- Remove `schedule: - cron: '0 14 * * *'` and let the external scheduler
dispatch the workflow, matching the other NPU-heavy jobs. The
workflow_dispatch inputs and their handling are left unchanged.
- Move schedule_main2main.yaml to the "without a cron trigger" table in
the CI workflow trigger docs.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

### How was this patch tested?

involves

I
