added.subject: [Feature][Config] Relax A5 MegaMoe intermediate size check to operator's actual range (#19473)
added.body:
### What

Replace the hard-coded whitelist check for A5 MegaMoe
`intermediate_hidden`
(`{1024, 2048, 3072, 4096, 7168}`, with 6144 only allowed for MiniMax M3
/ Kimi K3)
with a range + alignment check matching the actual constraint of the A5
MegaMoe
operator (arch35 tiling): the post-activation intermediate width
(`moe_intermediate_size`) must be within **[256, 4096]** and **aligned
to 128**
(equivalent to the full GMM1 output width `hiddenDim` within [512, 8192]
aligned
to 256).

### Why

The previous whitelist rejected valid models whose
`moe_intermediate_size`
(e.g. 3072 → hiddenDim 6144) is fully supported by the operator but not
listed
in the whitelist, causing silent fallback:
`mega moe operator is not supported by current a5 config, for
intermediate_hidden size 6144 is not in [1024 2046 3072 4096 7168]`.

The operator-side tiling check accepts hiddenDim in [512, 8192] with 256
alignment, so the framework check should reflect the operator's real
constraint
instead of a per-model whitelist.

Note: A3 (arch22) only supports intermediate_hidden in [512, 3072]
aligned to
256; this check is A5-only and a follow-up TODO is noted in the code.

added.subject: [Feature][1/N] Add KDA RecoverSSM Triton operators (#20128)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Add the Ascend GLM KDA RecoverSSM Triton operators. Verification records
correction/key/gate data; after sampling, commit reconstructs the
accepted recurrent state and compacts convolution history. Each KDA page
needs one recurrent checkpoint instead of additional per-draft
checkpoints.

Support NPU graphs, with optimized verify, compact and commit kernels
for A3/A5. This is part 1/N split from #19133, containing the operators,
their tests and required operator documentation in one commit. Model,
worker, configuration and PD integration are left to the framework
follow-up.

References: original Kimi-K3 RecoverSSM
([vllm#51855](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51855)) and GLM
KDA integration
([vllm#61566](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61566)).

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No serving behavior or configuration is enabled by this part. The new
operator entry points are exercised directly by the single-operator
tests; framework callers and user-facing activation will be added
separately.

The historical integrated-model results below remain experimental:
generation may differ from ordinary MTP; tokenwise equivalence is not
guaranteed. Reduced KDA checkpoint storage does not imply an equivalent
reduction in total reserved KV memory.

### How was this patch tested?

The following operator validation is inherited from the earlier
integrated version in #19133. The exact extracted operator/test source
passed 144 A3 cases and 1280 output comparisons; current-source A5
full-suite validation remains pending after its validation sequence
stopped during the commit microbenchmark due to device OOM.

#### Triton operator validation (A3/A5)

1. **Functionality:** GLM KDA verification, accepted-state commit and
convolution compaction reduce draft checkpoint storage. Eager and NPU
graph execution are covered with H32/H64, K=V=128, BF16/FP16 activations
and FP32/BF16 states. Operator documentation and tests are included.
Grouped commit uses the configured window, with explicit Q1/Q2/Q4/Q6/Q8
path regressions.
2. **Accuracy:** Against independent FP64 references, each device passed
142 tests and 1260 output comparisons. Every output achieved a 100%
element-wise mixed-tolerance pass rate and satisfied its maximum
absolute-error limit. The largest errors across both devices were BF16
`3.2176e-03`, FP16 `2.2898e-05` and FP32 `4.1121e-07`. Copy-only results
and untouched regions matched exactly. For the same-algorithm stride
optimization, all 24 checkpoint comparisons had zero maximum absolute
difference.
3. **Performance:** Compared with the same-algorithm baseline
`b5326cd6b`, nine alternating graph-timing rounds used recorded strides,
B11/B12, L11/L12 and accepted lengths 1/3/6. Commit latency changes
ranged from `-5.30%` to `+5.39%` on A3 and `-1.49%` to `+3.62%` on A5;
both improvements and regressions are reported. Removing the
fixed-window restriction retained identical checkpoints in six Q6 A5
cases; grouped latency changed by `-0.52%` to `+0.21%` against
`b7ec33b35`.
4. **Safety:** Shape/dtype/stride, static-window and tile specialization
sources were reviewed. With MTP5/Q6, after warmup, all four active
kernels recorded zero JIT memory-cache misses during the full GSM8K run,
with no new or modified persistent compilation artifacts. **No
recompilation was observed in this dataset run.** Write boundaries and
untouched regions were checked; nonlinear operands have FP32 assertions,
and the context patch is installed only for GLM with RecoverSSM enabled.

added.subject: [Feature][KV Pool] Support Mooncake SSD prefetch on exist (#19472)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Adds optional Mooncake SSD-to-DRAM prefetch on exist queries. When
`enable_ssd_prefetch=true` in `mooncake.json`, `batch_is_exist` passes
`ExistOptions(prefetch_to_memory=True)`, so Mooncake promotes SSD-only
objects into DRAM during the cache probe, and a follow-up get is served
from DRAM instead of SSD. Feature design lives in the Mooncake PR
(kvcache-ai/Mooncake#4272); concept from kvcache-ai/Mooncake#2213.

- Parse `enable_ssd_prefetch`, `ssd_prefetch_cooldown_sec`, and
`ssd_prefetch_dedup_ttl_sec`; forward each throttle knob to
`store.setup()` only when explicitly set, so omitted fields keep
Mooncake defaults (5s backoff, 30s dedup TTL).
- Capability probes keep this safe on older Mooncake builds: without
`ExistOptions`, prefetch is disabled with a warning instead of failing
initialization.
- When a knob is forwarded, setup uses the config-dict overload; the
store then owns its TransferEngine instead of sharing the global one.
- Document the new `mooncake.json` fields in the kv-pool feature guide.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. New optional `mooncake.json` fields (`enable_ssd_prefetch`,
`ssd_prefetch_cooldown_sec`, `ssd_prefetch_dedup_ttl_sec`). Behavior
changes only when `enable_ssd_prefetch=true` and a compatible Mooncake
build is installed; everything is off by default.

### How was this patch tested?

Unit tests (148 pass):

    pytest -sv tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/test_backend.py

Covers config parsing (defaults / set / null), capability probes,
prefetch resolve logic, both setup paths (keyword vs config-dict and the
TransferEngine ownership that follows), and the `exists()` call path
with and without prefetch options.

End-to-end on Ascend A2 with the Mooncake PR head: TTFT A/B and
SSD-offload smoke, evidence in the Mooncake PR.

added.subject: [CI] Change os label for two A2 single-node test cases to a2b3-8 (#20105)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

**Background.** The A2 generation servers have a hardware-design
constraint on NUMA affinity: each NPU is only affine to the CPUs within
its own NUMA node. If CPUs are assigned across NUMA nodes arbitrarily,
cross-NUMA access is introduced, which goes against the hardware design
and causes performance degradation.

**Change.** Move the two A2 single-node performance test cases from
`linux-aarch64-a2b3-4` (4-card runners) to `linux-aarch64-a2b3-8`
(8-card runners):

- `qwen3-30b-a3b-bf16-a2-performance`
- `qwen3-30b-a3b-w8a8-a2-performance`

With this change, each 4-NPU test case is scheduled onto a whole 8-NPU
machine as the only workload, so the CPUs it uses stay within the
NUMA-affine scope and no cross-NUMA access is triggered.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This only changes which runner label the two A2 test cases are
scheduled on.

added.subject: [BugFix][310P] Fix KV cache memory accounting incorrectly charging ot… (#19984)
added.body:
…her processes' HBM usage

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #14274, #19726.

The non-RC branch of `NPUWorker310.determine_available_memory()` mixed
device-global memory with a per-process profiling delta, so HBM held by
other processes and the driver reserve were deducted from the KV cache
budget a second time. On a shared device this made the KV cache negative
and the second instance failed to start.

Now it only subtracts this instance's own profiled footprint, matching
upstream vLLM.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
No

End-to-end manual test on a 310P device:

Start two vLLM instances on the same NPU (two processes sharing one
device).

Check the Available KV cache memory log line and whether the second
instance starts successfully.

With this fix, both instances start successfully and report non-negative
KV cache memory; before the fix, the second instance reported a negative
value and failed to start. This confirms multiple vLLM instances can run
on the same NPU at the same time.

added.author: Yao Liu
added.subject: [Feature] Enable fused RMSNorm+cast capability for Atlas A2 (#19304)
added.body:
## Summary

Enable the existing fused `npu_rms_norm_cast` operator on Atlas A2 by
exposing
`HardwareCapability.RMS_NORM_CAST` in the A2 hardware profile.

The kernel already has `ascend910b` build artifacts
(`csrc/moe/rms_norm_cast`),
but the capability was A3-only. As a result, A2 used the fallback
`RMSNorm` + `.float()`, which runs two kernels and round-trips the
normalized
BF16 tensor through HBM.

DSV4.1 consumes the FP32 normalized hidden state as the MoE router input
(`DeepseekV41DecoderLayer.rms_norm_cast`), so this fallback runs once
per layer.

## Change

- `vllm_ascend/device/hardware_profile.py`: add `RMS_NORM_CAST` to the
A2
  capability set and update the capability comment.
- `tests/ut/device/test_hardware_profile.py`: update the expected A2
capability
  set.
- `tests/ut/device/test_device_op.py`: expect the fused operator on A2
when
  custom ops are enabled.

No kernel source changes.

## Validation

Hardware: Atlas 800 A2 / 910B4 (32 GB HBM), CANN 9.1.0, torch
2.10.0+cpu,
torch_npu 2.10.0.post4.

Microbenchmark, hidden=5120, BF16 (fused `npu_rms_norm_cast` vs
`npu_rms_norm(...).float()`):

| tokens | eager fused | eager fallback | ACL graph fused | ACL graph
fallback |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.045 ms | 0.088 ms | 0.0125 ms | 0.0123 ms |
| 256 | 0.048 ms | 0.091 ms | 0.0281 ms | 0.0324 ms |
| 4096 | 0.269 ms | 0.281 ms | 0.2795 ms | 0.3086 ms |

- Eager: ~1.9x at small T, ~1.05x at T=4096.
- ACL graph: T=1 is neutral (within noise); ~15% at T=256 and ~10% at
T=4096.
- The op is ACL-graph capturable.

Operator consistency:

- `pytest tests/ut/device/test_hardware_profile.py -q` -> 12 passed.
- `pytest
tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/test_rms_norm_cast.py
-q`
-> 8 passed on 910B4 (FP16/BF16, hidden=7168, T=1/16/128, including the
NPU
  graph test).
- The fused FP32 output matches `npu_rms_norm(...).float()` exactly; the
existing e2e test asserts `actual_fp32 == actual.float()` with
rtol=0/atol=0.

## Notes

- `npu_rms_norm_cast` requires `gamma` to have the same dtype as `x`;
the
model RMSNorm weight is BF16, so the A2 path is valid. FP32 gamma paths
must
  cast or keep the fallback.
- This PR only changes the capability gate; it does not touch the
kernel.
- The e2e coverage already exercises the fused op directly; this PR
makes the
  model path use it on A2.

## Validation after updating main (2026-10-26)

The branch was updated onto main `06aac4532`. The sampling
cleanup in #19393 removed `NPU_TOP_K_TOP_P`; this PR preserves that
removal
and adds only `RMS_NORM_CAST` to the A2 capability set and its test
expectation.

- The CI checkout's `git rebase BASE_SHA` command passed locally. A
forced
  replay of the commit also passed and produced the same file tree.
- Full `bash format.sh ci` passed.
- 17 CPU cases for hardware profiles and RMSNorm dispatch passed with
temporary
import isolation for the unavailable vLLM/CANN dependencies. The three
Python feature
  files are unchanged from that validation.
- The Dynamo test fails on the local PyTorch 2.7.0 runtime because it
cannot
trace `frozenset.__contains__`. The same failure was reproduced against
  unmodified main; this PR does not change that path.
- The earlier A2 operator results above predate this update. No kernel
code was
  changed and no new NPU run was performed.

## Test plan

- CI unit tests.
- A2 e2e `test_rms_norm_cast`.
- DSV4.1 op-level tests on A2 (full-model validation requires the
documented
  4-node A2 pool).

added.subject: [Doc] Correct 950PR/950DT Mooncake container mounts and permissions (#19656)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

The multi-node Mooncake tutorial's shared Docker command maps 16 A3
device nodes and `/dev/devmm_svm`, while the 950 section only adds a few
options. On an eight-device 950DT host, the missing device paths prevent
container startup. The partial driver mounts also omit
`driver/topo/950`, and the RoCE section lists a provider configuration
file without supplying its shared library.

Provide a complete 950PR/950DT Docker command with the dedicated image,
correct device nodes, complete driver mount and required options,
followed by concise notes and Host RoCE additions. Document the tested
explicit-device + `NET_ADMIN` alternative and the HRN5 provider library
requirement. Describe version-specific `route.conf` guidance, retain
optional `hiroce5` mounts, and describe the scope of the automatic UB
configuration check.

Incorporate Yuli-yx/vllm-ascend#1: clarify physical-NPU-to-RoCE-IP
mapping and configurable endpoint directories, prominently mark the
future `roce:host` shortcut as unsupported, and explain bundled Mooncake
and optional custom source builds. Addresses #19659.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Documentation only. No runtime code or defaults change.

### How was this patch tested?

- `git diff --check`: passed.
- `npx --yes markdownlint-cli@0.45.0
docs/source/tutorials/features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.md`:
passed with the repository configuration.
- Checked the complete 950 Docker command with `bash -n` after
substituting the documentation version macro: passed. The additional
Docker option snippets were also syntax-checked in a Docker command.
- Latest follow-up validation (2026-10-26): `bash format.sh ci` passed
all hooks except `gitleaks-offline-scan`, which failed because this
macOS host has neither `gitleaks` nor `wget`. Full-suite success is not
claimed.
- Parsed the two endpoint JSON blocks and checked all 18 Bash blocks
before the Mooncake installation section with `bash -n` after
substituting version macros and wrapping Docker option fragments:
passed.
- Local workspace docs-tool smoke: `cd vllm-ascend && uv run pytest -q
tests/ut/_tools/test_docs_codegen.py
tests/ut/_tools/test_doctest_helper.py` was blocked during shared
conftest initialization because the installed Transformers lacks
`Kimi_K25VisionConfig`. Re-running the standalone tool tests with `uv
run pytest -q --noconftest tests/ut/_tools/test_docs_codegen.py
tests/ut/_tools/test_doctest_helper.py` passed: **52 passed**. This
checks documentation tooling, not NPU behavior.

Manual hardware validation used Ascend950DT, day20261015 950DT images
with CANN 9.2.0, and two processes restricted to two idle physical
devices. Each process allocated a 1 MiB NPU tensor and used Mooncake
`TransferEngine.initialize(..., "P2PHANDSHAKE", "ascend", "")`,
`register_memory`, and `transfer_sync_write`. The receiver copied the
tensor to CPU and compared every byte with the deterministic source
pattern. Successful cases required return code 0, exact data equality,
and HIXL logs confirming `UB_D2D` or `ROCE`.

| Controlled change | Result |
| --- | --- |
| UB automatic configuration, no `route.conf` present vs. host file
mounted | Both transferred and verified correctly |
| RoCE full mounts + privileged | Passed |

added.subject: [BugFix][xlite] Fix xlite fetching wrong `cached_lens` from upstream during spec decode due to host-side optimistic metadata update (#19936)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR fixes `xlite`'s incorrect use of host-side `seq_lens` metadata
during speculative decoding, due the upstream optimistic host-side
metadata updates. More specifically, during speculative decoding, the
host-side metadata `seq_lens` assumes all draft tokens are accepted
(counting rejected tokens), while the true `seq_lens` metadata is
updated on device.

The `xlite` backend requires `cached_lens` and `query_lens`, and the
`caches_lens` is derived from `seq_lens - query_lens`, where `seq_lens`
comes from host. Thus, during speculative decoding, `xlite` might get
**incorrect** context lengths for certain sequences, causing accuracy
regressions.

This fix keeps the original compute without speculative decoding
untouched. When speculative decode is enabled, `cached_lens` is derived
from the `positions` of the first tokens of all requests, instead.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No, bug fix only.

### How was this patch tested?

*Note: the following tests were conducted using `xlite` at commit
[a44690ed7](https://atomgit.com/openeuler/GVirt/tree/a44690ed7b42e048f73955ce9dfa71642ad5508b)*.

We benchmarked model accuracies with `GLM-5.2-w8a8` using `aisbench`.
The
[batch_aisbench.py](https://atomgit.com/openeuler/GVirt/blob/master/xlite/tests/e2e/batch_aisbench.py)
script was used with 416 questions from the `ceval` dataset:

```bash
# on one Atlas A3; for `aclgraph`, the GMU was set to `0.90`
python batch_aisbench.py "/root/benchmark" \
--num-prompts 8 \
--model-dir "/mnt/sdb/models" \

-MRV2 \

--broadcast-xlite
```

added.subject: [Feature][2/N] Add GLM KDA RecoverSSM framework integration (#20131)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Add the GLM KDA RecoverSSM framework integration for Ascend Model Runner
V2, split from #19133 as part 2/N. Connect the model's compact record
caches, upstream request/commit metadata, NPU graph staging and
post-sampling commit lifecycle. Adapt Mooncake pull PD transfer and
account for the GLM cache pools.

The existing `--use-replayssm` option selects the GLM path after
validating speculative decoding, Mamba cache mode `none`, disabled
prefix caching/stochastic rounding, PP/PCP/DCP=1 and supported Mooncake
connectors. Other models and disabled configurations retain the upstream
selection behavior.

This framework directly uses `kda_recoverssm_verify` and
`KDARecoverSSMCommitContext` from [part 1/N,
#20128](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20128), now
merged into `main`. The operator implementation is inherited unchanged
from the base branch. RecoverSSM eager/graph four-card E2E cases are
enabled alongside the native path.

The context binding patch is limited to GLM workers with RecoverSSM
enabled; remove it when upstream exposes a backend context factory. The
configuration validator patch can be removed when upstream supports GLM
KDA selection. Both removal plans are recorded in the patch registry.

The platform and worker KV dtype patches are kept identical to the base
branch; the unrelated KV dtype registry and FP8 fallback compatibility
changes have been removed.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

Enable GLM KDA RecoverSSM with the existing `--use-replayssm` option
alongside speculative decoding. Requires Mamba cache mode `none`, prefix
caching and stochastic rounding disabled, and PP/PCP/DCP=1. Supported PD
connectors are `MooncakeConnectorV2` and `MooncakePullConnector`. Native
AscendC remains the default with the option disabled.

### How was this patch tested?

End-to-end validation combines the RecoverSSM Triton operators (part
1/N, #20128) with this framework integration. The results below were
recorded on the integrated implementation
`97023fefd7106fff42b480e6ed629979b35d7d9e` after fully removing the
unrelated KV dtype compatibility commit `d2e1c892b`, paired with vLLM
`544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542`.

Real-weight GSM8K accuracy check (2026-10-28): the same first 30 test
questions for each condition, 4-shot, greedy generation, seed 1024,
reasoning effort `low`, up to 8192 output tokens and 30 concurrent
clients. Both devices use ordinary BF16 KV, MTP5 and target/draft
`FULL_DECODE_ONLY` graphs. Weight quantization remains A3 W8A8 and A5
MXFP8. Maximum context is 16384, `max_num_seqs=12` and
`max_num_batched_tokens=4096`.

| Configuration | Recover off correct / total | Recover on correct /
total | Natural stops per condition |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A3 W8A8, BF16 KV, DP8/TP2 | 29/30 | 28/30 | 30/30 |
| A5 MXFP8, BF16 KV, DP8/TP1 | 29/30 | 29/30 | 30/30 |

All four groups completed without output truncation. A3 has one
additional incorrect answer with RecoverSSM enabled; A5 has the same
correct count. Worker records confirm the RecoverSSM flag, BF16 KV and
target/draft graph mode on all 16 A3 workers and all 8 A5 workers. An A5
startup attempt failed during HCCL initialization before requests; a
retry with unchanged parameters completed the test.

This 30-question check covers startup and accuracy; it does not
establish full-dataset accuracy equivalence or BF16 KV performance.

added.subject: [Performance][DSpark] Merge DeepSeek V4.1 context WKV projections and reuse RoPE lookups (#19550)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR optimizes the DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark context path in two areas:

1. **Merge context WKV projections**  
Replace the per-layer WKV projections with one
`MergedColumnParallelLinear`, then split the output by draft layer. This
combines multiple smaller WKV GEMMs over the same context states into
one larger GEMM, improving NPU utilization while preserving the
per-layer projections used by draft-token forward.

2. **Reuse RoPE lookups**  
Query the required RoPE tensors once and reuse them across all DSpark
context layers.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This is an internal performance optimization with no changes to
public APIs, configuration, or model semantics.

### How was this patch tested?

#### Unit tests

Unit tests cover:

- Loading each layer's WKV parameters into the corresponding merged
projection shard.
- Executing the merged WKV projection once and splitting outputs in
layer order.
- Reusing one RoPE lookup across context layers.
- Handling missing per-layer context slot mappings.

#### Microbenchmarks

The microbenchmarks isolate the two optimized parts of the context path.
They use NPU Graph execution, NPU event timing, ABBA ordering, and the
median of repeated measurements on one Ascend 910B rank.

##### WKV projection

Three independent per-layer W4A8 WKV projections are compared with one
merged W4A8 projection. The benchmark uses synthetic BF16 context hidden
states and real checkpoint WKV weights and scales. RMSNorm, RoPE, and
KV-cache insertion are excluded.

| Context tokens | Before (µs) | After (µs) | Latency reduction |
Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,024 | 297.27 | 290.99 | 2.1% | 1.02x |
| 16,384 | 1,449.48 | 884.85 | 39.0% | 1.64x |
| 32,768 | 2,943.09 | 1,716.87 | 41.7% | 1.71x |
| 50,000 | 4,416.16 | 2,600.06 | 41.1% | 1.70x |

##### RoPE lookup reuse

Both paths execute the same three rotary kernels. The baseline performs
one RoPE lookup per DSpark layer, while the optimized path performs one
filtered lookup and reuses the result across all three layers. WKV
projection, RMSNorm, and KV-cache insertion are excluded.

| Context tokens | Before (µs) | After (µs) | Latency reduction |
Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,024 | 329.17 | 299.84 | 8.9% | 1.10x |
| 16,384 | 1,610.26 | 610.71 | 62.1% | 2.64x |
| 32,768 | 2,931.14 | 1,089.04 | 62.8% | 2.69x |
| 50,000 | 4,352.15 | 1,592.35 | 63.4% | 2.73x |

#### Ascend 910B benchmark

Environment:

- Hardware: 8 × Ascend 910B
- Model: `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-w4a8-chiro`
- Quantization: W4A8
- Execution mode: Graph enabled
- Requests: 20
- Input length: 50,000 tokens
- Output length: 350 tokens
- Request rate: 0.3 requests/s
- Identical server and benchmark configurations for baseline and PR

Benchmark command:

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8080 \
  --backend openai-chat \
  --model /data/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-w4a8-chiro \
  --served-model-name illm \
  --tokenizer /data/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-w4a8-chiro \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el \
  --metric-percentiles 50,95,99 \
  --dataset-name prefix_repetition \
  --request-rate 0.3 \
  --num-prompts 20 \
  --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --ignore-eos \
  --temperature 0 \
  --seed 8080 \
  --prefix-repetition-prefix-len 45000 \
  --prefix-repetition-suffix-len 5000 \
  --prefix-repetition-output-len 350 \
  --prefix-repetition-num-prefixes 1
```

Results:

| Metric | Baseline | PR | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Successful requests | 20 | 20 | No failures |
| Benchmark duration | 74.22 s | 73.59 s | -0.85% |
| Output throughput | 94.31 tok/s | 95.12 tok/s | +0.86% |
| Total token throughput | 13,575.06 tok/s | 13,692.49 tok/s | +0.87% |
| Mean TTFT | 2,182.98 ms | 2,152.01 ms | -1.42% |
| Median TTFT | 1,248.98 ms | 1,229.78 ms | -1.54% |
| P95 TTFT | 6,352.30 ms | 6,339.67 ms | -0.20% |
| P99 TTFT | 7,283.83 ms | 7,270.61 ms | -0.18% |
| Mean TPOT | 22.55 ms | 22.07 ms | -2.13% |
| Median TPOT | 23.08 ms | 22.31 ms | -3.34% |
| Mean E2EL | 10,054.64 ms | 9,852.71 ms | -2.01% |
| Median E2EL | 9,640.17 ms | 9,486.97 ms | -1.59% |
| DSpark acceptance rate | 29.39% | 30.44% | +1.05 pp |
| DSpark acceptance length | 2.47 | 2.52 | +0.05 |

The PR improves token throughput and reduces TTFT, TPOT, and end-to-end
latency without regressing DSpark acceptance metrics.

benchmark results are included above.

added.author: liben
added.subject: [BugFix][Attention] Preserve standalone MLA output gates (#20104)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Preserve the standalone MLA output gate when `_mla_preprocess` returns
no fused gate.

With the standalone `g_proj` layout, `AscendMLAImpl.forward` computes
the gate before preprocessing. Since #19694, both the plain and strided
preprocessing paths unpack the third return value into the same
variable. That return value is `None` for the plain QKV-A layout, so it
overwrites the standalone gate and silently skips `attention_output *
sigmoid(gate)` before `o_proj`.

Keep the preprocessing result in a separate variable and replace the
existing gate only when preprocessing produces a tensor. This preserves
standalone gating, fused gating, and ungated/prolog behavior. The
observed affected model is Kimi-K3 with a standalone gate on vLLM
v0.32.0; the fix follows the backend contract without model-specific
conditions. Any MLA consumer with the same standalone-gate contract can
be affected; a fused gate returned as a tensor, or a model without an
output gate, does not hit this overwrite bug.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Fixes incorrect Kimi-K3 generation when the MLA output gate is
projected by a standalone `g_proj`. No launch or configuration changes
are required.

### How was this patch tested?

- Added `tests/ut/attention/test_mla_output_gate.py`, exercising the
actual `AscendMLAImpl.forward` with CPU tensors and mocked device/kernel
boundaries. It covers prefill/decode, plain/strided/prolog
preprocessing, and standalone/fused/ungated layouts: **16 passed, 2
skipped** (fused+prolog is unsupported). The unpatched forward fails all
four standalone plain/strided prefill/decode cases.
- The new tests plus the existing `tests/ut/attention/test_mla_v1.py`
suite: **229 passed, 3 skipped**. The image's normal custom-op bootstrap
and a patched-module loader were used; this is focused unit coverage,
not a full repository test run.
- Actual Ascend A3 serving: Kimi-K3, DP4/TP16/EP64, DSpark7, sequence
parallelism and `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` graphs enabled. The persistent source
fix was deployed and the service restarted before evaluation. GPQA
Diamond, all **198** questions, maximum output **65,536** tokens, client
concurrency **64**, temperature **0**, seed **0**, zero-shot, thinking
enabled: **180/198 (90.91%)**, zero request errors. Four responses
reached the output cap without a parsed answer and count as incorrect.
This is post-fix quality evidence; no matched full-budget unpatched or
v0.30 full-model baseline is claimed.
- Hardware/unit validation used Ascend base
`bd42eea01d8312c4df469fabaed45f77a12df4d3` and vLLM v0.32.0
`5df63a7203cdb9328d824a27b682e77c7b9928be`. The branch is based on
community main `a1fcee98601b8da223d20afc46b7ba3c6c7da393`; the MLA
implementation and existing MLA test file are unchanged between those
Ascend bases.
- Ruff, formatting, codespell, typos, clang-format, Markdown lint,
secret scan, shell checks and repository Python policy checks passed.
Full `bash format.sh ci` was attempted, but its actionlint environment
provisioning stalled and was stopped. The same command passed with only
`actionlint` skipped; a separate Homebrew actionlint 1.7.12 run passed
for all 54 tracked workflow files with the same exclusions and
ShellCheck options (the pre-commit hook pins 1.7.11).
- `git diff --check` passed. No latency/throughput comparison or
full-model validation for other models is claimed; upstream CI remains
pending.

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] Boundary / edge-case coverage: standalone, fused and absent gate;
both prefill/decode and plain/strided/prolog paths.
- [x] Regression test: standalone cases fail without the fix.
- [ ] Error / failure path coverage: this change does not add an
exception or validation path.
- [x] Meaningful & reliable tests: assertions compare numerical outputs
against an independent sigmoid-gating expression.
- [ ] Performance impact: no performance improvement claimed; no matched
serving-performance comparison run.

added.subject: [Feature][GLM-5.3-Flash] Enable torch.compile for GLM-5.3-Flash backbone and MTP (#19076)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable `torch.compile` for the GLM-5.3-Flash text backbone and MTP draft
model.

- Keep KDA state updates and Triton-based normalization behind custom-op
boundaries so serialized FX/AOT artifacts remain reusable across
processes.
- Register KDA as a PIECEWISE splitting op and normalize into a
caller-owned output buffer. This prevents capture of the metadata-free
profiling path and stale-output reads during graph replay.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Compilation settings now take effect for the backbone and MTP, and
PIECEWISE prefill produces correct outputs for the previously failing
requests.

Draft compilation requires `"enforce_eager": false` in the speculative
config. Explicit eager mode remains supported.

### How was this patch tested?

- **CPU:** 95 related tests passed, covering runtime metadata, stable
output buffers, and FULL graph compatibility.
- **A3:** W8A8, V1, MTP5, P DP2/TP8 + D DP8/TP2, PIECEWISE prefill and
FULL decode. Cold and hot compilation-cache runs each passed 32
concurrent PD requests across all eight D instances.
- **A3 runtime:** CANN 9.2.0, PyTorch 2.10.0, torch-npu 2.10.0.post7,
vLLM 0.31.0 (`db9527a4`).
- **950DT:** TP8 + EP MXFP8 validation with V1, FULL_DECODE_ONLY and
three-token compiled MTP.
- **AIME2026:** Default-sampling evaluation is running; final accuracy
is pending.

added.subject: [Bugfix] Fix KV cache memory accounting for Ascend multi-allocation layouts (#20203)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?
This PR fixes a KV cache initialization failure when serving DeepSeek
V4.1 on Ascend, caused by
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53558.
When https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/18359 merged, this
patch can be removed.

The newer builder-based KV cache planner in vLLM uses`
KVCacheConfigBuilder._get_pool_bytes_per_block() `to determine the
memory consumption per KV cache block. When this method returns None,
vLLM falls back to probing a one-block placement and expects all
device-backed KV cache tensors to have the same backing allocation size.
However, Ascend's specialized KV cache layouts (including DSV4.1) can
involve multiple backing allocations with different sizes.

For DSV4.1, this causes the engine to fail during KV cache
initialization:

```
ValueError: KV cache tensors must share one device
backing allocation, but got sizes [131072, 147712].
Override KVCacheConfigBuilder._get_pool_bytes_per_block()
for placements with several device allocations.
```

Ascend already provides specialized per-block memory accounting through
_`ascend_pool_bytes_per_block()`, but the newer builder-based planner
does not use this existing override because it calls a different hook.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
N/A

added.subject: [Feature] Add MiniMax-M3 DSpark draft FlashAttn support on A5 (#19537)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable the original six-layer `Qwen3DSparkModel` DSpark draft for
MiniMax-M3 on Ascend A5 / Model Runner V2.

- Select CANN FlashAttn only for the `dspark_head` draft, including
dense and sliding-window attention. Support eager execution and full
draft graph replay using persistent device metadata.
- Keep the target model's existing dense / sparse attention backends,
graph replay and prefill metadata. Skip the runner's speculative
CPU-length copy/wait only for the supported M3 DSpark FlashAttn path;
target-backend synchronization remains in place.
- Supply target auxiliary hidden states to DSpark and fix mixed FP8
target / BF16 draft KV-page sizing and indexer kernel-page views.
Preserve the existing 64/128-token kernel pages.

All runtime changes are in vllm-ascend. Upstream vLLM is unchanged.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

N/A

### How was this patch tested?

#### NVIDIA MT-Bench acceptance alignment (2026-10-26)

Tested PR commit `f74ed6f3c254e071d54b4defab1a6b349cc1a0e0` with
upstream vLLM `a98247ab4db686ee03c66d5feb3c761e52a2f8ab`, without
upstream source changes.

- Reused the unmodified [NVIDIA SpecDec
benchmark](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer/tree/main/examples/specdec_bench)
native AsyncLLM wrapper, conversation loop and MT-Bench aggregation,
with Ascend engine-option overrides. All 80 questions / 160 turns
completed, with generated first-turn history retained for the second
turn.
- Generation: concurrency 1, K=8, greedy draft, temperature=0, top_p=1,
top_k=0, max output 4096 tokens per turn, normal EOS stopping, seed
1024. Adaptive verification and prefix caching disabled.
- Runtime: 8 Ascend A5 NPUs, Model Runner V2, TP4 / DP2 / EP8, KV block
size 128, max model length 16384, max batched tokens 8192, max sequences
8. `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` target graphs and full DSpark draft graph replay
enabled; CANN FlashAttn is selected only for the draft.
- Used the existing MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 target with BF16 activations and
`auto` / BF16 KV, and the original six-layer BF16 Qwen3DSparkModel draft
with BF16 KV. The draft safetensors SHA256 matches NVIDIA's published
checkpoint:
`0fdbf12b9f7d3158d445a10a0738dbeca5d5f0208fa89b37ef520725da1abcd7`.

The [NVIDIA model
card](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/MiniMax-M3-DSpark#evaluation) calls
tokens returned per decoding step “acceptance rate.” The A5 column uses
the public benchmark's `MTBench.process_final` aggregation: combine both
turns for each question, then average the 80 question-level lengths.

| Category | NVIDIA published AL (tokens/step) | A5 measured AL
(tokens/step) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Overall | 3.98 | **4.0706** |
| writing | 3.22 | 3.3690 |
| roleplay | 2.56 | 2.6725 |
| reasoning | 3.93 | 4.0107 |
| math | 5.78 | 5.7754 |
| coding | 5.08 | 5.3559 |
| extraction | 5.45 | 5.3367 |
| stem | 3.21 | 3.3958 |
| humanities | 2.63 | 2.6485 |

Overall AL is **+2.28%** relative to the published MT-Bench value.

Actual vLLM counters, reported separately from the question-average
metric:

| Metric | A5 measured |
|---|---:|
| Draft steps | 55,089 |
| Proposed draft tokens | 440,712 |
| Accepted draft tokens | 147,138 |
| Draft-token acceptance fraction (`accepted / proposed`) | **33.3864%**
|
| Global mean acceptance length (`1 + accepted / draft_steps`) |
**3.6709 tokens/step** |

The global mean weights decoding steps differently from the
question-average AL above. NVIDIA does not publish the corresponding
draft-token acceptance percentage, so no official percentage is inferred
from 3.98.

Validation: all eight categories contain ten questions; per-question AL
and summed per-turn counters match the final results; 11 local alignment
checks passed. Twelve of 160 turns reached the 4096-token output limit.
The longest input was 4552 tokens, within the 16384-token context limit.

The dataset, conversation handling and metric aggregation are aligned to
the public benchmark. The existing MXFP8 target and A5 hardware differ
from NVIDIA's original target / B300 setup, and the model card does not
publish the complete original evaluation command; these results are not
a bit-for-bit reproduction.

#### Full GSM8K results

| Metric | FIA control with compatibility fixes | This PR: draft FA |
|---|---:|---:|
| Requests | 1319 | 1319 |
| Conservative accuracy (%) | 95.5269 | 95.2995 |
| Raw AISBench accuracy (%) | 95.6027 | 95.2995 |
| Output throughput (token/s) | 786.1883 | 894.5911 |
| Request throughput (req/s) | 2.5968 | 3.2157 |
| Duration (s) | 507.9420 | 410.1751 |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 11303.8 | 9380.2 |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 38.7 | 37.4 |
| Mean E2E latency (ms) | 22473.8 | 19713.7 |
| Acceptance rate (%) | 58.5263 | 57.6747 |
| Mean acceptance length | 5.6821 | 5.6140 |
| Generated tokens | 399338 | 366939 |
| Normal EOS / token-limit cutoffs | 1317 / 2 | 1319 / 0 |

#### Comparison summary

Relative to the runnable FIA control, draft FA changes output-token
throughput by **+13.79%**, request throughput by **+23.83%**, mean TTFT
by **-17.02%** and mean TPOT by **-3.36%**. Conservative accuracy
changes by **-0.2274 percentage points** and acceptance rate by
**-0.8515 percentage points**. Both runs include all 1319 questions and
all cutoff work in the timed measurements; the token totals and finish
reasons above must be considered alongside the speed comparison.

added.subject: [Doc][Misc] DeepSeek-V4-Flash: serve the MTP checkpoint for DSpark and fix the A2 image block (#20161)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes two documentation defects in
`docs/source/tutorials/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash.md` that make the A2
deployment path unusable when the tutorial is followed literally.

**1. The A2 DSpark tab served a checkpoint that is not in the weight
list (Section 5.1)**

The "A2 series with dspark" tab serves
`UploadWeight/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark-w4a8-test`, which appears nowhere
in 3.1 Model Weight. A reader has no way to know where it comes from,
and when the path resolves to an empty directory `vllm serve` fails at
`ModelConfig` validation:

```
Value error, Invalid repository ID or local directory specified:
'/root/.cache/modelscope/hub/models/UploadWeight/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark-w4a8-test'
```

The standard `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-w8a8-mtp` checkpoint already ships the
draft weights and is what every other DSpark example in this document
serves (Sections 5.1 A2/A3 and 5.2). This PR switches the A2 DSpark tab
to that checkpoint, so the weight in the command always matches a row in
the weight table.

**2. The A2 tab in 4.1 exported `IMAGE` twice**

```bash
# deepseek-v4-flash uses the following image
export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0rc2

# deepseek-v4-flash-dspark uses the following image
export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:nightly-main
```

Both lines are in the same block and both execute, so the DSpark image
silently overrode the standard one. A reader who copied the block and
deployed the standard checkpoint ended up running the wrong image. This
PR keeps a single `export IMAGE` and binds the tag through the same
`vllm_ascend_version` variable the 950DT and A3 tabs in this section
already use, so the copied script resolves without an unrendered
template placeholder and all three tabs stay on one version token.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Documentation only. No code, API or behaviour change.

The A2 tab now shows one image variable per block instead of two, and
the A2 DSpark deployment example serves a checkpoint listed in Section
3.1. The 950DT and A3 tabs are untouched. No other tutorial is affected.

### How was this patch tested?

Documentation-only change; no test added.

Verified manually:

- Checked that the A2 tab now uses the same `vllm_ascend_version` token
as the 950DT (`-a5`) and A3 (`-a3`) tabs in the same section, so all
three resolve to one version at build time.
- Confirmed `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-w8a8-mtp` is published on ModelScope and
its `config.json` carries `num_nextn_predict_layers: 1`, the draft-layer
layout the other DSpark examples in this document already pair with
`--speculative-config '{"method":"dspark",...}'`.
- Rendered the modified page with the repository's mkdocs setup and
checked that the A2 code block resolves and that the
`#51-single-node-online-deployment` anchor still works.
- `markdownlint` per `.markdownlint.json` (MD013 disabled) passes.

added.subject: [BugFix] Preserve duplicate encoder inputs in recompute scheduling (#19573)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

With the main-pinned vLLM API, a multimodal request can terminate
`RecomputeScheduler.schedule()` with `ValueError: too many values to
unpack (expected 4)`. `_try_schedule_encoder_inputs` returns a fifth
value, `duplicate_encoder_inputs`, while both waiting and running paths
still unpack four values.

Consume the duplicate-input list in both paths and use the inherited
`_allocate_encoder_inputs` helper to preserve computed, external and
duplicate encoder-cache references. Add regressions using the real
upstream API and `ScoreEncoderCacheManager`, covering waiting requests
with shared encoder identifiers and requests that enter the running
queue.

Related to #19103. That PR's `normalize_encoder_schedule_result`
currently returns `result[:4]` against main. This focused patch retains
the fifth value and its allocation semantics; it is intended as concrete
code and regression evidence for integrating the fixes, rather than
replacing that broader compatibility work.

**Draft scope:** this patch targets vLLM main pinned at `a98247ab4`,
which has the five-value return contract and native allocation helper.
Compatibility with the 0.31.0 release four-value API is not validated
here and needs to be reconciled with #19103 before merge. No claim that
truncating the fifth value reproduces all upstream cache-reference
behavior.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Multimodal requests using the recompute scheduler can proceed under the
main-pinned API, retaining duplicate encoder-cache tracking. No new
options or performance changes.

### How was this patch tested?

- The two new regression cases reproduced the original `expected 4`
failure against unmodified code.
- With the original compatibility fix, 48 related
recompute/encoder-cache/dyntra/short-request tests passed in the
pinned-main environment. That historical test stack also included the
independent async-zeroing fix; it is not included in this PR.
- Live recovery checks passed for a text arithmetic request and an
official AI2D semantic sample. These are functional smoke checks, not
full model-quality scores.
- The initial submission ported the original fix onto Ascend main
`db8836752`. The review revision removes the duplicate type annotation
and strengthens waiting/running reference and release tests; its 44
related tests passed. The earlier 48-test compatibility stack
additionally included four independent async-zeroing cases, tracked
separately in #19579.
- `bash format.sh ci` and `git diff --check` passed. Full model
benchmarks and quality suites were not rerun for this submission.
Release-API compatibility remains an explicit Draft limitation.

#### Testing checklist

- [x] Boundary / edge-case coverage: waiting and running requests,
duplicate identifiers and cache references.
- [x] Regression test: two cases fail on the old four-value unpack.
- [x] Meaningful & reliable tests: real base scheduler API and
encoder-cache manager invariants.

### Review closeout

Fixed the CI mypy `no-redef` error by removing the second same-function
type annotation. Split waiting and running duplicate-reference
regressions; running now schedules a new encoder and a duplicate in the
same step, checks native allocator arguments `[1]`/`[2]`, and verifies
request release/cache invariants. All 44 related tests passed on the
pinned-main runtime. The review bot’s duplicate-only result is not
produced by this upstream API: duplicate IDs are recorded only alongside
an already scheduled compute/external input; cache hits register their
references directly. Upstream uses the same allocation guard, which is
retained. Replies include this source rationale.

change, as requested by the contributor.

added.subject: [BugFix] Support PCP/DCP preempt offload with local block spans (#19578)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable preempt offload for supported MRV2 PCP/DCP configurations and
correctly map tokens to DCP-sharded KV blocks. Existing code rejects
both DCP>1 and PCP>1, and uses raw group block sizes for transfer ranges
even when DCP increases the token span.

- Use `resolve_dcp_kv_block_size` for store/restore ranges, including
partial last blocks and speculative-tail exclusion.
- Remove the PCP=1 restriction. Each worker transfers its own local
cache; PCP expands the workers rather than the local cache's token span.
- Construct the CPU KV coordinator with `pcp_world_size=1`, matching
Ascend's coordinator contract, while preserving the actual DCP size.
- Preserve the full per-engine worker count (`TP × PP × PCP`) for store
completion. A single PCP slice must not mark a transfer complete.

No worker transport, circular-cache or physical buffer implementation is
changed. The repository's existing MRV2/platform constraints still
determine supported configurations. Related to #18090 and tracking
#19663; this remains a focused alternative implementation and regression
suite for vendor/community coordination.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Enables preempt offload for supported MRV2 PCP/DCP configurations and
corrects DCP block-span mapping. No new option or performance claim.

### How was this patch tested?

Rebased onto main `99a8e0a0e` on 2026-10-29. The net diff is limited to
the offload manager and its tests; redundant CI test rename commits are
dropped.

```bash
TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 pytest -q tests/ut/kv_offload/test_preempt_offload_connector.py
# 80 passed
bash format.sh ci
# passed
git diff --check
# passed
```

Fresh zero-NPU CPU tests use the real scheduler, CPU coordinator and
block pool with verified vLLM main `544f182d`. Twelve new cases cover
PCP1/2/4, DCP1/2/16, TP and PP2 combinations, plus sharded and
replicated KV groups. They verify CPU coordinator PCP=1/DCP=actual,
partial-block store/restore without multiplying the span by PCP,
speculative-tail exclusion, and waiting for completion from all PCP
workers. Host-capacity probing and physical GPU transfers are mocked.

RED/GREEN control: the new twelve-case suite against the previous
PCP-restricted manager yields ten expected PCP>1 failures and two
passing PCP1 controls; the candidate passes all eighty tests. Existing
DCP, sliding-window, Mamba, transfer-metadata and cleanup regressions
remain covered.

No NPU/model service or physical cross-worker PCP transfer E2E was run
for this change. The CPU results establish scheduler mapping and
aggregation behavior; physical integration remains a device-validation
boundary. Community CI must validate both supported release and main
lanes for the new head.

added.author: yFeng-dev
added.subject: [BugFix][PD] Handle TP-replicated Mamba state in Mooncake V2 (#19974)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Mooncake V2 currently treats every `MambaSpec` state as sharded across
TP/PCP workers. That is incorrect for a state marked
`tp_replicated=True`, such as PLE convolution state: each worker owns
the complete state. With unequal TP the sharded path can reject the
producer rank or attempt an unsupported SHORT_CONV split; with equal TP
it unnecessarily requires matching producer/consumer ranks.

Honor the existing `tp_replicated` contract when choosing a producer and
constructing transfer addresses:

- Put all producer PCP/TP workers in one replica group so the existing
selection logic chooses one complete copy.
- Copy the complete logical state after checking that local/remote
shapes and byte lengths agree. Preserve each side's physical block
stride.
- Keep existing rank, integer-ratio, and slicing rules for
non-replicated GDN/Mamba state. Missing `tp_replicated` attributes
retain the old behavior through `getattr(..., False)`.

This is a standalone fix based on upstream `main` at
`c5cf3a6b14a4281a79e12f781b332ff8c09088b7`. A model must supply a spec
with `tp_replicated=True` to opt into the replicated-state path; the
verified vLLM main revision already provides this field.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Mooncake V2 can transfer replicated Mamba/PLE state as a complete
copy across different TP ranks and sizes instead of treating it as a
head shard. No new flags, environment variables, model code, cache
layout changes, or monkey patches are introduced. This does not add
general model support or change non-replicated state partitioning.

### How was this patch tested?

Validation uses an isolated checkout of the upstream base plus only this
fix and its tests, with the repository's verified vLLM main
`544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542`. These are CPU unit tests in
the existing Ascend container; compiled extensions were reused for
imports and no model services were restarted.

- Before the fix: all **20 new regression cases failed**, 153 existing
cases deselected.
- After the fix: the complete affected module passed, **173 passed**, 14
warnings.

```bash
# Run new regressions against the original pull_worker.py, then restore the fix.
python -m pytest tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2/test_pull_worker.py \
  -k 'replicated_mamba_selects or replicated_short_conv_copies' -q --disable-warnings

# Run the complete affected module with the fix.
python -m pytest tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2/test_pull_worker.py \
  -q --disable-warnings
```

New cases cover equal TP, both directions of unequal TP, non-integral TP
ratios for replicated state, producer PCP replication, different
source/destination ranks, logical lengths smaller than physical strides,
and rejection of shape/length mismatches. Existing tests cover
non-replicated state behavior.

Earlier integrated Ascend 910C/A3 testing exercised the same
replicated-state logic with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-w8a8, MRV2, MTP3, block
size 1536, P TP8 → D TP8 and P TP8 → D TP4/DP2. Each topology completed
64 concurrent proxy requests with no repeated-exclamation outputs or
corrupted-request metric increments. That deployment also included
separate model/layout/NHD fixes; this is supporting integration
evidence, not an end-to-end result for upstream main plus this
standalone patch alone, nor a full GSM8K accuracy claim.

Repository-pinned Ruff check/format and `git diff --check` pass. `bash
format.sh ci` was attempted but stopped during markdownlint dependency
installation with npm `SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN`; full CI remains
pending.

### Checklist

- [x] Boundary / edge-case coverage: equal/unequal TP and PCP replica
selection.
- [x] Regression tests fail against the original production code.
- [x] Error paths cover shape and logical-length mismatches.
- [x] Tests assert selected transfer groups, byte addresses, and copied
lengths.
- [ ] Full upstream CI and comparative performance benchmarking.

added.author: freyfwt
added.subject: [Performance][EPLB] Wait for consumed event before HIXL buffer reuse (#19342)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

HIXL READs currently synchronize the entire EPLB stream before reusing
the shared expert buffer. For subsequent changed layers, the required
dependency is the previous foreground consumption of that buffer.

Pass the recorded consumption event from the existing Ascend async
worker to its HIXL communicator, then synchronize that event on the host
before submitting private-stream READs. Capture it after
`CpuGpuEvent.wait()` observes the foreground acknowledgement, since
`record()` replaces the underlying device event. Scope the dependency to
one model and rearrangement cycle, clear it after each layer even on
failure, and retain the stream fallback for the first changed layer and
other callers. Publication synchronization, transfer completion and
cross-rank failure confirmation are preserved.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API or configuration changes. This narrows an internal
synchronization boundary. No end-to-end throughput or latency
improvement is claimed.

### How was this patch tested?

Latest rebase validation at `eda265bbb`, using the pinned vLLM commit
`544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542`:

- `bash format.sh ci`: passed.
- Full `tools/mypy.sh 1` for Python 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12: passed across
`vllm_ascend`, `examples` and `tests` in a Linux lint environment.
- CPU/mock regression tests: **68 passed** across
`tests/ut/distributed/eplb/test_hixl_communicator.py` and
`tests/ut/patch/platform/test_patch_eplb.py`. Covers event replacement,
model/cycle isolation, repeated layer execution, empty READ batches,
fallback synchronization and failure cleanup.
- Real Ascend A5 two-device HIXL regression: **4 passed, 0 skipped**,
with both the ctypes backend and official Python binding. Tests the
stream fallback and consumed-event dependency using real device events,
delayed foreground consumption, HIXL READs and independent checks of
both buffer payloads. The event case also rejects full-stream
synchronization. The standard shared E2E conftest was used successfully.

```bash
VLLM_VERSION=0.32.1.dev0 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
  python -m pytest -sv -rs \
  tests/e2e/pull_request/two_card/test_hixl_eplb_registration.py::test_async_read_waits_for_previous_layer_buffer_consumption
```

The documented `VLLM_VERSION` override selects main compatibility paths
for the pinned source checkout. The real NPU run used CANN 9.2.0,
PyTorch 2.10.0 and torch_npu 2.10.0.post7.dev20261020. This validates
the dependency and buffer lifetime.

An additional exploratory full-model A5 comparison used exact parent
`c4090d8ef9854cd788cbcbdb1e95b961f3adc7ad` versus `eda265bbb` in the
same runtime: BF16 Qwen3-30B-A3B, TP2/DP2/EP4, zero redundant experts,
asynchronous STAIR/HIXL, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graphs, prefix caching
disabled, and eight prompts generating 512 tokens each. After observing
a committed real migration, three timed samples each generated 4096
output tokens.

| Source | Sample throughput (output tokens/s) | Aggregate throughput |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parent | 906.38, 910.34, 911.25 | 909.32 |
| PR head | 898.25, 908.12, 897.19 | 901.16 |

This single sequential pair measured about -0.90% aggregate throughput
and does not establish a statistically meaningful improvement or
regression. Later migration cycles differed in transfer work, so their
phase timings are not direct performance comparisons. The parent model
diagnostic passed. The head diagnostic completed all timed samples but
failed its final existing answer-prefix assertion: the last completion
began `called January` rather than `January`. That response answers the
question correctly, but the assertion remains failed; it was not
weakened or removed. The complete head model run is not reported as
passing. Repeated performance sampling and assessment of this
model/oracle boundary remain pending.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**
- [x] **Regression test**
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**
- [ ] **Performance impact**: narrower synchronization is asserted; a
matched model pilot is recorded above, with repeatability and
model/oracle acceptance still pending.

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542

added.subject: [Refactor][Triton] triton warmup jit (#19976)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?
Migrates vllm-ascend's Triton kernel warmup from five hand-written
per-op warmup scripts to upstream vLLM's declarative JIT warmup
framework (VllmTritonJitKernel + JitWarmupRegistry), so key-enumeration
knowledge lives next to each kernel and compilation reuses the upstream
parallel path.

AscendTritonJitKernel base class: drops upstream's is_cuda() gate to
enable parallel compile on NPU (reuses
VLLM_TRITON_JIT_WARMUP_NUM_THREADS); also the isinstance criterion for
pruning the CUDA-only registrations the upstream base RejectionSampler
leaves on NPU.
Colocated wrappers in 8 op files (@triton.jit bodies untouched),
registered at natural construction sites: fused Q-RMS in the DSA builder
__init__, 2 indexer kernels in DeepseekV41Indexer, v1 sampling stack via
register_v1_sampling_warmup(); DSpark is late-registered from
kernel_warmup because its key depends on the runtime block-table width.
Restores registry windows lost to NPU runner overrides (load_model /
initialize_kv_cache / may_reinitialize_input_batch / v1 sampling stack)
and adds MRv2 support via a window around super().initialize_kv_cache().
kernel_warmup.py orchestrates gates, DSpark late registration,
non-Ascend pruning, an empty-registry WARNING, then upstream
registry.warmup() (parallel/serial split). Deletes the 5 warmup files +
the early warmup thread; enable_early_kernel_warmup remains as a
deprecated no-op for JSON compatibility (extra="forbid").
Measured: full 42-key compile 59.8s serial → 9.4s @ 8 threads; all
compilation happens before ACL graph capture — no runtime JIT.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
- ascend_warmup_config.enable_early_kernel_warmup is now a deprecated
no-op; Triton warmup is unified under upstream enable_jit_warmup.
- Startup logs: "Early kernel warmup ..." lines → JIT kernel warmup
starting/finished in X.XXs.
- No new knobs; parallelism via upstream
VLLM_TRITON_JIT_WARMUP_NUM_THREADS (default 4).

### How was this patch tested?
- UT: 20 tests in tests/ut/model_executor/warmup/ (window semantics,
key-space golden sets, orchestration, gates) + v1/v2 worker test updates
— all green.
- NPU compile pass: all 42 keys across every wrapper compiled on real
NPU — 59.8s serial vs 9.4s @ 8 threads (CANN concurrent-compile safe).
- E2E: DSV4-Flash (w8a8, TP4×DP4, DSpark, v2 runner) on 16 NPUs, cold
Triton cache — every rank compiled exactly the 5 capture keys (rms
block_m {1,2,4,8,16}) in 3.65s before capture; warm re-run 0.02s; zero
empty-registry warnings.
- pre-commit (ruff, codespell, typos) clean.

How to onboard a new Triton kernel (contributor guide)
Step 1 — wrapper colocated with the kernel (upstream convention): add an
AscendTritonJitKernel subclass + module singleton in the kernel's own
ops/triton/*.py, with a frozen CompileKey, dispatch(),
get_warmup_keys(), warmup_inputs(), and a @kernel_launcher __call__.
Templates: rms_norm.py (minimal), reject_sample.py (multi-dimension
keys).

Step 2 — register where the kernel's owner is constructed (windows
already exist; do not open new ones):

| Owner constructed at | Register in | Collected by | Upstream precedent
|
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| model / layer __init__ | the same __init__ | load_model window |
sparse_attn_indexer.py, gate_linear.py |
| attention metadata builder __init__ | builder __init__ |
initialize_kv_cache window | mla_attention.py, deepseek_v4/attention.py
|
| v1 sampling stack | register_v1_sampling_warmup() | v1 runner __init__
window | register_top_k_top_p_warmups() |
---

Exception — keys depending on runtime-only values (e.g. block-table
width): register late in kernel_warmup.py (see
_register_dspark_swa_indices_warmup, which opens its own window). Open a
new window only if no existing window covers the construction path; in
methods unit tests call on partially-built runners, use the defensive
getattr(...) + nullcontext() form (see _initialize_kv_cache_upstream).

Free behaviors: out-of-window registration is a no-op; HAS_TRITON /
enable_jit_warmup gates; parallel compile (autotune kernels fall back to
serial automatically); non-Ascend registrations pruned; empty registry
triggers a WARNING.

Step 3 — tests: add
tests/ut/model_executor/warmup/test_jit_warmup_<op>.py with two cases —
a key-space golden set, and window semantics (nothing registers outside
a window).

I

test

and are

### What this PR does / why we need it?

MiniMax MXFP8 MoE dispatch must use the model's ceil-scale policy. The
default fused MC2 mode 4 and init-routing quantizers do not apply that
policy on these paths.

- Quantize MXFP8 activations explicitly for MC2 and AllGather routing
when the model selects scale algorithm 1.
- Transport or reorder the FP8 activations and E8M0 scales together,
then reuse the returned scales for the first expert GEMM.
- Avoid the extra default lossy MC2 combine quantizer for this path,
while preserving explicit configuration overrides.

Runtime changes cover `token_dispatcher.py` and the shared scale-policy
helper in `quantization/utils.py`. `DynamicMXQuantScaleAlg` names the
existing operator values (`MAX_EXPONENT = 0`, `CEIL = 1`) without
changing the scale policy.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. MiniMax MXFP8 MoE dispatch and combine use the intended scale
policy. No new CLI option or environment variable is introduced.

Release note: `release_notes/fragments/20120.yaml`.

### How was this patch tested?

Author-reported end-to-end accuracy evaluation on
**MiniMax-M3.1-Flash**:

| Configuration | Accuracy |
| --- | ---: |
| Without this patch | 89.36 |
| With this patch | 92.13 |

The accuracy score improved by **2.77 points**.

The conflicting reverted GBSA commits have been removed from branch
history. Forced rebase replay onto upstream base `ceac1a2bd` passed in
an isolated clone; subsequent changes only name the scale algorithms and
remove a comment.

- Regression coverage in `tests/ut/ops/test_token_dispatcher.py` checks
dispatch scale policy, prepared FP8/E8M0 payloads, and combine
defaults/overrides.
- Verified `base.py`, the quantization-method test files and sparse
attention match upstream base `ceac1a2bd`.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Four existing `TestDynamicMxQuantScaleAlg` cases passed using the
AST-extracted helper and enum with import/hardware dependencies stubbed.
This validates Python selection and integer compatibility, not
full-stack or NPU execution.
- `bash format.sh ci`: Ruff check/format, codespell, typos,
clang-format, Markdown lint, actionlint, filename/package,
forbidden-import, boolean-context-manager, long-function and
symbolic-meta checks passed. Gitleaks and logger hooks could not find

claimed.
- `python -m pytest -q tests/ut/ops/test_token_dispatcher.py` could not
start because pytest is unavailable. The local environment also lacks

The end-to-end accuracy results above were provided by the PR author.
Full matching-stack unit-test and additional NPU correctness validation

added.subject: [Feature][PCP] Enable DeepSeek V4.1 SWA bounded replay with DP (#20210)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable DeepSeek V4.1 SWA bounded decoder replay with PCP and DP together
on Model Runner V2. This follows #19321, which has already merged and
currently limits PCP replay to DP=1.

Coordinate decoder execution widths across DP replicas while retaining
suffix tokens on their original PCP owners. Replicas that do not trim,
including idle replicas, keep their original attention metadata and
padded layout but enter the updated DP forward context. Compact batches
rebuild padding and MC2 masks, restore the outer mask on exit, and pass
the PCP context through the current common-attention metadata interface.
Paths that skip DP coordination continue to bypass trimming. Replay
planning, DP coordination, and compact batch preparation are separated
into focused helpers through an immutable replay plan.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. DeepSeek V4.1 can combine `--prefill-context-parallel-size 4
--data-parallel-size 2 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --enable-expert-parallel
--swa-bounded-replay --enforce-eager`. Existing replay restrictions
remain in place. Release note: `release_notes/fragments/20210.yaml`.

### How was this patch tested?

**Latest refactor (`bd7ed489a`):** NPU-host `bash format.sh ci` passed
on the exact refactored source, including all configured formatting and
static checks; hooks made no changes. Unit tests, NPU E2E, and AISBench
were not rerun after this refactor. The runtime results below were
obtained before the refactor and are supporting evidence, not validation
of the refactored implementation.

- **CPU/Gloo:** 119 tests passed with vLLM 0.32.0
(`5df63a7203cdb9328d824a27b682e77c7b9928be`). Coverage includes mixed
trimming decisions, idle DP replicas, empty PCP ownership, preserved
execution widths, padding masks, exception cleanup, and a four-process
PCP2/DP2 test using real Gloo collectives.
- **NPU E2E:** 18/18 requests completed on eight Ascend950DT NPUs,
DP2/PCP4/TP1 with EP, MRV2, eager execution, prefix caching disabled,
and SWA bounded replay enabled. Sequential inputs contained 15, 135,
265, 1905, and 2505 tokens; concurrent requests mixed short and long
inputs at concurrency 4. No runtime errors or collective hangs were
observed.
- **Accuracy:** AISBench GSM8K fixed 48 questions (seed 42), concurrency
4, temperature 0, maximum output length 512: **43/48 (89.58%)**, with
48/48 requests succeeding. Three incorrect answers reached the output
limit without a final answer; one correct `$40,000` answer was extracted
as `000` by the standard evaluator; one answer differed from the
reference. The official score is unchanged. A historical run scored
46/48, but used different software/topology and is not a controlled
comparison. Accuracy acceptance has not been established.
- **Replay/full-row observation:** both paths completed. The 1905-token
example produced different text; the 2505-token example matched. Exact
output equality was not used as the functional acceptance criterion, and
the divergence remains uninvestigated.
- **Environment:** CANN 9.2.0, driver 25.6.rc3, torch 2.10, Python
3.12.13. Used vLLM 0.32.0 Python source with the image's existing
compiled NPU extensions. Engram CPU offload was enabled; THP was
disabled for the entire process tree before importing torch. All eight
workers reported `THP_enabled: 0` and zero anonymous/shared huge-page
usage after testing.
- **Formatting:** NPU host `pre-commit run --all-files` and `bash
format.sh ci` both passed, including Markdown lint and secret scanning.
The checked Git blobs match the submitted code; hooks made no source
changes.
- **Not covered:** throughput/latency comparison, APC, graph mode, other
parallel sizes, and long-running stability.

CPU/Gloo command:

```bash
TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 VLLM_VERSION=0.32.0 python -m pytest -q \
  tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_state.py \
  tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay.py \
  tests/ut/core/test_kv_cache_interface.py \
  tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_distributed.py \
  tests/ut/worker/v2/test_deepseek_v41_engram_state.py \
  tests/ut/attention/test_decoder_replay_swa_indices.py \
  tests/ut/worker/test_replay_slot_padding.py
```

Hardware configuration: `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, `--max-model-len
8192 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --max-num-seqs 4 --block-size 128
--quantization deepseek_v4_fp8 --no-enable-prefix-caching`, plus the
parallel/replay flags above. The launcher used `PR_SET_THP_DISABLE`
before starting vLLM; `use_thp=false` alone does not constrain the
shared Engram backing forced by the MRV2 PCP/DP configuration.

added.subject: [BugFix][Ops] Initialize A5 scatter core count before sort decision (#19775)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

`ScatterNdUpdateSk` on A5 evaluates `SkCeilDiv(indicesAxis_,
totalCoreNum_)` during shape parsing, before `GetPlatformInfo()`
initializes the core count. The local helper has no zero-divisor guard,
so nonempty inputs can terminate the process with `SIGFPE` during Host
tiling, before kernel launch.

Move the SIMD sort decision into `UpdateSimdSortDecision()` and call it
from `DoOpTiling()`, after platform initialization and before the
existing SIMD/mask dispatch. This matches the initialization-order fix
in [cann/ops-nn PR
#12579](https://gitcode.com/cann/ops-nn/pull/12579/discuss), which was
merged into `master` on 2026-10-28 (final upstream head:
`adb6dba58a5ffdae20ab4bb1a3949dfee8414e34`). The merged upstream
decision and call order are equivalent to this PR, with the local
`SkCeilDiv` helper retained. Related upstream report: [ops-nn issue
#7250](https://gitcode.com/cann/ops-nn/issues/7250).

The existing sorting threshold, kernel implementation and arch22 path
are unchanged. This fixes the initialization dependency; it does not
redesign the heuristic for different split modes or claim a measured
performance gain.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Fixes an A5 `ScatterNdUpdateSk` Host-tiling divide-by-zero crash.
No API changes.

### How was this patch tested?

- **Actual A5 regression: 6 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** on Ascend950PR
/ CANN 9.2.0, Python 3.11.10, PyTorch 2.10.0+cpu with torch_npu
2.10.0.post7, and vLLM 0.31.0. Rebuilt only `scatter_nd_update_sk` from
PR commit `b7da6129aaee0f5938ce5b1d20bb7eee7b80bdce` using `bash
build.sh --pkg --ops=scatter_nd_update_sk --soc=ascend950
--vendor_name=custom` and installed it into an isolated vendor
directory. The tests used the PR's original test functions, parameters,
assertions and repository conftest. The existing compatible PyTorch
bridge was reused; this was a fresh native OPP build, not a new full
wheel build.
- The six previously skipped cases comprise 4 unique-index cases (`a=77,
b=128`: FP16/int32, BF16/int64, FP32/int32, int8/int64) and 2
duplicate-index cases (FP16/int32 and BF16/int64), all with
`contiguous=True`. JUnit and call reports confirm all six executed.
Source-file hashes match the fixed Git commit. Loaded-library maps and
API symbol address checks identify the new `libcust_opapi.so` (SHA256
prefix `906a7512ccab`) and Host tiling library (prefix `efc7c43a092f`).
The observer did not replace the operator, inputs or assertions.

  ```bash

TEST=tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/test_scatter_nd_update_sk.py
pytest -sv \
"$TEST::test_scatter_nd_update_sk[True-var_dtype0-idx_dtype0-77-128]" \
"$TEST::test_scatter_nd_update_sk[True-var_dtype1-idx_dtype1-77-128]" \
"$TEST::test_scatter_nd_update_sk[True-var_dtype2-idx_dtype2-77-128]" \
"$TEST::test_scatter_nd_update_sk[True-var_dtype3-idx_dtype3-77-128]" \

"$TEST::test_scatter_nd_update_sk_duplicate_indices[True-var_dtype0-idx_dtype0]"
\

"$TEST::test_scatter_nd_update_sk_duplicate_indices[True-var_dtype1-idx_dtype1]"
  ```

- Native Host regression: compiled baseline and changed production
tiling against the CANN 9.2 SDK and its 56-AIV platform configuration.
The baseline `var=[77,128], indices=[19,1]` exits with `SIGFPE` (-8);
the fix passes 8 Host cases, including the 64/65-indices-per-core
boundary, SplitAfter, SIMT and deterministic tiling.
- `git diff --check`, Python compilation, Ruff checks/formatting passed.
A targeted AST comparison verified that re-enabling the tests changes
only the two defect-related skip branches and the unused `is_950`
import; parameter sets, reference assertions, FP8 capability guards and
the shared timeout protection remain unchanged. The earlier full-tree
format attempt on Windows encountered tool/environment failures; full
repository CI checks remain required before merge.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: Host regression covers the
sorting threshold boundary and distinct tiling paths.
- [x] **Regression test**: Re-enabled the 6 existing A5 cases skipped
for this Host crash and verified all six pass on actual A5 hardware.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: Existing tests check real
custom-op output against a CPU reference.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: This validation checks correctness only;
no performance benchmark or speedup is claimed.

added.subject: [Cherry-pick][main][CI][BugFix] Fix wheel jobs failing on non-root CANN 9.2.1 entrypoint (from #20270) (#20272)
added.body:
Cherry-pick of PR #20270 onto `main`.

Original PR: #20270
Original author: @zhangxinyuehfad

---
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes the "Release Code and Wheel" workflow, where all four wheel jobs
(a2 / a3 / 310p / a5) fail after a successful image build and wheel
build:

--: line 1:
/usr/local/Ascend/cann-9.2.1/share/info/ascendnpu-ir/bin/set_env.sh:
Permission denied
Error: Process completed with exit code 1.

Root cause: the CANN 9.2.1 manylinux base images
(`quay.io/ascend/manylinux:9.2.1-*`) define an entrypoint that sources
several CANN environment scripts, including
`ascendnpu-ir/bin/set_env.sh`. In 9.2.1 that file is no longer readable
by non-root users. The wheel-copy step runs with `docker run -u "$(id
-u):$(id -g)"`, so the entrypoint fails while sourcing before `exec
"$@"`, the `&&` chain breaks, and the container exits 1 — the `cp -r
/workspace/vllm-ascend/dist /outpwd` command never runs. 9.1.0 images
had the same entrypo

added.subject: [BugFix] Keep GLM KPool ND and scope NZ handling to A5 vision (#19564)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

GLM-5.3-Flash fails on Ascend A5 with Model Runner V2 and
`weight_nz_mode=2`:

**KPool weight extraction (NZ to FP32):**

```text
RuntimeError: The copy_ operator with internal format tensors is not supported on Ascend950, except for device-to-host copies and same-device copies between contiguous, non-view NZ tensors with the same dtype, matching shapes/storage descriptions, zero storage offsets, and tensor metadata matching their storage base metadata
```

**Vision projections (batched NZ Linear):**

```text
RuntimeError: matmul got not support format in current device: (2, 29)
```

Keep KPool's fused `wk_weights_proj` in ND for FP32 extraction and CANN
`key_pool`. Apply 2D inputs only to GLM vision projections requiring the
A5 workaround: NZ mode 2, unquantized BF16/FP16 weights. Cache this
decision at construction. Shared `ops/linear.py` and A2/A3 native
projection calls remain unchanged.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Fixes loading and text/image inference in this configuration; no new
public options.

### How was this patch tested?

- **CPU: 240 passed; A5: 112 passed.** Covers hardware/mode/dtype
selection, shapes/layouts, empty inputs, native bypasses and repeated
KPool processing.
- **Full-model A5:** TP8/DP1/EP, eager, V2, FP8 KV and CANN 9.2.0.

added.subject: [Feature][Model] Add Qwen3.8 Flash Next support (#16981)
added.body:
## Summary

This ports the Qwen3.8 Flash Next support originally developed in #15162
onto the current `main` APIs, while reusing the upstream Qwen4Exp model
implementation instead of copying upstream model code into the plugin.

The change adds:

- Ascend wrappers for `Qwen4ExpForCausalLM`,
`Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration`, and `Qwen4ExpMTP`;
- A3 QSA/Lightning Indexer support, including the QSA E3 custom operator
and Meta registration;
- ModelSlim W8A8 configuration;
- Model Runner V1-only speculative decoding integration through
capability protocols rather than scattered model-type checks;
- fixed-address PLE auxiliary inputs for eager and graph execution;
- correct `sigmoid` versus `swish` gating in Ascend's GDN normalization
path;
- deployment documentation and focused unit/source-regression coverage.

## Scope and compatibility

- vLLM-Ascend base after rebase:
`baa023ada41a5b889cac6249845a688aab130892`
- Model Runner V1 only; no legacy/v0 runner changes are included.
- The pinned vLLM revision contains the authoritative Qwen4Exp model
modules consumed by these wrappers. The current vLLM-Ascend release-tag
pairing based on vLLM v0.28 does not contain that upstream model owner,
so this PR should be reviewed and landed with that dependency boundary
in mind.
- A3-only native operator registration remains scoped to the A3 build
branch; the A5 operator set is unchanged.

## Validation

- Rebasing onto the above `main` base resolved the speculative proposer,
ModelSlim quantization, hybrid KV planner, six-region allocation, cache
binding, and gated-norm test conflicts. All 17 PR commits have DCO
sign-offs. Changed-file Ruff, repository F821 scan, Python 3.12
`compileall`, and `git diff --check` passed. Full NPU E2E has **not**
yet been rerun on this rebased tree; the runtime results below are from
the earlier base.
- Related CPU test selection before the latest fix: **283 passed, 13
skipped, 2 failed**. The two failures are the existing Eagle proposer
CPU-native tests for `_C_ascend::npu_copy_and_expand_eagle_inputs`; both
reproduce unchanged on base `8bd6fe0bc` because that operator has
PrivateUse1/Meta registrations but no CPU kernel.
- Explicit non-Qwen PLE runner regression: **10 passed**.
- Changed-file Ruff, Ruff format check, `compileall`, and `git diff
--check`: passed for the earlier port. The latest gated-norm change has
**3 focused unit tests passed**, syntax/diff checks passed, and its
changed-file Ruff import check passed.
- Clean A3 source build passed and installed
`vllm_ascend-0.1.dev5377+gbb19443b6`. Post-build wrapper import
resolution, native QSA schema registration, and Meta execution passed;
the Meta output aliases the supplied output tensor as required.
Post-build focused regression: **15 passed**.
- Real A3 W8A8 TP8/DP1 single-request runs with MTP=3 and decode ACL
Graph produced normal output. Prefix caching showed real long-prefix
hits and identical cold/hit output within prefix-on mode.
- **Prefix-cache parity isolated:** the earlier ON/OFF comparison used
different prefill partitions (`[2304, 96]` versus `[2400]`) and did not
isolate cache restoration. With matched `[2304, 96]` partitions, all 16
generated tokens, token logprobs, and 3421 sampled TP0 layer-trace
events matched. Real hits at 2304 and 1536 also matched same-partition
cold runs exactly. Prefix-cache restoration passed these eager, MTP-off
cases; partition-dependent numerical behavior remains a separate open
risk.
- The **upstream vLLM** QSA metadata fix for Graph-padded decode is
proposed in
[vllm-project/vllm#58040](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58040).
It clamps the mapped-token count to the real token count and fixes the
no-MTP Graph crash observed in this experiment. It is **not included in
this vLLM-Ascend PR**; no-MTP Graph validation requires that upstream
fix until it lands.

## Notes

Repository-wide Ruff currently reports two pre-existing import-order
findings in untouched E2E files. This change does not modify those
files.
