added.subject: [Feature] Enable prefix caching for GLM KDA RecoverSSM (#20369)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Allow GLM KDA RecoverSSM to use prefix caching with Mamba cache mode
`align`. Previously configuration validation rejected prefix caching,
and the inherited MRV2 KDA builder required physical state indices that
Ascend did not prepare.

Prepare those indices with the same device-independent helper used by
Ascend GDN before calling the upstream KDA builder. Reuse the existing
accepted-state recovery and block-boundary checkpoint kernels. Update
the serving guide and extend the four-card regression to check cache
hits and identical cold/warm token outputs in eager and graph modes.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Experimental GLM KDA RecoverSSM can now run with
`--enable-prefix-caching`; vLLM selects Mamba cache mode `align`
automatically. Disabling prefix caching continues to use mode `none`.
Other execution restrictions remain unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

1. Configuration, metadata, cache-layout, KDA-contract and scheduler CPU
regressions: 89 passed. State-index cases cover block boundaries,
changing sequence positions, padded graph rows and unchanged source
block tables.
2. A3 hardware (`80.5.9.129`, Ascend 9392): 12 RecoverSSM align-operator
reference tests passed. The four-card W8A8 synthetic Flash regression
passed with prefix caching enabled in eager and FULL_DECODE_ONLY graph
modes, checking nonzero prefix hits and identical cold/warm output
tokens.
3. Real GLM-5.3-Flash W8A8 on the same A3, TP8 + EP, BF16 model dtype/KV
cache, MTP5, FULL_DECODE_ONLY: 30 GSM8K questions with prefix caching
disabled and enabled. Accuracy was 28/30 with caching disabled, 28/30
with an empty enabled cache and 28/30 on warm repeats; the same two
questions were incorrect in all three runs. All 30 cold/warm token
sequences matched exactly; every warm request hit at least 1280 cached
tokens (640-token blocks). Generating a different suffix against a
shared prefix left the original request's output unchanged.
Disabled/enabled cold token sequences matched in only 2/30 cases. One
final numeric answer differed between the disabled and enabled runs;
both answers were incorrect. These results establish the observed
accuracy and cache-reuse behavior on this sample, not token equivalence
between cache modes.
4. vLLM source was aligned to the repository-verified main commit;
effective Triton Ascend was 3.2.2. Ruff, Ruff formatting, Markdownlint,
Codespell and `git diff --check` passed. Full `bash format.sh ci` was
attempted, but actionlint environment installation failed with a network
disconnect.
5. A5 align-operator tests passed (12 cases). A5 end-to-end validation
remains pending: its first run exited before model initialization
because another workload consumed the devices. This draft primarily
provides the completed A3 validation; no A5 end-to-end success is
claimed.

added.body:
## What this PR does / why we need it

Enable AscendStore pooling for the Qwen3.8 QSA/GDN hybrid cache and
coordinate QSA and PLE transfers with their cache state.

## User-facing behavior

Support pooling for the Qwen3.8 hybrid cache layout, including bulk
Memcache transfer with MTP and DRAM/SSD storage.

## Validation

- Unit regression with vLLM `544f182d`: **162 passed, 1 skipped**, exit
0, across hybrid pooling, AscendStore transfer, Mooncake hybrid,
layerwise hooks, PLE format, Mamba wrapper and MRV2 tests. Diff
whitespace, changed-Python syntax and documented test-path checks
passed. The subsequent E2E-file removal changes no production code or
unit tests; documentation references and diff checks passed. The final
squashed commit has exactly the same tree as the previously validated PR
state; no tests were repeated for history-only squashing.
- Key unit-test coverage is retained: packed shared-page bytes and
other-owner sentinels, both backend adapters, stride/fragment
boundaries, private-state replay boundaries, QSA/PLE ordering,
shared-layer loads, state-row ranges and deferred MTP finalization. The
standalone two-card Mooncake E2E test has been removed as requested; no
automated native NPU E2E coverage is added by this PR. Its documentation
command was removed too.
- The deferred-save reproducer fails before the forwarding fix and
passes afterward.
- Real A3 TP8 validation with vLLM
[544f182d](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542),
toolkit 9.2 and transformer operators 9.3:
- FULL graph capture: **8/8**; concurrent generation: **32/32** nonempty
responses.
- A 9,217-token prompt restored twice: each replay reports **8,192
external hit tokens**, **160 completed backend GET keys**, **0 local
prefix-hit tokens**, and the same output as the cold request.
- DRAM/SSD pressure test: after 32 distinct salted prompts, restoring
the original prompt reports **64 SSD GET hits**, **64 SSD-to-DRAM rewarm
operations**, **351,371,264 bytes rewarmed**, **0 rewarm failures**, and
the same output. Cumulative async SSD flush reached **22,059,614,208
bytes**.
- The SSD backend is a dedicated **1 TiB sparse file mapped through
loop**, not a dedicated raw SSD. Logical capacity is not preallocated
physical space.
- These hardware results use the earlier #16981 runtime stack plus the
identical wrapper fix, not the entire rebased PR head. They do not
establish full validation of the rebased dependency or all hardware
paths.
- The earlier MTP/three-tier GPQA run was stopped at the user's request
after 68/198 cases to restart with rebased code; it has no final score.
A fresh **GPQA Diamond 198 cold + natural external-replay subset** is
running on fixed source `27ebd066`, after its own concurrency, external
restore and SSD-readback prechecks passed. That running service has not
been changed to the latest PR source; its results must not be presented
as validation of the latest packed-page source tree. Earlier bulk
pooling scored 179/198 on a different configuration.
- Full PR-head CI, independent review and model/NPU validation of the
latest packed-page source remain outstanding. CPU regression does not
replace them.

## Bulk three-tier startup configuration

This is the bulk configuration used for the successful MTP and
SSD-rewarm checks. It uses `use_layerwise=false`. The separate layerwise
path requires PIECEWISE; this FULL_DECODE_ONLY example does not claim
layerwise compatibility.

Install the matching vLLM build, vLLM-Ascend native extensions, FLA
runtime and transformer 9.3 operators first. Source the toolkit 9.2,
Ascend IR and ATB environments and configure the installed FLA/custom
operator paths for the target environment. Map eight available host NPUs
to container device IDs 0–7 and provide a reachable HCCL interface.

### Dedicated file-backed storage

Create a new, exclusively owned backing file on a filesystem with
sufficient physical free space:

```bash
# Choose a NEW path; do not reuse another workload's file or device.
export SSD_IMAGE=/path/to/new-dedicated-cache.img
test ! -e "$SSD_IMAGE" || exit 1
truncate -s 1T "$SSD_IMAGE"
export SSD_LOOP="$(sudo losetup --find --show "$SSD_IMAGE")"
sudo losetup "$SSD_LOOP"  # Verify the exact backing file before use.
```

Pass only this owned loop device into the container and put its
container path in `ubsio.disk.path`. A sparse 1 TiB image does not
reserve 1 TiB of physical capacity. Monitor actual filesystem free
space; the validation supervisor is configured to stop work below 200
GiB free. Release only this workload's processes and detach its loop
device after all users of the device exit.

### Memcache local configuration

Replace placeholders with reachable addresses and the exclusively owned
device path:

```ini
ock.mmc.meta_service_url = tcp://<HOST_IP>:25250
ock.mmc.local_service.config_store_url = tcp://<HOST_IP>:25251
ock.mmc.local_service.protocol = device_sdma
ock.mmc.local_service.dram.size = 1GB
ock.mmc.local_service.max.dram.size = 1024GB
ock.mmc.log_level = info
ock.mmc.local_service.storage.enabled = true
ubsio.disk.path = <OWNED_LOOP_DEVICE_IN_CONTAINER>
ubsio.mem.size_in_gb = 10
ubsio.standalone.device_count = 8
ubsio.standalone.force_new_disk = true
```

`dram.size=1GB` is per die. `ubsio.mem.size_in_gb=10` is the separate
UBSIO memory setting; it does not replace the Memcache DRAM limit.
`force_new_disk=true` is for first initialization of this new,
disposable owned device; it must not be used to reopen storage whose
contents need to be preserved. No explicit
`ock.mmc.local_service.world_size` override is required by this example.

### Memcache MetaService configuration

```ini
ock.mmc.meta_service_url = tcp://<HOST_IP>:25250
ock.mmc.meta_service.config_store_url = tcp://<HOST_IP>:25251
ock.mmc.meta_service.metrics_url = http://<HOST_IP>:25252
ock.mmc.log_level = info
ock.mmc.evict_threshold_high = 70
ock.mmc.evict_threshold_low = 60
```

Start the matching installed MetaService in a separate process:

```bash
export MMC_META_CONFIG_PATH=/path/to/mmc-meta.conf
/path/to/python -c 'from memcache_hybrid import MetaService; MetaService.main()'
```

### vLLM startup

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -eo pipefail

# Source the installed CANN 9.2, Ascend IR and ATB environments first.
export MODEL_PATH=/path/to/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-w8a8
export VLLM_PYTHON=/path/to/python
export VLLM_ASCEND_SRC=/path/to/vllm-ascend
export MMC_LOCAL_CONFIG_PATH=/path/to/mmc-local.conf
export HOST_IP=YOUR_HOST_IP
export NETWORK_IFACE=YOUR_NETWORK_INTERFACE

# Python/native dependencies and custom operator vendors must be installed
# and discoverable in this environment.
export PYTHONPATH="$VLLM_ASCEND_SRC:${PYTHONPATH:-}"
export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export SOC_VERSION=ascend910_9382
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
export VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=INFO PYTHONHASHSEED=0
export ACL_OP_INIT_MODE=1 ASCEND_ENABLE_USE_FABRIC_MEM=1
export VLLM_HOST_IP="$HOST_IP" HCCL_IF_IP="$HOST_IP"
export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME="$NETWORK_IFACE"
export TP_SOCKET_IFNAME="$NETWORK_IFACE"
export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME="$NETWORK_IFACE"
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn
export VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1

exec "$VLLM_PYTHON" -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve "$MODEL_PATH" \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8097 --served-model-name Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-w8a8 \
  --trust-remote-code --quantization ascend --tensor-parallel-size 8 --data-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-model-len 139264 --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --async-scheduling \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4,8,12,16,20,24,28,32],"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --additional-config '{"enable_cpu_binding":true,"ascend_compilation_config":{"fuse_norm_quant":false}}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"qwen3_5_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3,"enforce_eager":true}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"AscendStoreConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"backend":"memcache","lookup_rpc_port":25138,"use_layerwise":false,"load_async":false}}'
```

The runtime normalizes the deprecated `qwen3_5_mtp` spelling to `mtp`.
The earlier `--mamba-cache-mode align` argument is deprecated and has no
effect in this vLLM version, so it is omitted here. Local prefix caching
is disabled; successful replay must therefore be supported by
external-hit and completed backend-GET evidence.

GPQA client settings: concurrency 32, `max_tokens=131072`, thinking
enabled, temperature 1.0, top-k 20, top-p 0.95, seed 101, fixed 198
cases and option ordering, and a fresh per-question cache salt. Final
results are pending; sampling, MTP, graph mode and cache-capacity
differences limit comparisons with earlier runs.

added.subject: [CI] Stage local actions in runner temp to reduce job setup time (#20068)
added.body: ### What this PR does / why we need it? #### Background Since runner-container-hooks v0.8.0 replaced shared volumes with exec-based file copying, the runner and job container workspaces may become inconsistent, causing local actions to fail with Can't find action.yml. This issue has been reported in [ascend-gha-runners/docs issues #146](https://github.com/ascend-gha-runners/docs/issues/146) and [actions/runner-container-hooks issues #337](https://github.com/actions/runner-container-hooks/issues/337). An upstream fix has been proposed in [actions/runner-container-hooks PR #445](https://github.com/actions/runner-container-hooks/pull/445), which restores a volume-backed implementation alongside the no-volume implementation, but it has not been merged yet. #### Previous workaround We previously used uses: `$/.github/actions/...` to work around the path resolution issue. However, this causes the runner to download the vllm-ascend repository during the Set up job phase, significantly increasing CI startup time. Additionally, this non-standard syntax requires extra actionlint ignore rules. #### Current approach This PR stages .github under `$RUNNER_TEMP/ci-workflow` and references local actions through uses: `./../../_temp/ci-workflow/.github/actions/....` This is intended to make action manifests resolvable through a standard relative uses: path while preserving reusable actions and removing the previous actionlint exceptions. The main trade-off is that this workaround depends on the runner's directory layout and introduces an additional copy step. If the workspace layout changes, the relative paths must be updated. It also requires the staged files to be visible to the runner. #### When can the official usage be restored Once the upstream issue is fixed and the fix is available in our runner environment, we can consider reverting to the standard uses: `./.github/actions/...` syntax. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? ### How was this patch tested? Complete the verification of the corresponding steps on a2, a3 and 310p; the `$RUNNER_TEMP` path can be found in all cases. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/40647840565/job/122687729037?pr=20068 --- ### Checklist #### Testing - [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change involves boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max values, off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). Where applicable, I added unit tests covering these edge cases in `tests/ut/` or `tests/e2e/`. - [ ] **Regression test**: If this PR fixes a bug, I added a regression test that would fail without the fix. - [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: I covered abnormal paths (exceptions, timeouts, out-of-range, division by zero) in addition to the happy path. - [ ] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New tests assert real behavior and are not written merely to satisfy CI. - [ ] **Performance impact**: If this PR touches a performance-sensitive path, I attached benchmark results and added performance regression tests. - vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542 --------- Signed-off-by: MrZ20 <2609716663@qq.com>

added.author: AuroraEmiya
added.subject: [Performance][Triton] Bound V2 bincount grids and optimize mask packing (#20258)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Thanks to [zihanlin-ai](https://github.com/zihanlin-ai) for [PR
#15270](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/15270), its
implementation and optimization ideas. We agree with its two-pass
approach: scatter prompt-presence flags, retain atomic output counts,
then pack flags into the existing bitmap.

The original operator and tests were migrated unchanged in `129aa5395`
before the following optimizations:

- Flatten both kernels to `min(actual Vector cores, total tiles)`
programs, distributing tiles evenly through internal loops.
- Cover
[#19958](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/19958): 64
requests at 1,048,576 tokens previously launched 65,536 programs; the
tested A3 now uses at most 40 per stage.
- Pack four flag bytes through a zero-copy int32 view, reducing the
per-word reduction width from 32 to 8.
- Preserve the API, persistent layouts, atomic output counts and
1024-token/128-word tiles.
- Fix the reported Triton-Ascend 3.6 `NameError` by constructing the
format constants with `tl.constexpr(value)`; the algorithm, grid and
tiles are unchanged by that compatibility fix.

Includes the A2/A3 NPU regressions, a release-note fragment and
[operator/test
documentation](https://github.com/AuroraEmiya/vllm-ascend/blob/1cfbe3680bc64471973bd4b57126422694f35ba8/vllm_ascend/ops/triton/v2/docs/bincount.md).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Faster initialization of penalty state for the measured long histories,
with bounded launches at the 1M-token boundary. Short histories with
multiple newly admitted requests can incur more initialization work, as
reported below. APIs and persistent layouts are unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

Performance and earlier Qwen3-8B measurements use operator SHA256
`83b871bc…`. The current constants-only compatibility revision is
`f07e939b…`; its compatibility checks and project-nightly results are
reported separately.

#### Correctness

- **50 NPU tests passed on A3** through normal repository conftests and
framework imports. Coverage includes int32/int64, strides, inactive-row
preservation, same-word bits across programs, request-row reuse, bit 31
and exact masks/counts.
- Exact #19958 boundaries: 64 requests with 1,047,552 / 1,048,576 /
1,049,600 tokens, vocabulary 151936 and zero output history.
- The compatibility revision passed **27 standalone cases on each of
Triton-Ascend 3.2.2 and 3.6.0**, on A3 with fresh caches and the bypass
flag unset.
- The A2/A3 nightly guard is retained. Fresh device-test evidence here
is A3; the separate A5 follow-up is linked in the checklist.

```bash
pytest -q tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_bincount.py
```

Prompt flags retain overlapping non-atomic byte stores of the same
value; output counts use atomic additions. Exact test results do not
establish a general backend memory-ordering guarantee.

#### Single-operator performance

Main: `5bd7714b5ef39315cc26867bc67826d42ac0760a`; PR15270:
`ef792533de1d4fcd25e458eda701fa105ffafeb4`.

Matched A3 Ascend910_9362, CANN 9.2.0, Torch 2.10.0 / torch_npu
2.10.0.post4, Triton-Ascend 3.2.2. These values sum **device-task work
including initialization**, rather than model latency. Ordinary cases
retain ten calls after three warmups.

| Requests / prompt / output | Main ms | PR15270 ms | This PR ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 / 32 / 32 | 0.096 | 0.151 | 0.076 |
| 1 / 4096 / 32 | 1.104 | 0.273 | 0.199 |
| 8 / 4096 / 32 | 9.592 | 1.125 | 0.524 |
| 64 / 4096 / 256 | 83.427 | 7.600 | 3.002 |
| 64 / 1047552 / 0 | 25859.443 | 2866.678 | 245.206 |
| 64 / 1048576 / 0 | coreDim=65536 failure | coreDim=65536 failure |
246.632 |
| 64 / 1049600 / 0 | Not rerun | Not rerun | 251.149 |

Large candidate/PR cases retain three calls after one warmup; serialized
main retains two. Failed launches are not timing samples.

Across 37 legal nonempty histories, exact three-way checks passed; this
PR reduces device work versus PR15270 on 37/37 and main on 31/37. The
six regressions versus main are:

| Requests / prompt / output | Main us | PR15270 us | This PR us |
Increase vs main us |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8 / 1 / 0 | 193.99 | 977.55 | 373.32 | 179.33 |
| 8 / 8 / 4 | 208.78 | 980.49 | 374.80 | 166.02 |
| 8 / 32 / 32 | 261.99 | 987.71 | 383.39 | 121.40 |
| 64 / 1 / 0 | 490.72 | 6607.16 | 2015.25 | 1524.53 |
| 64 / 8 / 4 | 622.77 | 6612.63 | 2014.21 | 1391.44 |
| 64 / 32 / 32 | 1100.46 | 6626.33 | 2030.82 | 930.36 |

**These are request-initialization regressions; the steady-state decode
path is unchanged.** `bincount` runs when penalty-using requests are
admitted or resumed. It scans the prompt and any output history already
present, builds the prompt bitmap and initializes output counts.
“Output” in these tables means that existing history; it is normally
zero for a fresh request.

Normal decode incrementally updates counts for newly committed tokens
and uses the unchanged `apply_penalties` kernel, without rerunning
either `bincount` kernel per token. Vocabulary-sized clearing and
packing add fixed initialization work, which can outweigh token-scan
savings for short histories. The full legal-shape table is in the linked
MD.

#### GPQA accuracy

**Project nightly configuration — current compatibility revision.** Used
[Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8-A3.yaml](https://github.com/AuroraEmiya/vllm-ascend/blob/1cfbe3680bc64471973bd4b57126422694f35ba8/tests/e2e/cases/models/configs/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8-A3.yaml):
MRV2, TP2/DP1, MTP3, FULL_DECODE_ONLY, prefix caching and async
scheduling; all 198 questions, official chat-CoT, concurrency 32, max
output 32768, temperature 1, `presence_penalty=1.5` /
`repetition_penalty=1.0`, with no request seed or thinking override.
Other settings follow the linked configuration.

Both sources used the same A3 devices, weights and cached Triton-Ascend
3.6 compatibility image, with CANN 9.2.0 / torch_npu 2.10.0.post7. This
used the project configuration, not the actual nightly image or A5
hardware. Official AISBench source:
`0da56eadb2ac85c31c2540f4f5b69af3ec5717a5`.

| Implementation | Correct /198 in rounds 1,2,3 | Mean accuracy | Sample
SD |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Main | 171,168,169 | 85.5219% | 0.7715 percentage points |
| Current compatibility revision (f07) | 171,169,168 | 85.5219% | 0.7715
percentage points |

All six runs passed the original 85.1±5 percentage-point range, with 198
unique successful predictions per run. Equal means do not imply
identical responses under temperature 1 without a request-level seed.
This presence-only configuration does not consume the prompt repetition
bitmap.

#### GSM8K serving performance

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Model / runner | Qwen3-8B BF16, MRV2, TP1 on one A3 device |
| Server | FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graphs; max model length 40960, max
sequences 32, max batched tokens 4096, memory utilization 0.85; prefix
caching disabled |
| Dataset | All 1,319 GSM8K test questions; official
`gsm8k_gen_0_shot_cot_str_perf` template |
| Input lengths | Dataset-dependent; benchmark reports 96,693 input
tokens per run, averaging 73.31 tokens/request |
| Client | AISBench streaming chat, concurrency 32, `request_rate=0`, 32
warmups |
| Generation | `temperature=0`, `top_p=1`, `top_k=-1`, `seed=42`,
`repetition_penalty=1.03`, `enable_thinking=False` |
| Output | Fixed 128 tokens/request: `max_out_len=128`,
`ignore_eos=True` |
| Repeats | Two sequential repeats per source, in main / PR15270 / this
PR order, on the same device |

All sources use the same weights, runtime and Python tree except the
penalty module. Upstream vLLM is
`544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542`; the common plugin Python
base is `c0e0e05b94830034e40270384002d5ba5a416821`. The runtime is CANN
9.2.0, Torch 2.10.0 / torch_npu 2.10.0.post4 and Triton-Ascend 3.2.2.

This is an **unprofiled serving-performance test**, using GSM8K as the
workload rather than reporting a GSM8K accuracy score. Each run
completed 1,319 requests, with zero failures and 168,832 generated
tokens.

| Implementation | Mean output token/s | Mean TTFT ms | Mean TPOT ms |
Mean E2EL ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main | 1448.24 | 156.75 | 20.70 | 2784.70 |
| PR15270 | 1470.24 | 162.50 | 20.30 | 2742.10 |
| This PR | 1467.56 | 169.90 | 20.30 | 2746.00 |

Mean throughput is +1.33% versus main and −0.18% versus PR15270; TTFT is
worse in these runs. Two sequential repeats without reverse-order
confirmation do not establish a stable whole-model speedup. Full per-run
results are in the linked MD.

Captured bincount device-work shares were **0.00836%** for one request
generating 64 tokens and **0.03652%** for eight GSM8K requests
generating 512 tokens in total. These divide inclusive bincount
device-task time by all captured device-task time; they are not
end-to-end wall-clock or critical-path shares.

#### Compilation

Changing only grid or tensor contents reuses binaries. Scalar
exact-one/divisibility classes, dtype and pointer alignment can create
variants; the audited 32-request/40960-context profile has a scoped
estimate of at most nine statistics and three packing variants. No
startup warmup integration is added.

### Checklist

- [x] **Correctness:** 50 A3 NPU tests, including #19958 boundaries,
same-word bits and request-row reuse.
- [x] **Performance:** main/PR15270 comparisons, legal short-history
regressions and GSM8K serving results recorded.
- [x] **GPQA project-nightly accuracy:** Qwen3.8-27B main 171/168/169
and current 171/169/168; both mean 85.5219%, all six within 85.1±5pp on
the A3 compatibility runtime.
- [x] **A5 compatibility:** [reported working on
A5](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20258#issuecomment-6519999362);
the constexpr fix also passed the A3 Triton-Ascend 3.6 checks above.
- [x] **Specialization:** scalar/type/alignment classes reviewed; no
warmup integration.
- [x] **CI:** required checks passed for unchanged head `1cfbe3680`.
[Workflow](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/41043089875);
A5 was skipped.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542

added.subject: [Refactor][Attention] Unify PCP O-proj weight switching (#18744)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Unifies MRV2 DSA-PCP and SFA-PCP O-projection execution in a shared
`ParallelOProjection` component. It owns checkpoint partitioning,
temporary full-weight views, exchange buffers, collectives and output
reductions while retaining native grouped and quantized kernels.
Full-weight, local-weight and token-exchange modes share weight
restoration after each forward.

Preserves current PCP/DCP cache mappings and NoPE padding behavior. This
revision follows main's removal of legacy DSA-CP (#19493): obsolete
implementations and their test files remain deleted, with lifecycle and
precision coverage aligned to the supported PCP/DCP classes.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No new user-facing API, environment variable or configuration option.
The existing PCP O-projection sharding switch remains supported.

### How was this patch tested?

Current validation head: `80ab94490591c9c672acc710c855ff45d05fa994`.

This CI follow-up changes only four collective mock targets in
`test_dsa_v1.py` and `test_dsa_v41_cp.py` to `torch.distributed`. Legacy
DSA-CP removal also removed the old `dsa_cp.dist` import alias, while
the shared `ParallelOProjection` uses the same public PyTorch
distributed module. Production source, test parameter combinations,
assertions and numerical thresholds are unchanged.

- Current-head pre-commit: **success**
([job](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/41048926329/job/124039856361)).
- Current-head cpu-ut (vllm@544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542) /
cpu-ut card-: **success**
([job](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/41048926329/job/124042119082)).
- Current-head cpu-ut (vllm@v0.32.0) / cpu-ut card-: **success**

added.subject: [BugFix][MoE] Fix A5 AllGather with MRV2 EPLB (#18549)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix MRV2 EPLB when A5 selects AllGather. Every rank routes the same
gathered rows, so rank-dependent replica selection can execute a route
twice or omit it.

- Use a rank-independent replica table for AllGather, preserving the
existing MC2/AlltoAll selection.
- Count eligible routes once on their physical owner, excluding source
padding and non-collecting phases. Preserve draft source masks across
prefill, decode, dummy runs and graph replay.
- Refresh captured routing tables in place after placement changes,
discard stale load history and handle elastic active-map resizing.
- Keep this change scoped to MRV2. Restore MRV1 load collection and the
existing input-id AllGather implementation to baseline.
- Consolidate MRV2 mask construction, AllGather alignment, owner
counting, validation and load writes in
`AscendEplbLayerState.record_load()`. `forward_impl` saves the source
row count before preparation and calls the state method after FFN
execution and before output finalization. The mask filters load
statistics and does not alter routing or GMM counts.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Fix incorrect routing and load accounting with A5 AllGather and
MRV2 EPLB, including redundant experts. The communication selector is
unchanged. Moving recording into the layer state adds no further
user-facing change.

### How was this patch tested?

Validation at `e409edd82afb4b532d919f87f5362766a1599d7f`, against the
pinned vLLM revision below:

- Related CPU/mock regressions: **330 passed** across the AllGather,
load-recording, routed-expert, fused-MoE, EPLB state/controller and
speculator tests. Coverage includes post-FFN mask communication order,
differing source/prepared row counts, ubatch and TP masks, padding
precedence, both count formats, source-ineligible owners, shared step
flags, V2 with no EPLB state and uninitialized recording fields.
- `bash format.sh ci`: passed.
- Full `tools/mypy.sh 1` for Python 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12: passed across
`vllm_ascend`, `examples` and `tests` in a Linux lint environment.
- Real Ascend A5 four-device regression: **2 passed, 1 deselected**,
with TP2/DP2/EP4, eager execution and full graph capture/replay. The
test directly invokes `AscendEplbLayerState.record_load()`, covering
ineligible sources, zero valid source rows and placement refresh under
replay. Runtime: CANN 9.2.0-beta.2, PyTorch 2.10.0 and torch_npu
2.10.0.post4.

  ```bash
  VLLM_VERSION=0.32.1.dev0 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
    python -m pytest -sv -rs \
    tests/e2e/pull_request/four_card/test_data_parallel_tp2.py \
    -k a5_dp2_tp2_allgather_eplb
  ```

This is weight-free component/graph validation using identity experts.
The version override selects compatibility paths for the pinned source
checkout. No native custom-op or performance result is claimed.

A separate CANN 9.1.0 environment segfaulted on both the previous PR
head and this refactor; that run is not counted as passing evidence. The
initial CANN 9.2.0-beta.2 attempt hit an occupied HCCL listener before
load recording; the successful run used disjoint process-local HCCL
host/NPU socket port ranges.

Previous full-model diagnostics did not establish strict token equality.
That limitation remains unresolved; full-model accuracy and performance
were not rerun for this refactor. Broader model/logit consistency,
MTP/SP integration and matched throughput/TTFT measurements remain
pre-merge validation.

added.subject: [Performance] Optimize Qwen PLE prefill with Triton on Ascend (#20344)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it

Optimize Qwen PLE prefill on Ascend with a prefill-only Triton module.
The Ascend model binding selects the path once: prefill calls
`ple_conv_prefill`; decode and speculative decoding call upstream
`ple_conv`. There is no single-request special case or backend-selection
environment variable.

The prefill path materializes the four-tap weights as contiguous `[tap,
channel]` data, reads channels contiguously, skips history-state loads
when a tap comes from the current chunk, and uses a measured
2048-channel tile with eight warps. The separate state-writeback kernel
preserves old history until every token has read it. Multi-request
batches, token remapping, initial history, null state slots, and both
state strides are supported. This replaces the earlier PyTorch prefill
implementation in this PR.

The model-local binding remains under maintainer review. The required
Ascend Qwen model adaptation is present in main; this PR supersedes
#20269.

### Validation

- In `qjj_flash_main` on Ascend 950DT with vLLM
`544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542`, an isolated checkout of the
final PR source passed all four NPU nightly operator tests. The tests
verify exact output and final state against upstream, and explicitly
verify mode routing through the model binding. Actual import paths were
checked before testing.
- Earlier diagnostic kernel sweeps covered 62 BF16/FP16 cases, including
mode semantics, token maps, both state strides, optional residuals,
4096/8192-token inputs, and channel tails. The final PR module is
prefill-only; decode/spec use upstream directly. Final module cleanup
was revalidated by the nightly suite.
- Focused final-dispatcher full-call timing at BF16 and 8192 total
tokens: 0.876 ms for one request with channel-stride-12 test state, and
0.758 ms for four requests with channel-stride-one state (the current
vLLM default layout). These are isolated operator times, not service
TTFT.
- Focused Ruff lint/format, Python compilation, and diff checks passed.

### Follow-up

- Model ownership and patch removal are tracked in #20384; rewire the
PLE operator after that refactor is integrated.
- Validate service-level TTFT and broader hardware/configuration
coverage.

added.subject: [BugFix] Fix request-major sampling masks for speculative decoding on Ascend (#19866)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix Ascend sampling-mask packing for the upstream request-major API. A
speculative-decoding request can commit multiple tokens in one round,
and each token needs the mask from its corresponding logits row. The
previous one-row-per-request implementation cannot accept the updated
arguments or represent these outputs correctly.

This PR accepts `cu_num_logits` and `rows_per_request`, reads row
`cu_num_logits[req_idx] + slot_idx`, and allocates `num_requests *
rows_per_request` output slots. Inactive slots receive zero
masks/counts. Device-side offsets and sampled counts remain dynamic
during graph replay, without adding host synchronization.

It preserves the zero-width compact-token-ID fallback and its
explanatory comments, so upstream decodes the exact packed mask. It also
adds integration coverage adapted from upstream
`test_replay_on_off_preserves_rejection_sampling_and_rng`.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, it corrects existing sampling-mask replay behavior with the
request-major upstream API, including multiple committed tokens during
speculative decoding. There are no new configuration options, response
fields or schema changes.

This revision targets the API exercised with vLLM 0.32.0 and vLLM main
at 544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542.

### How was this patch tested?

**Functional NPU regression: 36 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.**

The pushed implementation was validated on Ascend950DT. The 28 packing
cases cover ragged request-major offsets, inactive slots, empty batches,
invalid row counts, nonfinite logits, non-contiguous input, chunk
concatenation/slicing, processed top-k/top-p support and graph replay
with updated device metadata.

The 8 rejection/RNG integration cases use real Ascend
rejection-sampling, logprob and packing kernels. They cover immediate
rejection, rejection at the second draft position and full acceptance,
with single/chunked verification, two seed configurations and two
logprob settings. Replay on/off preserves committed tokens, counts,
valid logprobs, selected ranks and global NPU RNG state without
resetting RNG between passes; emitted masks match finite processed-logit
supports.

Reproduce from the vLLM-Ascend checkout with the patch applied:

```bash
python -m pytest -v \
  tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_sampling_mask.py 
```

**End-to-end server scripts and observed outputs (MTP off/on).**

These are the successful results fromvLLM `0.32.0+empty` . 

**MTP disabled — `start_non_mtp.sh`:**

```bash
#!/bin/bash
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=512

vllm serve /data/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B \
 --served-model-name auto \
 --max-num-seqs 64 \
 --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
 --trust-remote-code \
 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
 --data-parallel-size 1 \
 --host 127.0.0.1 \
 --port 21006 \
 --enable-expert-parallel \
 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
 --logprobs-mode processed_logprobs --max-logprobs 256 \
 --enable-scale-out \
 --return-sampling-mask \
 --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' 2>&1 | tee server.non_mtp.log
```

**MTP enabled — `start_mtp.sh`:**

```bash
#!/bin/bash
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=512

vllm serve /data/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B \
 --served-model-name auto \
 --max-num-seqs 64 \
 --max-model-len 4096 \
 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
 --trust-remote-code \
 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
 --data-parallel-size 1 \
 --host 127.0.0.1 \
 --port 21007 \
 --enable-expert-parallel \
 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
 --logprobs-mode processed_logprobs --max-logprobs 256 \
 --enable-scale-out \
 --return-sampling-mask \
 --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
 --cudagraph-capture-sizes 3 6 12 24 48 96 192 \
 --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}' 2>&1 | tee server.mtp.log
```

**Client request**, after the selected service becomes healthy:

```bash
cat > request.json <<'JSON'
{
  "token_ids": [
    785,
    6722,
    315,
    9625,
    374
  ],
  "sampling_params": {
    "temperature": 1.0,
    "top_k": 20,
    "top_p": 1.0,
    "max_tokens": 32,
    "logprobs": 256,
    "seed": 7,
    "ignore_eos": true
  },
  "output_mode": "tokens",
  "stream": false
}
JSON

# MTP disabled: run against the first service.
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:21006/inference/v1/generate \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @request.json -o response.non_mtp.json

  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @request.json -o response.mtp.json
```

**Operator performance.**

The baseline is the optimized Ascend implementation from #17193. 

Only the seven published #17193 configurations were used. I reran the
current PR for 10 rounds per configuration (70 new rounds), using the
same input construction and msprof settings as the retained baseline
measurements. Every application passed exact packed-mask/count checks
against an independent CPU reference.

Hardware: Ascend950DT; vLLM `0.32.0+empty`, torch-npu `2.10.0.post7`,
Triton-Ascend `3.6.0`, and CANN `9.2.0-B100` toolkit/ATB environment.
All sampled current/rated frequencies were 1650.

Measurements are mean target-kernel `Task Duration(us)`, excluding
Python wrappers, allocation, input preparation and the pre-kernel
contiguous copy. msprof settings: `launch-count=10`,
`launch-skip-before-match=6`, `warm-up=5`, and
`MemoryDetail,Occupancy,PipeUtilization,Roofline`. The input values were
reconstructed from the public configurations; #17193 did not publish its
complete profiling inputs.

| Case | #17193 baseline (µs) | Current PR (µs) | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| b1_v17_active1_colstride1_rows1 | 3.138 | 3.382 | +7.77% |
| b8_v8191_active1_colstride1_rows1 | 6.256 | 6.147 | -1.74% |
| b8_v8192_active1_colstride1_rows1 | 5.625 | 5.622 | -0.05% |
| b8_v8193_active1_colstride1_rows1 | 6.999 | 6.905 | -1.34% |
| b8_v8193_active0_colstride1_rows1 | 6.993 | 6.456 | -7.68% |
| b32_v151936_active1_colstride2_rows1 | 55.587 | 54.774 | -1.46% |
| b128_v151936_active1_colstride1_rows1 | 106.454 | 104.746 | -1.61% |

Change = `(current PR / baseline - 1) × 100%`; positive means slower.
B1/V17 is +7.77% in this cross-batch comparison (about 0.244 µs). The
two V151936 cases are -1.46% and -1.61%.
The seven current-PR runs completed successfully and passed their
independent correctness checks.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: Empty batches, inactive slots,
ragged offsets, packing boundaries and strided inputs.
- [x] **Regression test**: Request-major packing and integrated replay
on/off rejection-sampling/RNG coverage.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: Invalid `rows_per_request` and
forced rejection paths.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: Real NPU behavior checked against
independent expectations and replay-disabled execution.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: Manual hardware results are provided
above; an automated performance regression gate has not been
added/configured.

added.subject: [BugFix][Model] Backport MiniMax-M3 prompt reasoning boundary fix (#20468)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Backport
[vllm-project/vllm#63492](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63492)
to `releases/v0.32.0rc` (base:
`ffca1c99bb28d9c92dd5dcf327f8b242404a5055`). The vLLM `v0.32.0`
MiniMax-M3 parser does not contain that fix.

MiniMax-M3.1-Flash prompts contain literal `<mm:think></mm:think>`
instructions and may contain a previous assistant turn prefixed with
`</mm:think>`. Checking the entire prompt incorrectly marks the new
turn's reasoning as finished. Streamed responses then expose
reasoning/markers in `delta.content`, and structured-output constraints
can start before reasoning is complete.

- Register a platform patch so the serving process receives the fix.
- Wrap only `MiniMaxM3ReasoningParser.is_reasoning_end` and
`is_reasoning_end_streaming`, restricting their input to the last `]~b]`
message boundary, as upstream does. Retain the original parsing and
state handling.
- Preserve output-only IDs, tokenizers without the message-boundary
token, and non-streaming extraction. Skip patching when the upstream
`_last_message_ids` helper already exists; repeated loading is also a
no-op.
- Add 29 regression/compatibility cases and a manual HTTP E2E client for
single-turn, multi-turn and JSON Schema requests.

Architectural/removal plan: this is a temporary parser-only backport,
with no model runner or NPU kernel changes. Remove it when all supported
vLLM versions include #63492. The additional backward scan is over CPU
token IDs and stops at the last message boundary; output-only IDs
require a linear scan, as in upstream. No device synchronization or
tensor transfer is added. Hardware performance has not been measured.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. With `--reasoning-parser minimax_m3`, prompt/history markers no
longer prematurely terminate the current reasoning phase. Streamed
reasoning remains separate from content, and structured-output
reasoning-end detection uses the current message. A release-note
fragment is included in this PR.

### How was this patch tested?

- Hardware validation on 177.11.21.1 (8 x Ascend950DT), PR commit
`84e6fcce0efb10c9819fe1687e5e03d3db3a5b4e`: **29 regression tests
passed; all 6 HTTP requests passed** using the client below. Single-turn
returned `391`, multi-turn returned `Berlin.`, and JSON Schema returned
`{"answer":391}`, in both streaming and non-streaming modes. All
responses finished with `stop`, separated reasoning from content, and
contained no leaked reasoning markers.
- The dedicated MiniMax image reports vLLM `0.30.0` (commit
`ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607`); its original MiniMax parser
is byte-identical to vLLM `v0.32.0` (Git blob
`d49f9311f46026fa43650c3c8f07ec76edbc73fc`). This validates the parser
backport in the model image, not the entire release branch. Only the
patched service was exercised for HTTP validation; deterministic checks
with the real model tokenizer confirmed the incorrect pre-patch `True`
becomes `False` for both single-turn and multi-turn prompts.
- Normal platform import automatically loaded the registered patch. No
manual patch invocation was used during service startup. The validation
container was stopped afterward.
- Isolated source-level validation on Windows against **unmodified vLLM
v0.32.0** `minimax_m3_reasoning_parser.py`, `basic_parsers.py`, and
`abs_reasoning_parsers.py`: **51 passed** (22 existing upstream tests +
29 new tests). Unrelated import dependencies and protocol containers
were stubbed; the parser and its base implementations were real upstream
source. This is not a full installed-vLLM or NPU test.
- Deterministic before/after checks: both prompt-only `is_reasoning_end`
and prompt-prefixed/open-reasoning `is_reasoning_end_streaming` returned
the incorrect `True` before the patch and the expected `False`
afterward.
- Focused Ruff checks and `git diff --check`: passed.
- `python tests/e2e/models/minimax_m3_reasoning_client.py --help`:
passed.

```bash
python -m pytest -sv tests/ut/patch/platform/test_patch_minimax_m3_reasoning.py
```

#### Actual model A/B verification on Ascend

Use an already working MiniMax-M3.1-Flash Ascend deployment with the
same weights, template, vLLM version and serving options for both runs.
Follow the [release branch deployment
guide](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/releases/v0.32.0rc/docs/source/tutorials/models/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash.md#5-online-service-deployment)
for the hardware-specific full launch command. That guide uses dedicated
model images and Ascend-adapted W8A8/MXFP8 weights; the official NVFP4
checkpoint is not a drop-in Ascend substitute. Do not replace that
image's model adaptation with a generic source installation just to test
this parser fix.

The examples below target the guide's endpoint/model name:
`http://127.0.0.1:11223/v1` and `minimax-m3.1-flash`. Keep
`--reasoning-parser minimax_m3` in the launch command. If using tool
calls, also keep `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser
minimax_m3`.

**A. Before applying the patch**, start the service with your existing
working launch command and run this from the PR checkout:

```bash
curl --fail --silent --show-error http://127.0.0.1:11223/health
python tests/e2e/models/minimax_m3_reasoning_client.py \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:11223/v1 --model minimax-m3.1-flash
```

For a raw streamed reproduction:

```bash
curl --fail-with-body --no-buffer http://127.0.0.1:11223/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"minimax-m3.1-flash","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is 17 * 23? Give only the number in your final answer."}],"stream":true,"temperature":0,"max_tokens":4096,"chat_template_kwargs":{"reasoning_effort":"low"}}'
```

Affected behavior: `delta.content` may contain `<mm:think>...
</mm:think>` or a leading `</mm:think>`, while reasoning is absent.
Non-streaming normally separates the fields correctly. The client prints
both responses and fails on leaked markers. Generation is
model-dependent; use the deterministic reproduction above as the
reliable parser regression signal.

**B. Restart the service with this PR installed and rerun the client.**
Normal installations automatically load the patch through platform
registration; no manual apply step is needed. The installation snippet
below is only for an existing dedicated model image that does not yet
include this PR. To preserve the dedicated image's existing model
implementation, run the following from the PR checkout inside that
container instead of reinstalling the entire repository:

After the fix:

- The client completes all six requests (three scenarios, each
non-streaming and streaming).
- `content` has no `<mm:think>`/`</mm:think>` tags. When the model emits
a reasoning block, its text is reported in `reasoning`; an immediate
closing tag may legitimately produce empty reasoning.
- The JSON Schema case yields `{"answer":391}`. The client prints
reasoning separately. JSON validity alone does not prove the grammar's
activation timing; the deterministic end-check regression covers that
condition.
- A length-limited response is reported as incomplete, rather than
counted as a pass. Tool-call scenarios reported by upstream are not
covered by this manual client.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: empty input, empty final
message, boundary token ID zero, split markers, missing boundary token,
continued assistant messages.
- [x] **Regression test**: prompt/history markers and prompt-prefixed
streaming checks.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: missing reasoning-marker
vocabulary still raises; the E2E client rejects incomplete responses and
marker leakage.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: real upstream parser behavior and
unchanged extraction/state precedence, plus idempotence/upstream-fix
guards.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542

added.subject: [Performance][Qwen3.8Next][Attention] Dispatch prefill between FIA+mask and GBSA at 24K logical KV [v0.32.0rc] (#20467)
added.body:
## What this PR does

This PR ports the Qwen4Exp FIA + selected-token-mask dispatch and the
24K logical-visible-KV dispatch policy from #20304 onto
`vllm-project/vllm-ascend:releases/v0.32.0rc`. The original commit
ordering and author attribution are preserved while resolving the
release-branch integration against its latest head.

### Dispatch policy

- Pure decode always uses GBSA.
- For each prefill request in pure-prefill or mixed batches:
- if the cached logical KV prefix at the start of the current chunk is
below 24K, the whole chunk uses FIA + selected-token mask;
- if the cached logical KV prefix is at least 24K, the whole chunk uses
GBSA.
- A normal 4K chunk that crosses 24K is kept intact on FIA + mask. The
following chunk switches to GBSA.
- Mixed batches are classified per request, and consecutive GBSA rows
are coalesced without changing request IDs or output positions.

The threshold is based on request/query-row logical visible KV length,
not physical cache allocation or the fixed 4K scheduler capacity.

## Why

This retains FIA behavior for short and medium prefill while routing
later long-context chunks to GBSA. Decode remains on GBSA.

## Performance results

### 32K input / 1-token output

This single-request result compares the dispatch strategy before and
after the stacked optimization. Input length is 32K, output length is 1
token, and concurrency is 1.

| Metric | Unit | Before (dispatch strategy) | After | Change | Change
rate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| E2EL | ms | 13476.0 | 10325.2 | -3150.8 | -23.38% |
| TTFT | ms | 13475.8 | 10325.0 | -3150.8 | -23.38% |
| ITL | ms | 0.1 | 0.1 | 0.0 | 0.00% |
| Input Tokens | token | 32820 | 32820 | 0 | 0.00% |
| Output Tokens | token | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0.00% |

added.author: Karryking3
added.subject: [BugFix][v0.32.0rc] Fix SwigluGroupQuant MXFP tail store masks (#20540)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?
Fix the MXFP output-store tail masks in SwigluGroupQuant. Four
consecutive packed stores previously used four independent
remaining-column counters, so each store treated the same tail as valid
and could overwrite adjacent rows or UB buffers. Share one counter
across the four stores.

The issue was encountered with Qwen3.8-Next W4A8 MoE: the expert
intermediate dimension is **640**. This width leaves a partial final
vector in the four-way packed output-store path. The independent
counters incorrectly mark later stores in that final group as valid,
allowing writes beyond the row into adjacent UB storage and causing
incorrect or unstable quantized activations.

Add regression coverage for partial-vector widths (including 640),
FP16/BF16 inputs, repeatability, reconstruction error, and graph replay.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
Fixes incorrect or unstable MXFP activation quantization, including the
tested W4A8 MoE path. No new configuration.

### How was this patch tested?
- End-to-end Qwen3.8-Next W4A8 GPQA Diamond validation on the deployed
stack: **90.91% (180/198 correct)**, with all 198 requests successful
and zero request failures. P/D used TP2 x DP2, Combine quantization was
enabled, the UVA prefix-write optimization was present, and P/D static
kernel was disabled. This validates the combined deployment containing
the fixed custom operator; it is not an isolated accuracy attribution to
this fix.
- Ascend 950 / CANN 9.2: 22 NPU regression cases passed in
`tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/test_swiglu_group_quant_mxfp_tail.py`,
using the rebuilt fixed custom-op package.
- The hardware test used the deployed development stack; complete
integration validation on the target branch remains subject to CI.
- Ruff lint/format and `git diff --check` passed for the changed code.
Full `bash format.sh ci` was attempted in isolated target-branch
worktrees but could not complete because pre-commit tool-environment
installation stalled; full hook validation remains for CI.

added.body:
## Summary

Port the Qwen3.8 Flash Next pipeline-parallel (PP) and sequence-parallel
(SP/FlashComm1) support from #20311 to the `releases/v0.32.0rc` release
branch. The packed QSA/GDN/PLE KV-cache layout remains safe for PP
stage-local ownership.

## Changes

This PR preserves the complete twelve-commit PP+SP series from #20311,
including:

- FlashComm1/SP enablement for Qwen3.8 Flash Next.
- PP-compatible model-state and intermediate-tensor handling.
- QSA main-attention fused RMSNorm + MRoPE projection on the target
model, while retaining the graph-safe upstream decomposition for the MTP
draft model.
- MRV2 PP/SP token padding and full-token feedback handling.
- PP-aware packed QSA/GDN/PLE cache planning.
- Runner-level SP padding scoped to `PP > 1`, avoiding duplicate
model-internal SP padding in SP-only deployments.
- Compatibility patch documentation and source-regression coverage.

The release branch is descended from the original #20311 base. All
twelve commits therefore cherry-pick cleanly onto `releases/v0.32.0rc`
without conflict, while preserving author and committer attribution.

## Motivation

Qwen3.8 Flash Next already supports packed QSA/GDN/PLE cache storage and
MRV2 on Ascend. PP partitions model layers across stages, while
SP/FlashComm1 shards tokens across tensor-parallel ranks. The original
single-stage assumptions caused PP startup failures when state owners
were aggregated across stages or PLE existed on only one stage. This
work enables PP+SP together without weakening the packed-cache ownership
model.

symmetric per-channel INT4 weights and per-token INT8 activations.

scheme. Existing MXFP schemes are outside this change.

added.subject: [Performance][v0.32.0rc] Optimize A2/A3 INT8 QSFA no-RoPE computation and KV gather (#20584)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Backport of #20456 to `releases/v0.32.0rc`.

The six modified arch22 operator files are byte-for-byte identical to
the implementation in #20456. The release branch's existing arch35
changes are preserved. A local merge-tree check confirms that
integrating this branch into release base `a26cc45a` produces exactly
the prepared release-port source tree, with no changes outside the
intended operator files and the release note.

Optimize the arch22 INT8 per-tile implementation of
`KvQuantSparseFlashAttentionVllm` on A2/A3. The existing no-RoPE path
reserves and computes an internal 576-wide attention dimension; this
port computes the actual 512 dimensions and reduces sparse KV
preparation overhead.

The kernel implementation is ported from CANN ops-transformer PR
[!14492](https://gitcode.com/cann/ops-transformer/pull/14492), with
adaptive address-cache commit
[157a925c](https://gitcode.com/mufei_L/ops-transformer/commit/157a925c6282f54bb8707cac5dd63f42a210b3c9)
and valid-prefix commit
[9668a6d7](https://gitcode.com/mufei_L/ops-transformer/commit/9668a6d7b2236bbc6928a4ff7d239c26e91b250c).

- Specialize arch22 no-RoPE matrix computation to 512 dimensions and
perform KV ND2NZ during Cube loading, retaining the existing workspace
slot stride.
- Hoist invariant gather parameters, combine eligible KV transfers, and
reuse three UB staging slots.
- Cache page-table entries and prepare sparse physical row addresses in
batches. Use bounded address storage and S2 segments when a whole query
does not fit.
- Preserve address caching for the valid prefix of sparse-index rows
ending in `-1` in the adaptive large-table/large-K path.
- Limit idle arch22 launches for short query inputs.

Scope: FP16/BF16 query, INT8 per-tile key/value
(`key_quant_mode=value_quant_mode=2`, `quant_scale_repo_mode=1`,
`tile_size=128`), with RoPE dimension 0 or 64. The public operator
schema, softmax outputs, and existing tiling-key ABI are preserved.
Arch35 files are unchanged.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes: lower operator latency within the existing supported contract.
There are no new user arguments or environment variables. A performance
release-note fragment is included in this PR.

### How was this patch tested?

The hardware results below are carried over from #20456; they are not a
new execution of this release-branch checkout. The backported arch22
operator files are identical. This backport passed `git diff --check`,
codespell, and source/merge-tree equality checks. Release-branch CI and
hardware integration remain to be completed.

Hardware and environment: Ascend A3, CANN 9.2.0 B234, vLLM 0.32.0.

The A3 validation compares PR base `cae7ff02` with head `3b76b647`.
Native operators were compiled separately from each revision, without
additional modifications to operator or framework source code. The
subsequent co-author commit-message update does not change either source
tree.

#### Operator correctness and real-input replay

- Ran the repository QSFA tests on a single A3 device: **54 passed and
24 A5-only cases skipped for each version**.
- Replayed an actual full-model tensor dump without modifying the
inputs: Query `[16384,8,512]`, BF16 Query, INT8 KV, no RoPE, and no LSE
output. Each version was checked in three rounds; all outputs matched
the full-model reference element by element.

#### Full-model performance

Model: GLM-5.3-Flash-W8A8, MRv2, INT8 KV, `max-model-len=135168`.
AISBench used fixed concurrency 200 and 400 requests per group. Each
version ran three rounds.

**Prefill-only (P)**

DP2/TP8, one output token, `max-num-batched-tokens=16384`, and
`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` enabled.

- **4K input, 0% prefix-cache hit rate:** average TTFT decreased
**5.04%**; request throughput and input-token throughput each increased
**5.27%**.
- **128K input, approximately 89.71% prefix-cache hit rate:** average
TTFT decreased **2.13%**; request throughput and input-token throughput
each increased **2.13%**.

**Decode-only (D)**

DP4/TP4, concurrency 50 per rank, 1024 output tokens,
`max-num-batched-tokens=192`, and `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` enabled.

- Actual input lengths were **4353 / 130561 tokens** for the 4K / 128K
scenarios, respectively. Local prefix-cache hit rates were **99.977% /
99.999%**.
- **Neither scenario showed a performance gain.**

Earlier A2 validation also covered boundary cases and NaN/Inf
initialization: 129 legal supplemental configurations and 387 GM-poison
variants passed. These results supplement the A3 repository tests and
actual-input replay above.

Known scope: this PR does not add test files or change the public
operator contract. Tables of width <=256 with K<=2560 retain the CANN
small-table address-preparation path, where tail `-1` may disable
address caching; no universal performance gain is claimed for every
input.

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] Boundary / edge-case coverage reviewed and validated on hardware
as detailed above.
- [ ] Regression test added (no operator contract change; focused
external hardware validation used).
- [x] Error / failure path coverage, including expected unsupported-head
rejection and empty inputs.
- [x] Meaningful & reliable tests: independent references and
complete-output comparisons.
- [x] Performance impact: matched-workload A3 full-model prefill/decode
comparisons recorded above.

added.subject: [Performance][v0.32.0rc] Avoid per-element tracking for contiguous UVA writes (#20542)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?
Reduce MRV2 UVA fallback dirty-tracking overhead:
- Track contiguous prefix writes with a single bound instead of creating
per-element indices and invoking per-element callbacks.
- Support multidimensional NumPy and Tensor prefix slices, including
`[:n, :]` and `[:n, 0]`.
- Copy any contiguous dirty range with an asynchronous pinned slice
copy, including nonzero-start ranges outside a dirty prefix.
- Preserve mixed prefix/sparse writes, uint64 bit patterns, real-UVA
behavior, and upstream buffer-pool lifetime and rotation.

The pool test retains `pool._uva_bufs[pool._curr]`: the paired vLLM
implementation advances the index before selecting and writing the slot.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
Reduces CPU request-admission overhead for long prompts without adding
configuration or changing tensor contents.

### How was this patch tested?
- 13 focused unit tests passed, including multidimensional prefix slices
and nonzero-start contiguous ranges. The latter verifies that contiguous
synchronization does not fall back to indexed copy or re-pinning.
- 14 real-NPU tests passed on Ascend 950, covering buffer-pool growth
and rotation, NumPy/Tensor/list inputs, uint64 high bits, and
multidimensional prefix/contiguous-range mixing.
- AISBench steady-state throughput improved by **15.39%** in the
deployment-level comparison.
- With this optimization and P/D static kernel disabled, GPQA Diamond
completed all 198 requests with zero request failures: **90.91% (180/198
correct)**. This is combined-stack validation, not an isolated accuracy
attribution. A separate static-enabled GPQA attempt encountered a P-side
MoE Dispatch timeout and is invalid.
- Hardware and end-to-end evidence was collected on the deployed
development stack; pristine target-branch integration remains subject to
CI.
- Ruff lint/format and `git diff --check` passed. Full `bash format.sh
ci` was attempted in isolated target-branch worktrees but could not
complete because pre-commit tool-environment installation stalled; full
hook validation remains for CI.

added.author: zzzzzz198
added.subject: [releases/v0.32.0rc][BugFix][Performance] Zero QSFA TND output tail in-kernel and drop redundant SFA masked_fill (#20578)
added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

cherry pick of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20404

**Problem**: On the GLM-5.3-Flash SFA c8 (int8 KV, NoPE, TND layout)
path, the fork QSFA kernel (`npu_kv_quant_sparse_flash_attention_vllm`)
only writes valid rows of its output buffer. The output is allocated via
`at::empty` and the `needInit`-based output initialization excluded TND
layouts (plus used a BSND size formula), so
padding rows `[actual, T)` kept stale/NaN residue when graph bucket
capacity shrank between calls. The Python side carried a per-layer
`masked_fill` workaround (arange + lt + masked_fill × 11 SFA layers per
decode step).

**Fix** (ports cann/ops-transformer#14799 to the fork kernel):
- arch32 (A2/A3, 910_93): enable `needInit` for TND and zero only
`[actual, T)` read from the device-side cumulative query lengths, with
32B-aligned per-core ranges; full batches skip entirely. The fork's
extra softmax-LSE init section is preserved (flag-guarded early skip
instead of `return`).
- arch35 (A5): add `InitOutputTail()` hooked into `CleanOutput()` when
the full needInit path does not run; no new cross-core barrier (disjoint
tail writes, local MTE3_V event guard only).
- Remove the now-redundant Python `masked_fill` in `sfa_v1.py` (NoPE c8
branch).

**Tests**:
- E2E `test_tnd_output_tail_zeroed`: capacity-shrink (128→64) must
produce finite valid rows and an exactly-zero tail (fails on the unfixed
kernel with NaN tail).
- UT: NoPE c8 path returns the operator buffer unmasked (documents the
new contract).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

NO. Numerics of valid rows are unchanged; only previously-undefined
padding rows become defined (zero).

### How was this patch tested?

A3 precision:
 GSM8K 96.89%  AIME26 90.00%

A3 performance:
| Case | BEFORE | AFTER | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2k/512，bs 32 | 257.7 tok/s | 260.2 tok/s | +1.0% |
| 128k/512，bs 8| 12.26 tok/s | 12.44 tok/s | +1.5% |

A5 precision:
GSM8K 97.42%  AIME26 90.00%

A5 performance:
| Case | BEFORE | AFTER | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| prefill 4k | 10.7074 QPS | 10.7624 QPS | +0.5% |
| prefill 128k| 1.494 QPS | 1.5085 QPS | +0.9% |
| decode 4k/2k| 87.3 ITL | 87.0 ITL | +0.3% |
| decode 128k/1k| 121.9 ITL | 113.8 ITL | +6% |

added.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Optimize QuantLightningIndexer (QLI) on `releases/v0.32.0rc`, based on
[jj_tang/ops-transformer,
experimental_split_mode](https://gitcode.com/jj_tang/ops-transformer/tree/experimental_split_mode).

- Align the token Top-K working width to 64 and size UB accumulators and
LD merge buffers accordingly, reducing sorting, merging, copying and
extraction work. Update the corresponding LD workspace indexing/strides
while keeping the candidate-block Top-K accumulator independent.
- Batch candidate-score and integer mask/pinning vector operations with
AscendC Level-0 `mask + repeatTimes`, with up to 255 full repeats, exact
masked tails and retained vector barriers. This implementation comes
from
`experimental/attention/quant_lightning_indexer_v2/op_kernel/arch22` at
source commit
[66ae55e085d109f248fccc96e2c8cb9820316d20](https://gitcode.com/jj_tang/ops-transformer/tree/66ae55e085d109f248fccc96e2c8cb9820316d20);
credit to jj_tang.
- Preserve the integrated QLI v3 candidate modes, public schema, int64
K-scale addressing and integer `Adds(+0)` merge copy.

The two kernel headers and operator tests match the reviewed main
implementation exactly after line-ending normalization. The
release-branch patch contains no unrelated main commits. Base:
`ffca1c99bb28d9c92dd5dcf327f8b242404a5055`.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Reduce QLI Top-K merge work and vector dispatch overhead for
DeepSeek-V4.1 on Ascend A3. Public APIs and configuration remain
unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

- Retain the 72 CPU-reference candidate/strided-cache cases and 30
adaptive Top-K boundary cases (102 new cases). Both new test entry
points have explicit A2/A3 guards, including mode-3 controls, so
A5/other devices skip the arch22 coverage.
- Consolidate the cases with existing coverage in
`test_quant_lightning_indexer_v2.py`.
- Static parity with the reviewed main implementation, Python syntax,
applicable Ruff/format/lint checks, direct long-function/meta checks and
`git diff --check` passed.
- Full local formatting checks remain incomplete: actionlint's Go
dependency download timed out; Windows-dependent shell/PNG and other
unavailable hooks were excluded from the applicable-check run. CI is
required.
- **Historical hardware evidence for the same optimization
implementation, not a new release-branch run:** native build/install and
102/102 reference cases passed on Ascend A3, CANN 9.2.0, torch
2.10.0+cpu and torch_npu 2.10.0.post7. Three trials per state in
A1-B1-B2-A2-A3-B3 order, 500 warmups and 100 NPU-event samples per
case/run: 12 stable consumer cases reduced latency by 21.79%–30.69%; 10
stable source cases by 8.73%–9.67%. Two short source cases remain
inconclusive due to timing variance; disabled controls were within
noise.
- The rc branch has **not** been rebuilt or rerun on NPU for this
backport. Release-branch native build, NPU correctness, ACL graph and
model-level validation remain pending. Historical operator timings do
not establish release-branch or model throughput gains.

added.subject: [Cherry-pick][releases/v0.32.0rc][Bugfix] Support GLM-5.3-Flash PCP with torch.compile (from #20281) (#20473)
added.body:
Cherry-pick of PR #20281 onto `releases/v0.32.0rc`.

Original PR: #20281
Original author: @bnbryan

---
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix GLM-5.3-Flash prefill failures when combining PCP with
`torch.compile`.

Metadata-free profiling skips KDA's PCP gather/restore branches.
Compiled execution then passes rank-local tensors to KDA while the
request metadata describes global tokens, causing prefill to fail.

Wrap the PCP KDA path in a mutable-output custom op and register it as a
piecewise split point. This keeps metadata-dependent operations active
on every invocation and writes results into a stable buffer.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. GLM-5.3-Flash can process PCP prefill requests with compilation
enabled.

For PCP>1, the KDA attention path executes eagerly inside the custom op,
including projections and gather/restore. The surrounding backbone
remains compiled. PCP=1 retains its existing compilation boundary.

### How was this patch tested?

- 50 focused unit tests passed, covering metadata-free export followed
by live prefill/decode metadata,

added.subject: [Attention][BugFix] Use layer name instead of draft model flag in ForwardContext for QSA (#20597)
added.body:
## What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix Qwen4Exp MTP draft QSA projection selection on `releases/v0.32.0rc`.
The PP/SP implementation from #20443 checks
`ForwardContext.is_draft_model`, but that field is absent. As a result
the MTP draft takes the target fused norm + MRoPE projection instead of
the graph-safe upstream path. Select the draft by its stable `mtp.`
layer name and update the regression test to use a context without the
nonexistent field.

This PR is based directly on `releases/v0.32.0rc`, where #20443 is
already merged. It changes the QSA implementation, its focused
regression test, and the required bugfix release-note fragment.

## Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

Yes. It restores the intended MTP draft projection path for Qwen3.8
Flash Next PP deployments, preventing the low speculative-token
acceptance observed with the affected W4A8 service.

## How was this patch tested?

- On this release-branch source tree, `python -m py_compile` for the two
changed Python files and `git diff --check` passed.
- On the deployed eight-card overlay with the same QSA fix, `python3 -m
pytest -q tests/ut/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_upstream_abi.py` passed (3
tests). PP2TP2DP1 P + DP2TP2 D, GSM8K 16K/1K at concurrency 8:
21,920/32,655 draft tokens accepted (67.1%, cache off) and 21,377/34,266
(62.4%, cache on), 32/32 requests successful in each run.
- The hardware comparison also involved service restarts and cache
resets, so it is not an isolated single-variable A/B. The exact
release-branch unit test was not run on the remote host because its Git
proxy refused the fetch; CI validation is pending.

Related: #20443, #20311, #20558.

old_only.subject: [v0.31.0rc][Test][BugFix] Stabilize DeepSeek V4.1 MRV2 PCP nightly startup (#19522)
old_only.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Release counterpart of #19477, targeting `releases/v0.31.0rc`. The main
PR is still open; both branches need this configuration fix.

After the PCP-local profile token-budget optimization was reverted, the
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash MRV2+PCP nightly can retain only about 5.07 GiB per
Prefill rank for KV cache, below the approximately 5.56 GiB required for
its 1M context.

Keep `max_model_len=1048576` and adjust only the Prefill configuration:

- `max_num_batched_tokens`: 16384 to 8192, reducing profiling and
activation memory demand.
- `gpu_memory_utilization`: 0.9 to 0.92, increasing available KV-cache
headroom.

The Decode configuration remains unchanged. Lowering the Prefill
batch-token cap can reduce maximum Prefill batching capacity, so the
existing nightly performance cases need to be checked before merge.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This changes only an internal nightly test configuration.

### How was this patch tested?

- Parsed the release YAML with PyYAML and verified effective values:
Prefill `1048576 / 8192 / 0.92`; Decode `1048576 / 400 / 0.95` for
context length, batch-token cap, and memory utilization respectively.
- Compared the complete parsed YAML against the release baseline: only
the two intended Prefill values change. The changed lines match #19477
exactly.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- `bash format.sh ci` cannot start locally because `pre-commit` is
unavailable. Full hooks and two-node A3 release nightly validation of
startup, accuracy, and performance remain for CI/review before merge.

### Checklist

- [x] Focused port of #19477 with only two Prefill parameter changes.
- [x] YAML validation confirms the 1M context and unchanged Decode
configuration.

old_only.subject: [v0.31.0rc][Attention][BugFix] Preserve GLM-Next shared-pool KV budget (#19521)
old_only.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Release counterpart of #19457, targeting `releases/v0.31.0rc`. The main
PR is still open; both branches need this fix.

GLM-5.3-Flash MRV1 applies an unnecessary per-layer KV budget discount
after KPool attention is classified as SFA. The GLM-Next planner already
accounts for physical sharing, so the discount can leave insufficient
capacity for the configured 1M context.

Add `glm5_next` to the existing DeepSeek V4/V4.1 physical shared-pool
exemption. Preserve the release branch's V2 full/sliding-attention
sharing logic and all pre-existing tests. No deployment configuration is
changed.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. GLM-Next retains its complete physical shared-pool KV budget,
addressing the MRV1 startup capacity failure without reducing the
configured context length.

### How was this patch tested?

- Release base: `2bd3b7fcd044c51b78e5943ac64dd8208e56b543`.
- Ran the release worker and test sources in the reproduced nightly
image, using CPU-only containers without NPU devices. The unmodified
release worker reproduces **2 failed, 2 passed** across BF16/C8 and
sparse-on/off regression cases; the fixed worker passes **13 related
tests**.
- Regression checks cover the exact physical KV budget for a
1,048,576-token context, planner capacity, and physical allocation
sizes. Existing generic and DeepSeek budget tests also pass.
- Ruff check/format check, source compilation, and `git diff --check`
pass. The changed lines match #19457 exactly.
- `bash format.sh ci` cannot start locally because `pre-commit` is
unavailable. Full hooks and release NPU/nightly startup, PD requests,
accuracy, and performance validation remain for CI/review before merge.

### Checklist

- [x] Focused port of #19457; existing release logic and tests
preserved.
- [x] Release baseline reproduces the regression; 13 related tests pass
with the fix.

performance.title: 消除 compiled embedding 的整容量缓冲拷贝
performance.mechanism: 以 invocation-local padding/masking 和现有 collective API 替代 persistent buffer 切片写入，避免 AOT 重建整个 backing buffer。
performance.applicable: compiled embedding exchange；作者 DSV4 Flash W4A8、A3 8卡、PCP8/EP8、C8、32输入/1024输出。
performance.result: 作者三轮：输出吞吐197.40→212.01 tok/s（+7.40%），TTFT −6.18%；profile 每rank每步移除1.625 GiB逻辑拷贝。
performance.caveat: 收益来自本地副本消除，collective payload 不变；kernel 时间和逻辑字节数不能直接折算端到端提升。
performance.subject: [Performance] Avoid full-buffer copies in compiled embedding token exchange (#19409)
performance.kind_label: 直接优化 / 性能恢复
performance.evidence_label: 作者报告：模型 / 服务实测

performance.title: V up projection 直接使用内部转置 batch matmul
performance.mechanism: 删去 N×L≥65536 时显式 transpose+contiguous 分支，支持的 CANN 算子直接接收 perm_x1。
performance.applicable: SFA，存在 npu_transpose_batchmatmul；依赖支持大 shape 的 CANN，缺算子仍有 bmm fallback。
performance.caveat: 是完整 _v_up_proj 局部延迟；小shape133.5→133.0 μs基本持平，无整模型测量。

performance.title: Engram lookup 输出从 zeros 改为 empty
performance.mechanism: lookup 覆盖所有本地输出 head 后无需再预先全量清零，保留无效ID写零契约。
performance.applicable: Engram preparation；作者单NPU、HBM或local-host VMM backing、TP=DP=1。
performance.result: 局部准备耗时下降2.68%～23.88%的列出样本；覆盖dirty buffer与图replay。
performance.caveat: 不包含实际多rank通信、远程HCCS读取和服务吞吐；不是新引入Engram/VMM能力。

performance.applicable: GLM-5.3-Flash recurrent KDA；普通decode与spec输出各有有效行/清零约束。
performance.result: 作者报告一次forward约1.08 ms中节省10.6 μs。
performance.caveat: 该数字是局部测量且上下文披露有限，不能推出每请求或整个版本同幅提升。
